reviews.summary:
H002 whole-contract review: `nerva chat -z` preserves final-answer-only stdout, bounded piped/file/argument input, nonzero refusal/failure/usage/auth/unreachable/interrupt exits, confirmed versus requested session attribution, and an atomic nerva.chat.usage.v1 receipt on ordinary success and failure paths. It never approves a queued action; pending IDs remain queued and force an incomplete result. Interactive output/exit compatibility remains while its optional receipt can report incomplete.

The hub supplies request-owned bounded generation usage on JSON chat replies and SSE end events. Accepted owned generation dispatch attempts are observed after quota, physical data-handling and host/protocol checks. Retries, specialists, synchronous response-driving auxiliary generation, streaming and synthesis are included; control probes, embeddings/audio and explicitly detached title/review/cache jobs are excluded. Task-owned pending attempts prevent cross-task usage attribution; nested scopes preserve provenance, inactive inherited scopes cannot authenticate a model, unknown POSTs during generation make totals unknown, and closed/bounded collectors reject late or overflowing observations. Tokens require complete valid provider counters for every attempt; failed/partial retries cannot hide behind later success. Local zero needs positive provider/route/host proof and complete counters. Exact requested models confirmed against the wire can use dated repository estimates; unsupported cache-write premiums, Gemini Pro long-context tiers, unknown models and uncertain provenance stay unpriced. Mixed identities receive a bounded breakdown. The provider field denotes the backend adapter, not an attestation of remote weights or an invoice.

Source-assigned runtime stops survive synthesis independently of prose: settled tool-loop exits, exact thinking exhaustion, terminal agent failures/timeouts, policy/continuation refusal and terminal synthesis errors make one-shot execution incomplete. Stop metadata is finite and bounded; malformed present metadata fails closed. Legacy hubs retain text-fallback limits. Successful deterministic synthesis fallback may still return complete specialist answers; a failed observed attempt keeps its usage unknown. Authorization and early owner/session preflight errors retain their HTTP failure codes and can yield unavailable telemetry while still producing a failure receipt. CLI validators reject malformed, missing, negative, boolean, nonfinite, oversized or inconsistent telemetry without crashing or changing the answer verdict; error objects carry only bounded projected telemetry.

Verification includes real owned HTTP MockTransport calls through actual backend adapters, actual ASGI JSON/SSE, concurrent/nested/late task behavior, runtime-stop to synthesis to HTTP to CLI, malformed receipts, pending approvals, transport failures, real isolated FastAPI lifespan/CLI smoke and the frozen backend milestone with its explicitly recorded outcome. No live-provider, native Windows/device or invoice claim is made. Unrelated Hermes flags, invocation IDs and writing through a symlink are outside the frozen acceptance; the atomic replace behavior is retained. Interrupt review and regressions verify exit 130 before POST and after decoded response/output, preserving observed session, usage, stops and pending IDs; already emitted terminal text cannot be retracted. The full frozen run was not green (32 failed cases); all 32 original nodes pass after fixture/status repairs, and the isolated interrupt fix passes integrated CLI coverage.

reviews.summary: `nerva doctor` rulează `scripts/doctor.py` fără să schimbe nimic, cu un motiv numit pentru fiecare verificare, `--json` și `--smoke`. Are cinci verificări obligatorii (python, venv, locks_in_sync, bind_is_loopback, data_root_writable) și zece consultative (runtimes, readyz, runtime_resolves, voice din H613, config_sources, model_roles din H277, smoke și, din H501, host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords, container_storage; scripts/doctor.py:118-120). Iese cu 1 doar când pică una obligatorie; o consultativă care pică e `warn`. Din HEQ lot 1 (H242), `runtime_resolves` verifică dacă ruta pe care o ia un turn Jarvis chiar se rezolvă la un model utilizabil, nu doar dacă răspunde un runtime. Citește verdictul strict al hub-ului, blocul `model` din `GET /api/onboarding/command-center` (același select_backend, fără generare), cu un singur credențial local: `JARVIS_USER_TOKEN`, altfel `JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN`, pe care îl trimite doar unui hub de pe această mașină, decis după adresă, nu după ortografie (scripts/doctor.py:353, scripts/doctor.py:400-407). E `ok` doar pe `ready: true` care numește ruta, providerul și modelul. Altfel dă motivul numit (`configured_not_resident`, `route_unselected`, `needs_token`, `malformed_reply` …), iar fără un hub gata e `skip`. `readyz` și această citire folosesc aceeași adresă de hub ca `nerva status` (`NERVA_HUB_URL`, altfel `JARVIS_HOST`/`JARVIS_PORT`; o adresă wildcard e apelată prin loopback). Din H273, `config_sources` arată, informativ, din ce strat vine fiecare cheie de configurare (mediul procesului > `.env`-ul repo-ului > `.env`-ul din data home) și ce valori din `.env` sunt acoperite de un strat de mai sus — doar nume, niciodată o valoare. `nerva status` arată același verdict pe o linie `runnable:`, separat de vechiul `model_state`, afișat acum „resident”. Alte diagnostice sunt verbe separate: `nerva desktop status` (ce îi lipsește host-ului pentru operatorul desktop), `nerva security audit` (vulnerabilități cunoscute, prin OSV) și `nerva extensions doctor`. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): diff-ul scripts/doctor.py de la pin (7b2d7873) adaugă verificarea consultativă `model_roles` (H277: rolurile de model citite offline din mediu, `warn` pe un provider nefolosibil sau pe o variabilă ignorată, niciodată `fail`), deci numărul și lista consultativelor au fost corectate, iar citările mutate au fost re-ancorate după conținut; nici doctor.py, nici agents/cli/nerva.py nu au primit `--fix`, `--live` sau `--ack`, iar tests/test_nerva_cli.py și tests/test_doctor.py trec (164 teste).
reviews.remaining: Lipsesc jumătățile de reparare și de operare ale rândului: nu există `--fix` (reparări numite, în tier reversibil, cu tot ce atinge credențiale sau postura pus în coada de aprobare), `--live` (rulare continuă) sau `--ack ADVISORY_ID`. Lipsesc și verificările cerute pentru o instalare deja configurată: accesibilitatea serverelor MCP, token-urile canalelor, postura kernel/flag-uri, integritatea lanțului de audit și credențialele/conectivitatea fiecărui provider configurat. `runtime_resolves` judecă doar ruta pe care o ia acum un turn Jarvis, iar o rută cloud trece pe decizia de disponibilitate a routerului, fără un apel care să verifice credențialul la provider.

reviews.summary:
Whole frozen H015 contract reviewed, batch 06 (2026-10-10). CLI/API support list/create/edit/pause/resume/run/remove/status/tick, durable runs, incidents, independent KV notes and read-only doctor. List provides global scheduler status; status provides job/request outcomes. A completed one-shot rearms through edit to a distinct future time and may then run immediately under the same gate/reservation. Direct actions reserve one pending run before execution and finish that row atomically with counters/output and any failure incident. Cancellation/orphan recovery yields unknown without replay, only while the execution gate proves no cooperating executor is live. Scripts reserve one one-shot/repeat slot in their own CAS transaction, freeze input notes and reconcile once. Deleted configuration cannot deliver a later model result; history and acknowledged incidents survive reopening. Terminal history is bounded at 200 rows/job and 10,000 globally with active references protected.
Incidents group normalized redacted failures by job/signature, expose numeric IDs and detected/closed state, acknowledge idempotently, preserve the three-failure pause and never invent an alerted transition. Closed matching signatures remain closed. Diagnostic redaction covers known environment/settings/catalogue secrets before cuts and fails closed. Notes are separate from previous model output: 128 printable characters/key, 16 KiB/value, 64 KiB/job and 256 keys, enforced transactionally. Continuity defaults on; disabling omits previous output but keeps KV and saves the latest bounded output. Both enter shared direct/script asks as JSON-escaped fenced untrusted data. Additive continuity edits merge atomically without replacing other options. Detailed model failures become failed attempts before delivery; legitimate queued-approval answers and silent suppression retain their meanings.
Existing script/URL monitors skip the model when unchanged. Native no_agent executes a bounded approved Python command rather than introducing a shell. Scripts need fresh risk-3 ASK per attempt; URL hops remain plugin.egress. Task jobs preserve kind, payload, risk floor and host-bound inbound:job identity through the live governed worker as ASK, with no raw-queue fallback or standing grant. Existing action gates remain on direct ask/delivery paths. All five new routes are admin guarded. Core 476/476, surface 137 passed/3 unavailable-Fish skips, 43 route/doctor guards and actual disposable lifespan CLI smoke passed. Full backend milestone is separately required before assessment update. H451 watchdog/recovery, H452 classifier/alerting/preflight, H454 cross-job context and new dedicated HUD/mobile controls remain separate. No live-provider/native-host claim.

reviews.summary: `nerva send --channel <id> <mesaj>` livreaza fara thread primit anterior, iar `nerva send --list` enumera destinatiile configurate cu motivul cand una nu e gata. Trece prin POST /api/channels/send (admin), respecta rate-limit-ul de trimitere si se inregistreaza in IntentLog ca `channel.send`. Din 2026-09-16 (H480) corpul poate veni din fișier sau stdin, cu un subiect `-s` purtat ca titlu ntfy sau ca prima linie a mesajului; scara de ieșire 0/1/2/3/4 e declarată în `--help`. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): diff-ul agents/core/channels/outbound.py de la pin (92c3eeb3) doar permite pasarea chat-ului owner deja citit în _owner_chat_id (citarea web-nepregatit mutată la outbound.py:91, același test pe clients); DIRECT_SEND_CHANNELS rămâne telegram/web/voice/ntfy, diff-ul agents/cli/nerva.py păstrează `send --list/--channel/-s`, iar tests/test_channel_outbound.py, tests/test_nerva_cli.py și tests/test_nerva_send.py trec (169 teste).
reviews.remaining: Randul cere orice platforma configurata. Nerva expune doar canalele direct-send (telegram, web, voice, ntfy), iar web nu e gata cat timp niciun client nu e conectat la el: HUD-ul nu conecteaza unul, asa ca `nerva send --list` si /api/channels/targets il arata ca nepregatit, cu motivul (agents/core/channels/outbound.py:91). Slack si Discord sunt reply-only prin brokerul channel.reply si nu pot fi adresate de `send`; email-ul e exclus deliberat, ca mailul inbound neincrezut sa nu capete efect SMTP.

reviews.summary: The port-conflict diagnostic, plus one stale line of evidence corrected. `serve.py` gains `probe_bind(host, port)`, called from `main()` after the posture guards and before uvicorn binds: a taken port prints the exact address, the command that identifies the holder (`nerva status`) and the way out (`JARVIS_PORT`), then exits **12**; `EACCES` exits **13**, and since #1177 that arm branches on the port number instead of asserting a cause it cannot know — below 1024 it names the privileged-port rule (root or `CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE`; move `JARVIS_PORT` above 1024), at or above 1024 it says outright that this is *not* the privileged-port rule and root/Administrator will not help, then points at the reservations that actually produce it (Windows `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange tcp`, whose Hyper-V/WSL blocks routinely cover the shipped default 8080; an SELinux `name_bind` denial on Linux) plus `JARVIS_PORT`. Both codes are deliberately distinct from uvicorn's `STARTUP_FAILURE` (3), which it uses for *every* startup failure — that collision was the actual defect, because a supervisor could not tell "the port is taken" from "the lifespan crashed". The probe is a **diagnostic, not a lock**: it binds and closes, reserves nothing, and any `OSError` outside the two named arms is swallowed, so an unexpected probe failure can never turn a boot that would have worked into a refusal. The socket **constructor sits inside the guarded region** too — a first cut that built it above the `try` turned `JARVIS_HOST=::1` on a box with no IPv6 stack into an 8-frame traceback + exit 1 in place of uvicorn's one-line error + exit 3, the diagnostic making the boot worse than no diagnostic. It also mirrors asyncio's own flags rather than stricter ones: `SO_REUSEADDR` on POSIX, because `uvicorn.Server.startup` binds through `loop.create_server` where asyncio sets it, so a probe without it would refuse a port merely holding a TIME_WAIT connection from the instance the owner just stopped — a boot uvicorn would have completed; and `IPV6_V6ONLY` on an AF_INET6 probe, so an IPv4 listener on the same port cannot turn a working v6 boot into exit 12. **The frozen 2026-09-07 evidence was stale on one point**: it recorded "no --status", but `nerva status` has existed since the unified CLI (the `status` verb in `agents/cli/nerva.py`). 13 `test_probe_bind_*` functions, 16 collected cases (the IPv6-conflict case skips on a box with no IPv6 stack). Both exit codes are asserted **by execution** rather than by reading the branch — the sub-1024 `EACCES` arm runs in a child dropped to an unprivileged uid with `setpriv`, because pytest runs as root here and a sub-1024 bind simply succeeds; the high-port `EACCES` arm is driven through a stubbed `bind()` that answers `EACCES`, parametrised over 1024/8080/49152/65535, because its real reproduction is a Windows excluded port range that cannot be staged on Linux, and a sibling test pins that port 80 still gets the privileged-port sentence. ENV-122 in `docs/test-manual/01-environment-and-boot.md` moves from a message-quality finding to an asserted string plus exit code. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): de la pin (92c3eeb3) `serve.py` schimbă doar citirea `JARVIS_HOST`/`JARVIS_LOG_LEVEL` prin `env_str`, iar `probe_bind` și codurile 12/13 sunt neatinse (serve.py:118, serve.py:122, apelul la serve.py:251); manualul schimbă doar rândul ENV-176 (H689), ENV-122 rămâne asertat (docs/test-manual/01-environment-and-boot.md:450); tests/test_h2311_operability.py (neschimbat) dă 37 trecute + 2 sărite în această sesiune — sărite sunt cazul IPv6 (nicio stivă IPv6) și cazul sub-1024 rulat sub uid neprivilegiat, al cărui copil nu a putut importa `serve` din acest worktree, deci acel braț nu a fost re-executat aici.
reviews.remaining: Hermes's row is start, check **and stop**, and the stop half is entirely absent: no `stop` verb, no pidfile, no ready file. The row cites `hermes dashboard --status/--stop` plus backend ready sentinels and a ready file (06-cli-f.md, 16 entries); Nerva has `nerva status`, which reads the HTTP surface and so cannot report a hub that is starting or wedged before the port opens, and Ctrl-C. Hermes also signals the conflict as a machine-readable `BACKEND_PORT_IN_USE`, where this slice signals it as an exit code and an English sentence — enough for a supervisor, not enough for a caller parsing a status stream. Not delivered either: `--isolated`, `--skip-build`, `--no-open`, the SSH session-token file and owner-nonce, or the interactive auth-setup prompt. **One known limit, in the safe direction:** the probe picks a single address family from the host string while uvicorn binds every address `getaddrinfo` returns, so a dual-stack name like `localhost` is probed on v4 only and can miss a conflict held on the v6 address — it misses silently, and uvicorn then reports it exactly as it does today. The Windows half of the `SO_REUSEADDR` choice is read off asyncio's `reuse_address = os.name == "posix"` line and has never been executed here; that test skips off POSIX and the docstring says so.

reviews.summary: `nerva prompt-size` există și raportează costul fix per apel, pe componente, cel mai mare primul — offline, fără hub, fără backend, fără nicio cerere: citește personele de pe disc și cere registrului specurile pe care oricum le declară. Exact asta îl face utilizabil pentru întrebarea la care răspunde („cât plătesc înainte să înceapă conversația") pe o cutie unde hub-ul nici măcar nu rulează. `agents/core/prompt_size.py` sparge costul în: câte o linie per persoană de agent găsită pe disc, câte una per unealtă — costată ca **JSON-ul care chiar traversează sârma**, nu ca numele ei, fiindcă un `input_schema` stufos poate cântări cât o persoană întreagă — indexul de skill-uri randat exact cum îl randează `build_prompt`, și schela de tură pe care fiecare cerere o plătește. Numărul pe care raportul îl scoate în față e **podeaua per apel**, nu suma: cele 18 persoane sunt listate separat fiindcă o cerere reală trimite una singură, a agentului rutat. Prima versiune a raportului aduna toate cele 18 și anunța 71,8 % dintr-o fereastră de 32k, când o cerere reală plătește ~6,5 % — un număr greșit e mai rău decât niciun număr, așa că podeaua per apel e ce se citește primul și un test o fixează. Fără agent numit se folosește persoana cea mai grea, deci cifra e cazul realist cel mai prost, nu unul măgulitor; un agent inexistent nu e taxat tăcut pe seama altcuiva. Raportul spune despre el însuși că cifrele sunt estimări din aceeași funcție pe care o folosește bugetul la runtime, și trimite la H673 pentru singura măsurătoare exactă — cea raportată de provider. Ieșire text tabelară sau `--json`. reviews.remaining: No busy-input semantics for the turn itself. A mid-turn message cannot redirect or interrupt the running model turn: it only cancels a running execute_code child in that conversation, and the message then waits behind the lease. There is no explicit FIFO `/queue`, no `/steer` into the running turn and no configurable mode between these with downgrades. `/stop` is not a hard kill: it engages the e-stop but does not cancel the running turn or unlock the session. It is also dispatched inside `_handle_input` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2472), so it waits behind the same lease. While a turn holds the lease past the wait bound, `/stop` itself is answered with `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` (named at agents/core/orchestrator.py:4292). There is one busy string, not a set of acks saying whether a message was queued, steered or interrupted. None of the protective demotions exist (running subagent, in-flight compression, photo burst, very fast follow-up merged as the same intent). The lease is the only slot reservation; there is no pending-agent sentinel. `SlashCommand` (agents/core/commands.py:71) carries no `busy_policy`.

reviews.summary: Turns are serialized per resolved session. `Orchestrator.turn_lease` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2101) holds one asyncio.Lock per key, and `_lease_key` (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2091) follows `_resolve_session`'s order, so the lease names the session the turn will actually use rather than the routing key. It is taken by channel turns (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1981) and the web /chat path (agents/web.py:1332), and it is re-entrant within one turn. After 180 s a waiting message is answered `TURN_BUSY_REPLY` instead of starting (tests/test_turn_lease.py:72, tests/test_turn_lease.py:118, tests/test_turn_lease.py:104). The lease table is capped at 1024 entries and prunes unlocked locks when full (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2120, tests/test_turn_lease.py:163). The `_active_session` ContextVar (agents/core/orchestrator.py:307) keeps concurrent turns from reading or writing each other's session (tests/test_concurrent_session_isolation.py:96). reviews.remaining: No run generation lets a late callback from an abandoned turn detect that it no longer owns the session. The only compare-and-set is the checkpoint-clock commit of a compaction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4612), and it guards a summary, not turn ownership; the H063 route generations in channels/session_lifecycle.py fence which session a channel route resolves to after a reset, not whether a running turn still owns its session. There is no active-session slot claimed before the first await and no `max_concurrent_sessions` cap: turns on different sessions run concurrently without bound (tests/test_turn_lease.py:88). No watchdog evicts a session whose turn is wedged: its lease stays held until the turn ends, and later messages only get the busy reply. There is no eviction of an in-memory slot whose durable routing row ended, and no single per-session `SessionState` object with explicit lifetimes. There is no per-session warm agent cache and no memory-pressure eviction. Agents are process-wide: every session shares `orchestrator.agents`, which the compaction-boundary persona refresh walks as a whole (agents/core/orchestrator.py:473).

reviews.summary: Un mesaj vocal pe Telegram e transcris înainte să-l vadă agentul — echivalentul lui `stt_enabled` din Hermes. `InboundVoiceReader` întreabă poarta înainte de descărcare, mărginește octeții, îi trimite prin `BytesIO` direct la decodor (vorbirea nu atinge discul) și transformă fiecare eșec într-un motiv numit; santinelele motorului nu ajung niciodată la model ca vorbire. Transcriptul circulă ca o tură obișnuită, nu în gard: sunt chiar cuvintele expeditorului, iar protecția reală e filtrul de halucinații (H530). Jumătatea rostită: `/voice off|voice|always` e mod per conversație (`voice_mode.py`, magazie JSON `canal:chat`, implicit off, setat de chat pentru chat), `stt_echo_transcripts` e setarea `voice.stt_echo_transcripts` (o linie de serviciu „am auzit: …” înaintea răspunsului, niciodată rostită), iar `spoken_reply.py` transformă textul livrat într-o notă vocală peste motorul TTS al gazdei — doar proza (fără cod, linkuri, marcaje), tăiată la o limită de propoziție, fișierul șters după citire, nimic din text în log. Cârligul stă unde textul chiar ajunge (`send()` și `finish()` al draftului în flux), deci modul nu poate livra ca audio ce ruterul n-ar fi livrat ca text; orice eșec costă nota vocală, niciodată textul; un 400 pe `sendVoice` reîncearcă o dată ca `sendAudio`. `/voice` numește motorul care ar vorbi și spune „cloud” când e edge-tts. Reevaluarea inițială a raportat 15/15 mutanți uciși; numărul nu a fost reprodus la recitirea din 2026-09-22. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): diff-ul agents/core/channels/telegram.py de la pin (4b7714f9) leagă marca de voce de tura care rulează în chat (_after_reply; liniile de serviciu — ecoul transcriptului, notițele de atașament, împerecherea — trimise cu voice=False nu sunt rostite și nu consumă marca), iar diff-ul agents/core/commands.py nu atinge `/voice`; cârligul din send()/finish(), sendVoice cu căderea pe sendAudio și InboundVoiceReader rămân, consumatorul TTS în flux încă lipsește, iar cele patru fișiere de test fixate trec (112 teste).
reviews.remaining: Consumatorul TTS în flux care începe să rostească propozițiile terminate cât timp modelul încă generează (nota vocală se sintetizează după răspunsul complet). Intrarea/ieșirea dintr-un canal de voce pe Discord e sărită deliberat de rândul original (funcție de comunitate, nu de asistent). Doar Telegram: pe Slack/Discord replica trece prin brokerul `channel.reply`, fără audio. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun mesaj vocal Telegram adevărat, niciun model Whisper încărcat, niciun `sendVoice` real — Telegram acceptă `.mp3` ca mesaj vocal după documentație, iar căderea pe `sendAudio` e plasa pentru cazul în care nu.

Edit-based streaming replies exist on Telegram. `TelegramDraft` in agents/core/channels/telegram.py sends the first token as a message and edits it in place at most once per `STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL` (1.2 s), skipping frames whose visible text did not change; the preview is capped below the message limit, and `finish()` writes the first chunk of the final text into the edited message and sends the overflow as continuation messages, retrying rejected markup as plain text and falling back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. `TelegramChannel.begin_stream` returns a draft only for a chat id; `Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft` opens it only when the adapter's descriptor declares `supports_edit`, the Settings DB toggle `channels.streaming_replies` is on and the delivery router would send to that source; observed group messages never open one and a draft that never started falls back to the normal send (tests/test_telegram_streaming.py). Slack and Discord are refused a draft on purpose: their workspace replies are governed `channel.reply` approvals delivered whole after approval, and edit support alone cannot publish unapproved tokens (tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py `test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens`). reviews.summary: Telegram photos are read, not only recognised. `classify` (agents/core/channels/inbound_media.py) recognises the ten attachment kinds in `RECOGNISED_KINDS` and turns a missing file handle, a declared size above the 20 MB bot ceiling or an unreadable kind into a named reason, so the sender gets one plain line from `describe` instead of silence. `InboundImageReader` (agents/core/channels/media_reader.py) describes a photo through a proven-local VLM and hands the description to the turn as data, never as instructions. Locality follows the `screen_locator` rule: `is_local` derives only from `resolve_vlm_config().is_local`, `TelegramChannel._read_image` asks `refusal()` before any download, and `_backend_call` checks again before it posts: `interactive_local_identity` re-reads the live config and refuses a non-loopback base URL, the role consent and model-selection guards run, and the call goes through `unattended_media_request_scope` with `generate_vision_checked`, so a non-loopback VLM receives no bytes (the sender is told the owner must configure or acknowledge the local vision model, `REASON_POLICY`). `_download_file` bounds the transfer by the bytes that actually arrive, not by the sender-chosen `file_size`, and `_safe_file_path` rejects any `getFile` path that is not Telegram-shaped before it enters the bot-token URL. The description is folded to one line, capped and wrapped in the Wave 5a `fence_tool_result` fence, deliberately without the `spotlight` datamark, which would replace spaces with '▁' and blind the gateway's `detect_injection`; a photo with '<<END UNTRUSTED>>' written on it cannot close its own fence. The caption never reaches the describer: it travels separately as the sender's question. The turn goes through the normal door, so `Gateway._inbound_meta` marks it `inbound:telegram` and runs the detector over exactly what the model reads. Voice notes are read on the other path: a transcript is the sender's own words and travels unfenced as an ordinary turn (`inbound_voice`, row H071). `ChannelDescriptor` separates `recognises_media` from `reads_media` with the subset invariant checked at construction, and `READABLE_KINDS` is exactly {photo, voice}. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): media_reader.py now re-resolves the VLM config per call and adds an owner policy/consent gate (REASON_POLICY) plus a loopback identity check and native wire scope before posting, telegram.py gained ephemeral replies, owner-once/consent hooks and topic replies without touching the photo download path, and the media test now expects REASON_POLICY for a remote URL; photo/voice reading, the size bound, the path screen and the fence still hold and 132 pinned tests pass.
reviews.remaining: Only photos and voice notes, only on Telegram. Not delivered: reading audio files, video, video notes, animations, documents and stickers (recognised, answered with 'reading … is not wired up yet'); a disk cache under a media directory so vision tools can open a local path (bytes stay in memory for one call); location and venue pins (recognised as `location`, deliberately not echoed, not read); caching of media from observed group messages and from replied-to messages; media ingestion on WhatsApp, Discord, Teams, Google Chat and email (those adapters pass text only). Documented limitation, not solved: taint cannot be tracked through the model; what travels is the coarse fact that the turn read untrusted material, and the channel's `inbound` origin is what keeps an action derived from a photo in approval. `mark_turn_recall_tainted()` is not called here because it would be a no-op (escalate-only over an already untrusted origin). UNVERIFIED on real services: the suite is hermetic; no real Telegram message received, no local VLM actually called, `getFile` and the download exercised only against a fake client.

reviews.summary:
Message batching remains per (chat, sender), in arrival order, with the existing 0.35-second rolling window, 1-second cap and 32-part bound (agents/core/channels/batching.py:45-47). Telegram keys the batch by (chat, sender) and, inside a forum topic, also by the topic id (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1306-1308); Discord keys by (channel, author) (agents/core/channels/discord.py:156) and Slack by (channel, member, thread) (agents/core/channels/slack.py:649-650). Ordinary Telegram callbacks flush held batches and enter the chat lane; ordinary messages, attachment descriptions, command and reason ordering and merged-text injection scanning retain their existing paths: a command flushes what was held and is delivered alone (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1309-1314), and the Gateway scans the merged turn normalised (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:275-278). Reserved autc reusable-consent callbacks are an explicit exception: they intercept before the normal batch flush. A registered current callback uses a separate bounded 32-task lane to release its waiting owner/model turn; stale, malformed, replayed, unregistered or overflowing reserved callbacks refuse promptly without entering the occupied ordinary lane. The existing live aut1 owner-once callback retains its separate post-flush lane. This is deliberate collateral behavior review with existing batching/reason/owner-once regressions, not a new batching feature or renewed mutation receipt. Batch collateral review (2026-10-04, base 9bfa085c): Native reusable-consent `/deny` is now a reserved direct reply to the delivered card. It dispatches outside the occupied chat lane and consumes stale or malformed `/deny` without forwarding it as a model turn. Ordinary batching, callback, command and reason paths retain their existing ordering. This is a scoped lane exception, not new batching equivalence or live Telegram proof.

Owner-once denial collateral review (2026-10-04, base 22005244): an original current `/deny [reason]` reply to the delivered owner-once card is now another reserved pre-flush exception. Telegram selects exactly one current owner-once or reusable-consent registry, dispatches the selected reply outside the occupied ordinary chat lane, and consumes stale, ambiguous and malformed `/deny` without forwarding text to the model. The (chat, sender) batching window, cap, part bound and ordinary callback/command/reason paths are unchanged. The new native owner-once test exercises the occupied-lane reply and refusal paths; this preserves the prior batching verdict without a live Bot API or new mutation claim.

Pending-input drift re-read (2026-10-11, PR #1249 head): the h067 pending-input work added two more reserved pre-batch exceptions and does not change the batching contract. (1) A `h067:` callback is dispatched on its own bounded 32-task lane before the consent/owner-once callback handling and before any batch flush (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:882-889); with no hook, a bad id or a full lane it is answered "Not applied." without entering the ordinary lane. (2) A fresh, directly authored, group-admitted text with no attachment that is not a claimed decision reason is first offered to the Gateway's pending handler (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1045-1047; agents/core/channels/gateway.py:77-78 runs it ahead of the rate limit, pairing and the merged-text scan), and only a consumed clarification answer skips batching; anything not consumed continues down the unchanged reason/batch path. Discord offers original human messages the same way before the batch submit (agents/core/channels/discord.py:156). The held Telegram batch now carries session metadata, and coalescing keeps a pending_input_eligible=False mark sticky across the merged pieces (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1315-1318). The topic-scoped key and the sticky mark are not exercised by the pinned regressions; the 0.35 s / 1.0 s / 32-part contract, the command and reason ordering, the Discord and Slack bursts and the shutdown discard are, and all 301 pinned tests pass at this head. reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (9f92d937): Matrix support is an unencrypted client-server shim: MatrixChannel posts m.room.message plaintext to /_matrix/client/v3/rooms/{room}/send with a bearer token (agents/core/channels/webhook_channels.py:183-198) and parses plaintext inbound events (agents/core/channels/webhook_channels.py:201-210). - cross-signing verification via a recovery key
- proxy mode for platforms where native E2EE fails
- tests for encrypted round-trip and verification

Cancellation and late-response suppression preserve one active turn; ordinary text payloads remain unchanged. The chosen provider/model/destination and source are visible before consent; the binding changes on provider/key/policy drift, and POST performs no discovery. Real mocked-transport GET-to-POST regressions and the complete 1861-case frontend suite pass. This does not add images to the ordinary agent context or native mobile composer. Existing image intake and separate VLM-turn behavior are unchanged; ordinary agent multimodal context remains open. Desktop/mobile browser and mocked HTTP tests passed. The answer remains a separate, client-only vision bubble. Mocked HTTP tests cover the native body, response, destination drift and remote acknowledgement; no live Ollama call or persisted chat image is claimed. reviews.summary:
Whole frozen H145 contract re-reviewed, batch 06 (2026-10-10), replacing stale broad historical pins with the complete current log feature review. The registered Logs panel has File/minimum-Level/Component/Lines controls, text-only colored records and five-second visible/enabled polling without overlapping reads. LIVE requires enabled logging and accepted admin access; rejected credentials stop polling, rejected filters clear stale records and removed rotations reset selection. The admin-only no-store endpoint reads off the event loop. Allowlisted regular primary/numbered files, no-follow/nonblocking open and descriptor checks reject arbitrary files or swapped links. Reverse reading is bounded to 4 MiB, 500 records and 8,000 characters/record while preserving traceback/error headers. Scanner/catalogue, credential-assignment and known environment/settings value redaction precedes cuts; unavailable redaction returns no entries. Controls/bidi are removed; disabled/error/missing/partial states remain explicit.
Accepted native adaptation remains one actual rotating hub log rather than six nonexistent service logs, and a severity floor rather than exact-level matching. DEBUG under ALL and CRITICAL under ERROR remain colored; the component menu reflects the bounded scan. Backend log regressions passed in the focused H049 selection; all 14 existing Logs panel tests and frontend TypeScript passed in this batch. No browser/native-host/deployment claim.

JobStore/HUD/CLI au creare și editare pentru cele patru acțiuni, constructor vizual de program, 16 blueprint-uri cu formulare tipizate, repeat limitat atomic și livrare per job către canale deja configurate sau doar istoric. Există doctor, incidents (pauze după eșecuri), notepad editabil, status/remove și tick idempotent în fusul scheduler-ului, refuzat când scheduler-ul rulează. Gate-urile task/quiet hours/buget/e-stop sunt păstrate; flush-ul mesajelor amânate verifică acum e-stop. Accesul Automations din bara principală deschide un spațiu dedicat; dialogul nativ de creare gestionează focusul, Tab, Escape și revenirea la buton. Tipurile OpenAPI includ cele patru rute noi. Review: update scrie doar câmpurile cerute și nu poate reseta rezervările atomice; istoricul păstrează textul efectiv pentru brief/remind fără livrare. Scripturile Python locale au acum snapshot de sursă legat de aprobarea fiecărei execuții, rezultate pending persistente și livrare directă no_agent sau context izolat ca date neîncrezătoare. API/CLI disting acceptarea de finalizare; conținutul gol nu apelează modelul. Manual run now persists a bounded receipt and returns HTTP 202; scheduler/offline tick executes through the shared job firing path. Atomic coalescing and portable cross-process locks prevent duplicate execution. Configuration snapshots, pending-script reconciliation, crash-unknown state without replay, and concurrent retention are tested. HUD and CLI restore accepted request status and distinguish queued, waiting and completed execution. Ask jobs now persist effective request-local model/provider pins through CLI/HUD options, with preflight routing, closed lifetimes, approved-model enforcement and resolved context budgets. Unavailable pins fail explicitly; ordinary chat configuration is unchanged. Independent review repaired file_read re-spilling under a pinned window. Owner-authored reminder media IDs now produce actual bounded Telegram file/text delivery with frozen content/recipient bindings, a validated total deadline and durable held/partial/unknown outcomes. CLI/HUD authoring and status expose these outcomes; editing an explicit empty options document clears prior settings correctly. Approved script-only options.workdir now persists a canonical existing directory within current terminal roots for script plus no_agent:true. CLI/HUD author it, doctor checks availability, and each task freezes cwd before fresh approval. Real concurrent subprocess tests verify relative reads and unchanged parent cwd; denial, e-stop, deleted/escaping directories, restart and changed task arguments are covered. Model project instructions/tool workspace context remains unsupported. Model-bearing ask jobs now accept enabled_toolsets through CLI and HUD using an explicit installed basic/files/terminal catalog. Missing/null retains defaults; [] disables tool offers. Immutable per-run name sets intersect both runtime/profile offers and ToolRPC intake before preflight, handlers or approval enqueue. Nested scopes only narrow and inherit revocation; ordinary callers and concurrent jobs retain isolated defaults. Unknown/unavailable groups refuse. Existing approvals retain frozen concrete arguments and do not reread job options or revive a request scope. Doctor reports the configured tool-name upper bound, not effective contextual offers. Actual runner/Agent/RPC, queued-edit/restart, cancellation, UI and concurrency tests are evidence; tool selection grants no new authority. reviews.summary:
An agent's persona can now be edited in the UI and is live on its next turn. That is Hermes' persona editor, over the version history Nerva already kept. Until now the history was a side record: a commit or rollback in the Prompts panel changed a JSON file while the agent kept its old persona. agents/core/soul_edit.py holds the one path an edit takes, apply_soul (:152). (1) Refusals. An agent the hub has not loaded is refused (404; agent_folder, :100, returns an enumerated folder name in the id alphabet, so no request value reaches a path). So is text over MAX_SOUL_BYTES (256 KiB of UTF-8, :40; 413), safe mode (:171; 409, because overlays are not read there, H275) and a persona the H387 guard would drop (:174; 422 with the verdict). guard_verdict (:60) runs the same scan and cap as Agent._load_soul, and GET /api/agents/{id}/soul now reports it through the same function. A line the guard only quarantines is applied, and the verdict names it. (2) Nothing live is lost. The first edit keeps the file on disk as v1 ("on disk before the first edit"). A file changed on disk since the last version, such as a hand edit, is kept as its own version ("on disk, changed outside the editor") before it is replaced (:185). An agent with no persona file has nothing to keep. (3) Written where the model reads it. The text goes to the owner's overlay (overlay_path, :115): souls/<id>/SOUL.local.md in the data home, else the repo-local SOUL.local.md, never the shipped SOUL.md. The write is atomic (_write_atomically, :126: temporary file, fsync, replace; a failure leaves no temporary file and records no new version). (4) Versioned, then live. The text is committed (:195; the same text twice is one version). The agent re-reads its persona (_load_soul, :197), and the result says whether the running agent now reads the written file. (5) Audited without the text. A SETTINGS_CHANGE row names the agent, the version and its hash. A plain commit and a history-only rollback are audited the same way (record_version, :224; agents/core/routers/admin.py:805, :860). Surfaces. PUT /api/admin/agents/{id}/soul {content, message} (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:132, admin). POST /api/admin/prompts/{id}/rollback applies the version through the same path for a loaded agent (agents/core/routers/admin.py:846); the shared contract _identity (served from IDENTITY.local.md) and keys that are no loaded agent keep the history-only rollback. Description. A description: field in the SOUL front-matter is the agent's one-line description (description_of, :84, and description_in, :89: one line, at most 400 characters). It is listed on GET /agents and the SOUL read (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:179, :124) and is never part of the prompt. POST /api/admin/agents/{id}/description/draft (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:150; draft_description, :238) asks the strict-local model for one paragraph from the live persona and saves nothing. With no local model it is a 503, never a cloud call (:255-258). HUD. The Dossier has an Edit persona button that opens the live SOUL in frontend/src/soul-edit.tsx (SoulEditor, :49, mounted at frontend/src/modes.tsx:96). It offers Preview against the live text, Apply, Draft description with Use it (withDescription, :15, writes the front-matter line), and the hub's refusal in words (refusalText, :32). The Dossier also shows the description. The Prompts panel (PromptsPanel in frontend/src/gap.tsx, not pinned: high-churn) gets apply beside commit, through the same PUT, and says when a rollback is live. Tests: tests/test_soul_edit_route.py (29) covers the apply, the seed and hand-edit versions, deduplication, blocked and quarantined text, the audit row, size, ids, an unloaded folder, admin, the repo overlay, safe mode, a failed write, no store, a reload that misses the file, rollback (live, to the shipped text, refused, missing, history-only keys, audited), a plain commit, the description (listed, bounded, never prompted) and the draft (a proposal, strict-local, empty). frontend/src/test/soul-edit.test.tsx has 6. tests/test_h10_22_prompt_versioning.py now asserts that the rollback is live, in a throwaway data home. 61 mutants: 58 caught, eight of them after survivors got cases. Two survivors of the first-edit-only seed led to keeping hand edits as versions; that code's own five mutants are caught. The fsync is a crash-only property. Built on this branch. Hermes has a Documentation page inside its dashboard with an "open in a new tab" affordance. Nerva's written material (the user guide, FLAGS.md on what each posture flag costs, and the privacy and camera-privacy notes) was only in the repository. The Dockerfile copied it into the image, but nothing served it.

(1) The route. agents/core/routers/help_docs.py is registered on the app in agents/web.py (not pinned: a high-churn file; the pinned route tests drive web.app) and user-guarded on the router (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:27).
- GET /api/help/docs (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:103) lists the allowlist: slug, title, whether the file shipped, and each document's sections.
- GET /api/help/docs/{slug} (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:113) returns the Markdown text, capped at MAX_DOC_CHARS with a truncated flag (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:121).
- The allowlist is the fixed DOCS table (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:31): user-guide, flags, privacy, camera-privacy. A slug is only ever a key into it, never joined into a path, so an unknown slug, '../' or encoded traversal is 404.
- A file must be a regular file under the install root; a symlink is refused (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:85). A file missing from an install reads as "not available", not an error.
- Responses are no-store.

(2) The page. DocsPanel (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:37) is registered in the console's Start group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:6), in PANEL_COMPONENTS (frontend/src/gap.tsx:5277) and in the desktop app's route allowlist (desktop/src-tauri/hud-routes.json:49).
- It lists the documents, disabling one not shipped, and renders the chosen one through the new shared Markdown component (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:101).
- That component emits React elements only (no innerHTML path): headings with anchors, code fences, pipe tables, lists, quotes and rules, plus bold, italic, inline code and links. A link renders only for http(s) or a same-origin path, in a new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer (safeHref, frontend/src/markdown.tsx:25). Raw HTML in a document stays literal text. There is no regex lookbehind, so older Safari can parse the bundle.

(3) Open in a new tab. Every document is a standalone deep link, /v2/console/docs?doc=<slug>[#section] (docHref, frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:15). The panel offers it as "open in a new tab ↗" with rel=noopener noreferrer (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:67), and a #section is scrolled into view (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:49).

(4) The flag's cost where it is flipped, per the row rationale.
- Each document's sections carry the names their headings document. The hub computes them with heading_anchor (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:44), which one shared fixture pins character for character to the renderer's headingAnchor (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:94).

(1) One confirmation, graded by RiskTier. frontend/src/confirm.tsx declares RISK_TIER (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:19) with the names and values of agents/core/autonomy/policy.py:26 RiskTier, and tests/test_confirm_tiers.py:22 ties the two lists together. confirmStyle (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:23) gives READ_ONLY one click, REVERSIBLE two steps (the button arms, a second button confirms) and EXTERNAL and IRREVERSIBLE_OR_MONEY a phrase typed exactly (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:143); a tier it does not know takes the most. ConfirmAction (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:74) moves focus to the control that replaced the one pressed. Escape cancels, and a cancelled phrase is not remembered (frontend/src/confirm.tsx:95). Enter confirms only on a match. An action that returns a promise keeps the confirmation open, with both buttons held, until it lands; one that answers false keeps it armed to retry (fire, frontend/src/confirm.tsx:97). A page can open and close it itself (armed/onCancel, frontend/src/confirm.tsx:114, taking focus as it opens, :110) or keep a typed one always open (open: no trigger, no cancel). (2) Every hand-rolled site uses it. The kill switch's HALT ALL stays one click on purpose (READ_ONLY, frontend/src/gap.tsx:779), because an emergency stop must never wait for a second click; disengage is typed (DISENGAGE, frontend/src/gap.tsx:777, :778). Forget-me types FORGET (frontend/src/gap.tsx:3655) and the acquisition purge its phrase (frontend/src/gap.tsx:4590). Trust-ops rotation types the scope in an always-open confirmation that a refusal leaves filled and a rotation clears (frontend/src/panels/trust-ops.tsx:397). The marketplace uninstall types the folder it deletes, because the rmtree has no undo on this box; a changed folder is typed again, and a refusal keeps it armed (frontend/src/panels/marketplace-admin.tsx:313, confirmRemove :207). The webhook delete is two steps, opened by the row and held while that row's switch is pending (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:420, remove :285). The ESTOP pause is two steps (frontend/src/modes3.tsx:216). tests/test_confirm_tiers.py:26 checks that each of these files imports and uses ConfirmAction and has no window.confirm. (3) Markdown wherever agent text is shown. Chat bubbles, for agent and vision replies (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:79, :96), and decision cards (frontend/src/shell.tsx:144) render through Bubble (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:130). Bubble is memoised on the text, so a streamed token re-parses one bubble. It uses the shared React-only Markdown (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:101): lists, fences, tables and http(s) or same-origin links render, while raw HTML and any other link stay text. Canvas Markdown artifacts go through the same renderer (MarkdownBody, frontend/src/artifacts.tsx:78) and are bounded to MARKDOWN_LIMIT (4,000) code points when shown as well as when saved. A new breaks option (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:171) keeps a single newline as a line break for chat and artifacts, and documents keep paragraph joining. The owner's own turns are shown exactly as typed. Test-manual gap G22 (collapsed newlines, fences as prose) is closed. reviews.summary: Governed SSH terminal execution remains available only for declared, enabled targets. The runner applies hardline, audited target policy, durable approval, the terminal.exec contract and Action Kernel before the built-in SSH transport; the transport reconstructs a quoted remote argv, pins known hosts, requires key authentication, bypasses user SSH config and agent, and disables forwarding and ControlMaster (agents/core/environments/execution.py:162-231,390-405,743-923; agents/core/environments/ssh_transport.py:310-344,346-415). Owner-once approvals now add a private, one-use physical gate at ssh_transport.py:396-400: it rechecks the exact request, target decision, kernel decision and runtime before spawn. Tests prove paused policy/kernel revocation blocks dispatch and spawn (tests/test_h485_owner_once_transport.py). This adds no connection manager, real-host interoperability evidence, or other missing Hermes features. Batch collateral review (2026-10-04, base9bfa085c): The manual (legacy) kernel lane was then explicitly `decision.backend == "docker"`; it now also admits local and SSH targets only when a request check and legacy kernel check are configured (execution.py:215-220). The initial cross-backend refusal-precedence regression was corrected in 02aba704: the existing SSH-flag-off fixture again receives `ssh_transport_not_implemented` without a request callback. SSH transport, private owner-once gate and this row’s remaining remote-manager limitations are unchanged. The corrected six-module offline scope passed 413 cases; no real SSH host was contacted. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): execution.py and ssh_transport.py diffed from 02aba704/42840e3d: run() and both dispatch branches only moved, and the accepted-manual (legacy) kernel lane, formerly Docker-only, now also covers local and SSH when a request check and legacy kernel check are wired, with its own pre-spawn physical gate on SSH (ssh_transport.py:401-405) and tests/test_h011_manual_host_kernel.py added as its proof; the SSH-flag-off refusal (execution.py:390-392) and the remote-manager gaps are unchanged; 151 pinned tests pass, no real SSH host contacted.
reviews.remaining: Rândul cere mult peste execuție și restul nu e livrat: manager de conexiuni ControlMaster, erori clasificate, sugestii de gazde din ~/.ssh/config, bootstrap care refolosește-sau-pornește un serviciu remote, revalidare de liveness, tranzacție de update cu jurnal de recuperare și linii de restore per profil, fan-out "update all instances". ControlMaster e o divergență deliberată, nu o scăpare: un socket de control partajat e un canal autentificat reutilizabil lăsat pe disc, iar transportul îl dezactivează explicit. NEVERIFICAT pe hardware: nicio sesiune SSH reală nu a fost deschisă din această livrare — suita e ermetică, fără socket și fără binar ssh, deci interoperabilitatea cu un sshd real rămâne nedovedită.

reviews.summary: Default-off per-turn keep-awake with host.control gate, refcount and release. Battery/resume state via guarded snapshot/SSE, scheduled tick and background job deferral. Desktop background-throttling policy on both webviews. Current verification: 75 passed, 1 rustc skip; power-chip Vitest passed in 23-test group; no native Windows/systemd/macOS acceptance.
reviews.remaining: Windows keep-awake state can be falsely reported active: _windows_set_state ignores SetThreadExecutionState return value (zero means failure), while KeepAwake._start unconditionally sets _win_held=True (agents/core/power.py:173-177, :280-283). SetThreadExecutionState is per calling thread, but acquire/release may execute on different turn/shutdown threads; release on another thread may not clear the original assertion. Use one owning thread or a host-supported process-level mechanism, validate return and release on that owner; cover failure and cross-thread behavior. Host-bound systemd/macOS/Windows and browser background behavior has no live acceptance in this review; H182 cannot be claimed fully equivalent from mocks alone.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 together with H153 (critic note 7: one spec, one panel), then fixed after an adversarial review. The v2 console has a Webhooks panel, WebhooksPanel (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:187), registered in the Interop group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:50; the entry is asserted at frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx:71). Interop mode's WEBHOOKS list links to it by an accessible name (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:343). Every panel call sends the admin credential. The backend stays admin-only CRUD: list, create, switch and delete all carry Depends(admin_guard) (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:175, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:181, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:194, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:221).

Interop mode is built from its four sources alone (hydrateInterop, frontend/src/api/live.ts:126). All four (A2A peers, MCP servers, widgets, webhooks) are admin-only routes and are fetched with the admin credential, and so is the webhooks settings category: while the receiver switch is off every webhook row reads "receiver off", and a switch it could not read is said under WEBHOOKS (frontend/src/api/live.ts:119, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:344). A section whose source failed is empty and says "not connected", and an empty real list says "none" (Section, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:304); the demo seed's rows are never shown under the LIVE chip. When no source answers nothing is overwritten, so the mode stays "Not connected" and DEMO keeps its seed. The review found that fetching only the webhooks list with the credential had marked the whole mode LIVE over seeded peers, MCP servers and widgets.

The five accepted parts:
(1) Create dialog: name, agent or workflow target, target id and an HMAC-signed toggle, and, since H153, a description, an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only, posted to POST /api/webhooks. A refusal shows the hub's own reason, and an empty target is refused before any request. The create button is held while the call is pending and while a new hook's credentials are on screen, so a second hook cannot replace a secret before it was saved.
(2) Created result, shown once (Reveal, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:145): the absolute trigger URL (triggerUrl, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:52: the page origin, the base path and the encoded id), and the token, or the signing secret for a signed hook, each with a copy button that says "copied" in a polite live region, plus the header the sender must send. Only the warning sentence is an alert, so a screen reader does not read the secret aloud. On a loopback origin it says a sender elsewhere needs an address it can reach. The secret lives only in the panel's state and is dropped on "I have saved it" (focus returns to the create form) or unmount. The list never carries it: WebhookStore masks the token to a 4-character hint (agents/core/webhooks.py:635).
(3) Detail pane: clicking a hook expands its trigger URL, auth header (with the token hint), calls, last call and creation time, the deliveries its event list skipped and the last event skipped, and an editor for its event list and prompt template (H153). The row shows target_type:target, an HMAC or token badge, an on/off badge and an event-count badge.
(4) Delete with confirmation: "delete…" arms an inline confirmation that explains the sender's credential dies with the hook and moves focus to "delete for good", which sends DELETE; "keep it" returns focus to "delete…". Each row button's accessible name includes the hook's name. A row's buttons are held while its call is pending, and every switch or delete reloads the list whatever the hub answered: a hook already deleted elsewhere is reported as gone ("ci was already deleted", "ci no longer exists") and its row disappears, with focus moved to the create form; a refused delete keeps the confirmation and says why. A per-hook on/off switch (PATCH, H153) is offered as the reversible alternative.
(5) Governance: creating, switching and deleting a hook each write a SecurityEvent (_audit_webhook, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:143, called at agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:190, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:215 and agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:227). It names the hook id, the target as a JSON string (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:137), so a target cannot pass its own text off as the row's id or flags, and the signed and enabled flags as the store reads them, never the token or signing secret. A delete of an unknown id writes no webhook audit row (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:226) and answers 404 "webhook not found" (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:229). Since #1247 the admin guard's own auth telemetry (AUTH_SUCCESS and AUTH_FAILURE rows) lands in the same audit log, so the backend tests set those rows aside before counting webhook rows (_action_events, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:266); an unknown switch adds none (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:322) and a repeated delete adds none (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:331).

The receiver-disabled banner: when the receiver switch (H153, the setting webhooks.receiver_enabled) is off, the panel's receiver row says every delivery is refused until it is switched back on (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:352). The restart-gateway banner is not needed: a delivery sees the switch at most a second old (at once after a write in this process), and hook CRUD is served live; the receiver row says so. Not built, and not part of this row: a `nerva webhooks` CLI verb (critic note 7 places it with H409, as `nerva webhooks inbound|outbound`) and a mobile screen.

Tests: frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx has 56 cases. By describe block, 23 are this row's (the panel, the trigger URL and the review round; one of them, an open delete confirmation held while the same row switches, was added by H168), and 13 of those failed on the pre-review panel: the pending hold, the reload and the ghost row after a switch or delete, the one-POST create and the create held while a secret shows, the hook-named buttons, focus, the alert without the secret, the "copied" live region, the loopback hint and an unencodable id. The other 33 are H153's: the subscriptions, the receiver row and banner, the event list, the template, Deliver to, focus after a hook is gone, the push note and a proxy's 404. frontend/src/test/interop-live-honesty.test.tsx (14 cases, 5 of them H153's receiver read) drives the real useLiveModes against admin-guarded mock routes and renders InteropMode. The backend audit and DELETE guards are pinned in tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:367, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:377, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:386); the file has 35 cases. Mutation: 60 mutants of the review round's guards (11 backend, 27 panel, 15 Interop, 7 v1) and 16 of the H153 panel additions were each run against their own suite, and all were caught; before the review round, 12 of the reviewer's 42 mutants had survived.  Re-read 2026-10-12 (b339672c): the only change to agents/core/routers/webhooks.py is the quiet-hours hour now read in the app zone (H450 fix); no claim or cited line of this row moved.

reviews.summary: The HUD's keyboard shortcuts live in one registry, as in Hermes. frontend/src/shortcuts.ts defines every action once (ACTIONS: id, category, label, default chord, scope): the ten mode keys, World (w), the Console (`), Ambient (a), Cinema (m) and its three stages (o, n, b, scope cinema), focus the message box (/), the command palette (mod+k) and the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (mod+/). app.tsx (World's key included: WorldAwareApp passes onWorld and shares the live overrides through useShortcutOverrides) and the cinema overlay in shell.tsx dispatch through matchAction over bindings(overrides) instead of literal key maps, and every key hint (palette, top bar, World, Console, cinema stages) is read from the registry (chordOf, displayChord). A matched action takes the key from the browser (preventDefault); Shift+letter falls back to the bare letter unless it is bound itself. frontend/src/shortcuts-panel.tsx is the panel mod+/ opens: categories Navigation, View, Composer and Session with search (searchBindings); click a chord to record a new one ("Press a key…", Esc cancels, a lone modifier keeps listening; chordFromEvent, rebind); the palette and the panel take only a chord held with Ctrl/⌘ or Alt (acceptsChord), fire in an input only then (firesInInputs), and the palette always has a Keyboard shortcuts entry, so no rebinding can lock the panel out; Space is spelled "space", and a chord with no key is refused on record and on read; Esc closes the panel without closing what lies beneath; per-binding reset and Reset all (resetBinding); an "Also bound to X" note when two actions share a chord (conflictsFor). Overrides persist per viewer in localStorage under hud.shortcuts, validated on read (readOverrides, loadOverrides, saveOverrides), and survive storage that is off. Governance: defineActions refuses any action whose id, category or label names an approval, a decision, an accept, reject, deny or consent (FORBIDDEN_TARGET), so no chord can reach a Decision Inbox action. Tests: frontend/src/test/shortcuts.test.tsx (25), app-routing.test.tsx (+14: panel, rebinding, persistence, World, composer focus, the Space and Ctrl+Space lockout, the palette entry, the typing guard, preventDefault, World behind the panel, storage off, live hints, Esc beneath, Cinema), cinema.test.tsx (+1: rebound stage keys); voice-orb and briefing-wall expect the registry's stage titles; 38 mutants, 36 killed, 2 equivalent; the review round's 19 mutants, all killed (4 by tests added after a first pass). Re-review on 2026-10-02: The current app diff only passes the active agent into the image composer; keyboard shortcut behavior remains unchanged. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. reviews.summary:
Archived chats exist, as in Hermes. CheckpointManager.set_archived stamps or clears archived_at in a session's metadata without creating a session. get_sessions(archived=...) filters on it in SQL, read only from valid JSON, so the limit counts only the view asked for. agents/core/routers/sessions.py serves several routes. GET /sessions leaves archived chats out; ?archived=true lists only them, each row with archived_at. POST /sessions/{id}/archive and /unarchive (user_guard) are 404 for an unknown session and 400 for an invalid id. Resuming a chat through POST /sessions/resume unarchives it. agents/core/session_archive.py holds the rest. run_auto_archive archives sessions whose ended_at, else started_at, is older than memory.auto_archive_days (0 = off, at most 3650) and never touches the active one; it runs as the archive phase of the hourly, interval-gated data lifecycle sweep (SchedulerService.schedule_retention), which replaced the separate 03:40 job; pinned chats are never auto-archived. DELETE /sessions/{id}?confirm=DELETE (admin_guard) holds the session's turn lease (409 session_busy) and the memory locks. It refuses the chat in use (409), a chat another chat continues (409 has_continuations), and an id that is not a session or whose snapshot is not this session's (404). delete_session first writes an encrypted, fsynced, read-back backup (the backup cipher, key under JARVIS_KEY_DIR) of the session's rows (session, checkpoints, clock, continuation seed, history binding, foreign-import receipt), transcript snapshot and log (unreadable ones byte for byte), compaction archive, checklist and note. The backup goes to <data root>-forget-archives/sessions/<id>-<stamp>.json.enc, outside the data root, keeping the newest JARVIS_SESSION_BACKUP_KEEP=10. Only then does it delete them and clear the live conversation, with the chat's turn embeddings (VectorStore.remove_where; 503 recall_unavailable if the store cannot) and with secure_delete plus a WAL truncate. Facts already extracted into the knowledge graph, and the audit log, are not touched. A backup that does not land raises backup_failed and deletes nothing. The file work runs off the event loop. The HUD SessionsPanel (frontend/src/panels/sessions.tsx) has chats and archived tabs, archive, unarchive and a two-step "delete permanently" that names the backup. llm.project_dir only sets the folder whose convention files H594 reads (project_context.start_dir); file tools (FileScope.resolve, list_dir, search_files) and the terminal cwd still resolve relative paths from the first file root, and the setting's label says so. Hermes' "what can it do right now" view is here: one read-only answer, for one agent as seen by one principal, built from the code a turn runs and served on three surfaces. agents/core/inspector.py holds it; build_inspector (:108) returns up to five sections (SECTIONS, :63). (1) Views. VIEWS (:56) names the five tool-profile postures: the owner and a guest on the HUD (owner, guest), the owner and a stranger on an external channel (inbound-owner, inbound; Telegram stands for every channel, under the inbound action origin a real channel turn has) and no human (internal). The look binds that principal and origin in a task of its own (:125), so nothing it binds, and nothing the runtime notes while resolving the offer, outlives it. (2) status (_status, :155): version, the backend and model the router serves, the local model's state through project_llm_status, the transcript budget llm.tool_loop_context_tokens (0 reads as 75 % of the model window), the tool loop and safe mode. (3) tools (_tools, :194): the tool runtime's own resolved offer for the agent under that principal (_resolve_offer: registry or the capability registry's view, job toolset, posture, the agent's tools: list, the shared-session rule), not the raw registry. Each row says whether the tool is gated and whether its output is fenced as untrusted, with the description cut to DESCRIPTION_CHARS (160, :65). The withheld names are listed, a resolver failure offers nothing, and loop_enabled says whether the model sees any of them (with the loop off they are what the posture would offer). (4) skills (_skills, :215): the rows prompt_catalog gives the prompt under that principal and that offer, or none when llm.skills_in_prompt is off. (5) mcp (_mcp, :225): each server's transport, trust tier, transport-aware liveness (is_connected, so an HTTP server reads connected; a probe that raises is down) and visible tools, with no URL or command line. (6) system_prompt (_prompt, :253): the agent's system prompt and the user part Agent.build_prompt sends for an empty user message: persona, agent context, the core-memory block, the runtime, language and grounding rails and the skills block. tokens (:280) estimates what that fixed part costs every turn before history. The texts are masked by the log redactor (SecretRedactionFilter; nothing is shown when it cannot load, _redactor :73) and capped together at PROMPT_CAP_BYTES (64 KiB, :64) on a character boundary. The core block is read with freeze=False (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3713, documented at :3688, read by the prompt builder at :3832): the frozen block when a turn froze one, else a fresh render that is not kept, so a look never fixes the day's snapshot. GET /api/admin/inspector?agent=&view=&section= (agents/core/routers/status.py:123, admin-guarded; 404 for an unknown agent, 400 naming the views or sections, 503 before the hub is up). nerva inspect [agent] [--as VIEW] [--section tools|skills|prompt|mcp|status] [--json] (cmd_inspect, agents/cli/nerva.py:1118; render_inspector :1139) prints the same payload section by section, or as it came. reviews.summary:
Nerva now knows which surface holds each microphone. A surface arms only if the owner allowed its kind; one device's microphone has one holder at a time; and arming, pausing, resuming and stopping carry the surface's identity and are audited. This is the adaptation's missing concept, on top of the voice primitives that already existed (wake word, push-to-talk and hands-free capture, TTS, STT, capabilities, and H222's listening indicator). The lease table is agents/core/voice/mic.py (MicArbiter, agents/core/voice/mic.py:93; one process-wide ARBITER, agents/core/voice/mic.py:232).
(1) Surfaces and devices. A surface is kind:client: host:hub (the hub's own wake-word pipeline), hud:<tab> or mobile:<device> (ARMABLE, agents/core/voice/mic.py:39). A Wyoming satellite has its own microphone and is not armed here. A lease is for one device. host is the machine the hub runs on, and a browser that the route sees on loopback shares it. The route decides that from the address a trusted proxy vouches for (_mic_device, agents/core/routers/voice.py:527), so a LAN client cannot claim to be local. Otherwise a browser gets remote:hud:<tab>, and every phone gets mobile:<device>.
(2) One holder per device. A second surface arming a held device is refused, naming the holder (MicRefused mic_busy, agents/core/voice/mic.py:49; HTTP 409). With take_over, it pauses the holder and tells it (on_change, agents/core/voice/mic.py:144). A pause frees the device (agents/core/voice/mic.py:199). A resume asks again, both for consent and for the device's holder (agents/core/voice/mic.py:212). A stop releases the lease (agents/core/voice/mic.py:221).
(3) Consent. A kind arms only if the setting voice.mic_surfaces allows it (allowed_kinds, agents/core/voice/mic.py:59). The setting is a declared tags setting whose values are validated against host, hud and mobile (agents/core/settings_db.py:254, agents/core/settings_db.py:1153). The default is hud and mobile (DEFAULT_ALLOWED, agents/core/voice/mic.py:40): surfaces someone uses on purpose. The hub's always-on listener needs host added. So VoiceChannel.start (agents/core/channels/voice.py:29) opens the host microphone only with a lease. Before this, it started at boot with no check. It stops the pipeline when taken over and starts it again when given back (_on_lease, agents/core/channels/voice.py:48). Withdrawn consent ends a lease at its next renewal.
(4) Leases lapse. A browser or phone lease lapses LEASE_SECONDS (45, agents/core/voice/mic.py:42) after its last renewal (_expire_locked, agents/core/voice/mic.py:108). The host pipeline's lease does not lapse. The table holds at most 32 leases.
(5) Audit. Every arm, take-over, pause, stop and refusal is one audit row naming the surface and the device. A renewal is not.
(6) Routes, all user-guarded. GET /api/voice/mic answers who holds each device, the paused leases and the allowed kinds (agents/core/routers/voice.py:548). POST /api/voice/mic/arm (agents/core/routers/voice.py:557) takes hud or mobile and answers 403 or 409. /pause, /resume and /stop act on a lease by name (agents/core/routers/voice.py:576, agents/core/routers/voice.py:587, agents/core/routers/voice.py:601).
(7) The HUD. The voice loop arms its lease before getUserMedia (frontend/src/voice.ts:414; armMic, frontend/src/mic-lease.ts:47) and renews it every 20 s (frontend/src/voice.ts:434). It releases the lease on every end of the loop (frontend/src/voice.ts:135). If a renewal is refused, it stops and says who took the microphone. Only a hub refusal blocks: a hub that cannot answer does not. The loop offers take over (takeOver, frontend/src/voice.ts:454; the voice pill, frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:256). The voice settings list the holders, with pause, resume and stop (MicLeases, frontend/src/mic-leases.tsx:17).

A settings reset now shows what it will change, never touches a secret and can be undone, and the HUD marks every setting that differs from its default. Hermes' config-reset and defaults surface is covered, on top of H157's search, secret-free export, dry-run import and per-category reset. (1) Defaults. Every declared row that is not a secret carries its declared default (agents/core/settings_db.py:739, in _mark_overlay :731, used by GET /api/admin/settings and each category read). A secret carries none. The Settings panel marks a row whose value, or staged edit, differs from its default ("changed", with the default in its tooltip); a ↺ button stages the default and the usual save writes it through the validated PUT (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2856). (2) A preview before any reset. plan_reset (agents/core/settings_db.py:1493) computes what a reset of one category, or of every category, would write: each declared setting that is neither a secret nor a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and whose stored value is not its default. POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset and POST /api/admin/settings/reseed take {"dry_run": true} and answer the changes as current → default without writing anything (agents/core/routers/admin.py:391, :430; _dry_run_asked, :379; only a JSON true, in a body of at most 4 KB). The changes use describe_changes, so a credential-shaped value shows as (hidden). Arming the reset in the HUD asks for that preview and lists it, and counts the settings kept (secrets and route-only rows, all labelled secrets) and names the settings the posture still forces (ResetPreview, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:64; ResetCategory, :92). (3) The reseed no longer deletes the store. It used to run DELETE FROM settings, wiping every setting, secrets included, with no preview and no way back. It is now the per-category reset over every category: secrets and route-only rows are kept (and named), rows nothing declares are left, it takes a JSON request from this origin only (415/403 otherwise, as H157's writes), and it is audited with the settings that moved (agents/core/routers/admin.py:430). The v1 admin page sends it as JSON (agents/web/static/admin.js:1520). The HUD gets "reset every category…" with the same preview (ResetAll, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:115). (4) Undo. reset_settings (agents/core/settings_db.py:1533) writes the defaults and records what it replaced in settings_resets (:120) in the same transaction, keeping the last 20 (RESETS_KEPT, :1516). POST /api/admin/settings/undo (agents/core/routers/admin.py:461; undo_last_reset, agents/core/settings_db.py:1590) puts back the latest reset not yet undone. A setting changed since that reset, one its declaration no longer accepts, or one no longer declared is left as it is and named in skipped. The undo is audited, and the listeners hear every value a reset or an undo writes, so the webhook receiver switch follows it. GET /api/admin/settings/resets (agents/core/routers/admin.py:91; list_resets, agents/core/settings_db.py:1577) lists the resets, newest first, naming settings but never their values. The HUD shows "last reset: <scope> · N settings · <time>" with "undo…" (UndoReset, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:135). Every reset and undo in the HUD is a two-step ConfirmAction at the REVERSIBLE tier (H168). Adapted from the row's ask: the reseed does not go through the approval queue's irreversible tier, because it is no longer irreversible. It keeps secrets, previews, and can be undone. Routing it through the queue would need a new kernel action kind for it, and none is declared (agents/core/kernel/registry.py's one settings kind is H613's settings.voice_command).
