reviews.summary: H270 stays PARTIAL; the triage's "already equivalent" does not survive contact with the code, and this re-read retires three claims the row had carried since before H502 (#1174 moved the hash while the text stood still) plus one the text was about to inherit. Hermes' contract has two halves and Nerva has only one of them. Outbound (what a child inherits) is genuinely stronger than Hermes and is tested: scrub_child_env (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:172-210) is default-deny with SAFE_ENV_PREFIXES (:17-33) plus the three-name JARVIS_CHILD_ALLOWED_ENV (:47-51), covered by tests/test_environment_primitives.py:62,90; STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST (agents/core/mcp/client.py:161-173) with stdio_env_baseline (:245-280) drops a credential-shaped name even when it is on the static list (:275, _SECRET_LIKE :174-176), covered by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:351 — and since H502 the baseline is the DEFAULT, not an opt-in: stdio_env_baseline_enabled() returns env_flag(STDIO_ENV_BASELINE_FLAG, True) (:179-190; flag :90 "Default ON"), docs/FLAGS.md says "on by default since H502" (its MCP defaults block, the JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE entry and the flag table row), and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins unset-flag → OPENAI_API_KEY withheld and =0 → full inherit (the row previously cited :395-399 as pinning the opposite; that was the pre-#1174 test, which at 45be62bd read "Flag off (default): historical behaviour — inherit everything"). The outbound allowlist's one deliberate exception is the owner's own: a name listed in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — owner-declared and host-wide, not an inbound gate. What #1179 changed here is disclosure, not policy: the module docstring (:17-39) now names the filesystem as a second recovery route for a same-UID child (cwd defaults to the hub's, so open(".env") reaches the file the keys came from), cwd_secret_files (:215-242) reports a readable .env/.env.local in the child's cwd, and _merged_env (:561-572) logs a WARNING "withholding is undercut" (:567) beside the INFO count, filenames only — pinned by tests :830-853 and :854-890. None of it touches a name policy, a writer or the override path, so it moves nothing for this row. The fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) is likewise off-subject: it added tool_patterns_over_bounds (agents/core/mcp/client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ (:407-418) and a bounds refusal for tools_allow/tools_deny in admin_mcp_add (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:216-222); none of it reads or writes an env name, and MCPServerConfig still has no env field, so only line numbers moved (client.py +19 from the new helper on and +31 from that __init__ block on; routers/mcp.py +4 from the filter check on). Inbound (what a surface may persist) has no general policy: no ENV_WRITE/WRITE_DENYLIST/writable_env symbol and no `config.write` kind in agents/core/capability_actions.py (the only ENV_VAR_NAME symbol is skills/frontmatter.py's _ENV_VAR_NAME, a syntax check on a skill's declared required variable names that writes nothing). Since H595 (#1243, 852ea63e) one inbound name policy does exist, for one writer: the llm.execute_code_env_passthrough setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:225) persists host environment-variable NAMES that execute_code may pass into its interpreter, and validate_category refuses any name that agents/core/code_env.py:84-92 _passable_name rejects (agents/core/settings_db.py:993-999); the same check filters skill-declared names in CodeEnvRegistry (agents/core/code_env.py:192). _passable_name is a denylist plus a name-format check, not a declared-names allowlist: it refuses the control names and prefixes at agents/core/code_env.py:65-77 (PATH, SHELL, HOME, ENV, BASH_ENV, NODE_OPTIONS and every PYTHON*, LD_*, DYLD_*, GIT_CONFIG*, LC_* and XDG_* name), the exact managed credential set at agents/core/code_env.py:35-61 and any JARVIS_/HERMES_/AUXILIARY_ name, but it passes NODE_PATH, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, BROWSER and GIT_SSH_COMMAND (checked directly at HEAD), which Hermes' denylist refuses. Values for passed names come only from the host's own environment, never from the writer.  A correction the row must carry, because it shapes the deliverable: Hermes' hijack names are NOT all absent from the code. Outside the H595 code_env denylist above (which names NODE_OPTIONS and the LD_/DYLD_/PYTHON prefixes), LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PYTHONSTARTUP, GIT_SSH_COMMAND and PAGER appear in no other product code, but PATH and SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are MEMBERS of the two outbound allowlists — deliberately, because a child needs them as plumbing — and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 pinning that collect_tokens keeps only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. So the two allowlists the rationale points at as the pattern to reuse admit precisely the names Hermes forbids on write; the inbound registry has to be its own list, and "run overrides through the same name policy" is not by itself a fix, since that policy passes PATH/NODE_PATH/PYTHONPATH untouched. Apart from that H595 setting there is still no env writer to gate: the hub's only os.environ assignment is the reality harness's JARVIS_STRICT_EGRESS toggle (agents/core/observability/reality_harness.py:685,714; the os.environ installs in session_kernels.py, sandbox.py and hermes_runtime/worker.py run inside child workers on an env the hub already computed; scripts/qa_audit_probes.py and scripts/install_smoke.py set os.environ only as probe/smoke harnesses); no set_key/dotenv write; agents/core/paths.py:135-139 only copies .env.example verbatim; GET /api/admin/env (agents/core/routers/admin.py:549-561) is read-only and mask-redacted, and its one sibling, GET /api/admin/env/sources (H273), is read-only and returns key names and layers only, so neither writes the environment; the HUD states it in its own copy (frontend/src/panels/workflows-advanced.tsx:48 "There is NO route to change either"). Nerva's actual config writer is settings_db.put_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:1209-1245), which UPSERTs only DEFAULTS-declared keys and skips the rest (agents/core/settings_db.py:1226-1236), behind validate_category (agents/core/settings_db.py:1112-1149) and the 422 at agents/core/routers/admin.py:195-206 — the right shape, and except for the H595 key above it holds settings keys, not env names. Three things are nevertheless still owed, so this is not equivalence. (1) The row's own deliverable — a declared-names allowlist at the write boundary, depends_on "the key registry" — is unbuilt (the H595 gate is a per-writer denylist with gaps), and the rationale defers rather than excludes it ("the moment the config writer lands, this must land with it"). (2) The MCP env boundary is unrefused: MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:145-156) has no env field and sets no model_config, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" SILENTLY DROPS an `env` body key rather than refusing it — reproduced at HEAD both on the model (model_config {} and env absent from model_dump) and end to end through TestClient: POST /api/admin/mcp with {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}} → 200 {"ok": true}, the stored MCPServer.env is {} and to_config() carries no env — and POST builds the MCPServer without one (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:226-238). The non-round-trip half IS now pinned — test_per_server_env_has_no_owner_reachable_config_surface (tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522, from #1174) asserts "env" not in MCPServerConfig.model_fields, to_config (agents/core/mcp/client.py:798-812) exports no env and load_from_config (:814-849) ignores one — but no test asserts the route REFUSES an env body, and the field it would fill is live: MCPServer.env (:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Reachability today: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449; no add form, nothing sends env) and no CLI or script adds servers, so the raw API is the only path. (3) Per-server overrides still bypass the allowlist in both branches: stdio_env_baseline applies them unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring agents/core/mcp/client.py:253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch — reachable only under JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 since H502 — does merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env) unfiltered (:575-576). Latent, not live: the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names set on the host (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56), and the admin route cannot pass one. Also checked and cleared: scripts/nerva_import.py IS a setup-flow writer that persists foreign env-var names verbatim (docstring scripts/nerva_import.py:31-32, .env lines scripts/nerva_import.py:357-358, JSON walk scripts/nerva_import.py:371, settings.json env block scripts/nerva_import.py:389-393, SecretStore write scripts/nerva_import.py:1034), but _SECRET_NAME_RE (scripts/nerva_import.py:85) is applied on every path and admits only credential-shaped names — tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 with tests/test_nerva_import.py:825 is the one existing test that exercises a hijack-shaped name (EDITOR) at an import boundary and pins it dropped — and SecretStore (agents/core/secrets.py) never exports a name to a process env (it reads only JARVIS_SECRET_KEY, :111). HEQ lot 1 moved two cited files without touching this row's subject: settings_db.py gained the H583 openrouter_* llm rows and a slug check inside _validate_value (settings keys, not env names; put_category and validate_category are unchanged), and scripts/nerva_import.py gained H344's skill.install mediation and --update re-import for skills, while its token path (the .env/JSON/settings.json readers and _SECRET_NAME_RE) is unchanged. Tests re-run on the lot-1 head: 55 passed, 0 failed across the four cited files (test_environment_primitives 6, test_mcp_transports 33 — two of them #1179's, test_mcp_admin 8, test_settings_integrity 8), and tests/test_nerva_import.py 44 passed, 1 skipped; none exercises an env-var write boundary. MCP transport audit collateral review (2026-10-09): the route adds only fixed-field authentication telemetry at the existing RPC gate. This row's admin/listing, validation or transport-auth behavior and remaining limitations are unchanged; its previously current mcp.py pin and explicit coordinates were reviewed. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): diffed routers/mcp.py since 39d6f81b, routers/admin.py and paths.py since 92c3eeb3, settings_db.py since 4b7714f9, and workflows-advanced.tsx and capability_actions.py since 91f595c3; the MCP env boundary (no env field, extra ignored, POST builds MCPServer without env), the unfiltered per-server overrides and the read-only env routes are unchanged and their citations were moved to HEAD lines, while H595 (#1243) added the first env-name writer, the llm.execute_code_env_passthrough setting gated by code_env._passable_name, whose denylist still admits NODE_PATH, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, BROWSER and GIT_SSH_COMMAND; the summary's no-writer and no-symbol claims were corrected, code_env.py and two H595 tests were pinned, and the pinned tests give 137 passed, 1 skipped.
reviews.remaining:
Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. #1179 changed nothing on this row's subject: its client.py change is an outbound disclosure (cwd_secret_files :215-242 and the "withholding is undercut" WARNING in _merged_env :561-572), not a name policy or a writer. Neither did the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1: tool_patterns_over_bounds, a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ and a tools_allow/tools_deny bounds refusal in admin_mcp_add) — it touches no env name, writer or override path and only moved line numbers. H502 (#1174) did change item 3 and half of item 2, and that is folded in here. Three items owed, two shippable today against real surfaces:

1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No general env-name registry exists and no `config.write` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py. The one writer that persists env-var names today, H595's llm.execute_code_env_passthrough setting and skill declarations, is gated by code_env._passable_name (agents/core/code_env.py:84-92, enforced at agents/core/settings_db.py:993-999), a denylist that still passes NODE_PATH, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, BROWSER and GIT_SSH_COMMAND; owed there: refuse those names too, or replace the denylist with the declared-names registry. Of Hermes' hijack names, PATH, SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:162), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are named as members of the two OUTBOUND allowlists, and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 (pinned dropped at tests/test_nerva_import.py:825). Design consequence: the outbound lists cannot double as the write-side registry — they deliberately admit the plumbing names Hermes forbids on write — so the registry is a separate, inbound-only list. When any env/config writer lands, that allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:147-151 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :159-160.

2. THE MCP `env` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED (shippable now; the "untested" half closed with #1174). MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:145-156) sets no `model_config`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes `POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it — reproduced end to end at HEAD through TestClient (200 {"ok": true}; stored MCPServer.env == {}; to_config() has no env key). The field it would populate is live — MCPServer.env (agents/core/mcp/client.py:424) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Already pinned by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522: `env` is not a MCPServerConfig field, to_config (:798-812) does not export it and load_from_config (:814-849) does not read it. Reachability: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449) and no CLI adds servers, so the raw admin API is the only path today. Still owed: `extra="forbid"` (or an explicit named refusal) on MCPServerConfig, plus a test asserting the route refuses an `env` body rather than swallowing it — and the same refusal must cover the hijack names above on the day `env` becomes operator-settable.

3. PER-SERVER `env` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:278-279; docstring :253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does `merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env)` with no filter (:575-576). The "decide whether the baseline should become the default" half of this item is DONE: since H502 the baseline is on unless JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 (:179-190; docs/FLAGS.md "on by default since H502") and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins both directions, so the legacy branch is now the explicit escape hatch rather than the shipped path. Owed: gate per-server overrides on the item-1 write-side registry (NOT merely on STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST + _SECRET_LIKE — that policy passes PATH, SHELL, NODE_PATH and would pass an operator-supplied PATH/NODE_PATH override untouched), or make the bypass an explicitly reviewed, audited exception. Severity, checked directly rather than inferred: LATENT. `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field, the admin route constructs MCPServer without one (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:226-238), and the only production caller passing an override is Nerva's own WorldView writer with an in-repo secret plus the WORLDVIEW_HOST_ENV names (agents/core/mcp/worldview_write.py:222-227, :49-56). No untrusted input reaches the override loop, so this is a boundary to close before `env` becomes operator-settable, not a live hole. The outbound allowlist's one intentional exception — a name the owner lists in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — is owner-declared and host-wide, and is not this row's write boundary.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only.

The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour:
- Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO.
- The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used.
- PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch.
- The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read.
- A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once.
- It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?".
- files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read.

provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running.

The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:463) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once:
- serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:244). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard.
- The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:473). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed.
- The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:106), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:73): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:490), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:72; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:110; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183).
- agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect.
- PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:83), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry.
- Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off.

Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:526) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment.
- What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:100).
- JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72).
- Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:93): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies.

The lists are measured, not declared:
- A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there.
- A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:667).

The two false read-again entries are fixed:
- The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:293; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:419). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:109): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:137), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits).
- The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:34), which re-reads the client ids after the load.

Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:202): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:143) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too.

derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:327) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:294). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe.

- `nerva doctor`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:702):

Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:379). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://[::1]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:297), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:337). The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, *_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's *_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:570).
  - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:816). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:588); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters.

An unknown stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection; a stored row that is not JSON (the posture included) no longer reads as off: the whole store is validated when it is first opened and before every full listing (_require_readable_store, agents/core/settings_db.py:553), and the listing raises SettingsUnreadable instead (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:739). `nerva config list` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:956).

Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment.

Known limits:
- On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled.
- A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound.
- In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once.
- JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split.
- The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why.
- A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1).
- A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together.
- A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked.
- A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py.
- Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value.
- A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token.
- The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines).
- The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it.
- Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it.
- The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today.
- JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before.

The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour:
- Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO.
- The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used.
- PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch.

- A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once.
- It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?".
- files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read.

provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running.

The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed.
- The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:106), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:73): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:490), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:72; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:110; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183).
- agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect.
- PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:83), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry.
- Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off.

Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:526) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment.
- What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:100).
- JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72).
- Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:93): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies.

The lists are measured, not declared:
- A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there.
- A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:667).

The two false read-again entries are fixed:
- The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:293; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:419). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:109): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:137), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits).
- The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:36), which re-reads the client ids after the load.

Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:202): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:143) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too.

derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:327) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:294). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe.

Surfaces:
- GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:564) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included.
- `nerva doctor`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:702):
  - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:379). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://[::1]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:297), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:337). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost., ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:353). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:395). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why.
  - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, *_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's *_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:570).
  - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:816). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:588); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters.
  - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why.
  - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash.
- The `nerva` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:116) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only. Its loopback rule is the doctor's, pinned equal over one table of spellings. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:156), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:795; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4).
- The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:701). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection; a stored row that is not JSON (the posture included) no longer reads as off: the whole store is validated when it is first opened and before every full listing (_require_readable_store, agents/core/settings_db.py:553), and the listing raises SettingsUnreadable instead (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:739). `nerva config list` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:966).
- The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:261).

Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment.

Known limits:
- On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled.
- A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound.
- In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once.
- JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split.
- The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why.
- A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1).
- A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together.
- A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked.
- A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py.
- Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value.
- A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token.
- The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines).
- The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it.
- Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it.
- The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today.
- JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before.

The hub can boot in safe mode, with every owner customization left out and no gate relaxed. JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1, or `python serve.py --safe-mode`, which sets it before the hub is imported (apply_safe_mode_switch, serve.py:18), is the one flag, read at call time by one module (enabled, agents/core/safe_mode.py:140). The runtime (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py, which passes it to scripts/coordinator.py) takes --safe-mode too, since it runs heartbeats, owner jobs and agents on the same data root; deploy/systemd/README.md says to set JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1 in the env file both units read and restart both. It leaves out the owner's layers (15 since H490, H594, H613 and H464c, whose `company_mode` layer leaves the company-mode sweep out; LAYERS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:63). Skills: discovery does not open the data home's skills folder (agents/core/skills/loader.py:647), and any skill in the bundled tree that is not a shipped one (generated, imported, edited or pending review, by the loader's own external classification) is not loaded (agents/core/skills/loader.py:722); every shipped skill still is. Approving a pending skill in safe mode signs it but says it loads on the next normal boot (loaded: false; agents/core/routers/skills.py:753). MCP: the saved servers are not registered (agents/web.py:1958; mcp_servers is reported only for a non-empty saved list) and their saved configuration is not touched: _save_mcp_config never rewrites it from the empty manager (agents/web.py:1929), and adding or removing a server answers 409 `safe_mode` before anything changes (_safe_mode_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:174). Acquired packages and extensions: the acquisition runtime reports itself disabled (agents/core/acquisition/runtime.py:44), and names acquired packages as left out only when acquisition was switched on, so nothing promoted is re-registered and extensions() returns None, which the activate route answers as unavailable. Plugin grants: JARVIS_PLUGIN_GRANTS, which only ever widens access under least privilege, is ignored (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:670). Persona and contract overlays: soul_path_for (agents/core/agent.py:389) and identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolve through _pick_overlay (agents/core/agent.py:375), which in safe mode returns the shipped SOUL.md or IDENTITY.md and never a SOUL.local.md or IDENTITY.local.md from the data home or the repository; construction and the H672 compaction-boundary refresh both resolve through it, so a safe-mode session cannot pick an overlay up mid-conversation. An overlay that cannot even be probed (an unreadable souls folder) counts as left out rather than stopping the boot (present, agents/core/safe_mode.py:157), for personas and heartbeats alike. Owner jobs stay saved and are not put on the scheduler, neither at boot (agents/core/scheduler_service.py:64) nor by a later create, /remind, edit, resume or first run: JobRunner._held (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1420) keeps register and register_manual off the scheduler, and a queued request waits for a normal boot. A manual tick is refused, run now answers 409 safe_mode (agents/core/routers/jobs.py:356), and the create confirmation says the job fires after a normal boot. Group gating (require-mention, chat allowlist, observe mode) exists as GroupPolicy (agents/core/channels/group_policy.py:43-60) but reads only TELEGRAM_* settings and is consumed only by the Telegram adapter (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1053). reviews.remaining:

reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (9f92d937): Nerva reaches the owner on Telegram (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:236), Discord (agents/core/channels/discord.py:47), Slack (agents/core/channels/slack.py:101), email (agents/core/channels/email.py:35) and ntfy (agents/core/channels/ntfy.py:139), plus a webhook family for WhatsApp, Signal, Matrix, Teams and Google Chat (agents/core/channels/webhook_channels.py:127, :158, :183, :214, :239) wired at boot from JARVIS_WEBHOOK_CHANNELS (agents/web.py:648). reviews.remaining:

reviews.remaining:

reviews.summary:
The owner declares which skills, plugins and MCP servers load at boot, and a plugin toggle survives a restart. Six declared settings rows (agents/core/settings_db.py:447-452), category `loadset`, hold comma lists: skills_disabled/skills_only, plugins_disabled/plugins_only, mcp_disabled/mcp_only, editable from the settings page and `nerva config set` (which says a loadset.* key or a plugin switch applies at the next start). A disabled name does not load; a non-empty only-list loads only what it names; the disabled list wins (permits, agents/core/load_set.py:96). A list is read at call time (declared, agents/core/load_set.py:74), trimmed, de-duplicated and bounded to 256 names of at most 128 characters without control characters (parse_names, agents/core/load_set.py:43), and an unreadable store narrows nothing. For plugins the settings page's existing per-plugin `plugins.<id>` switches, which nothing used to read, count too: an explicit off is off (agents/core/load_set.py:84). SkillLoader.discover reads the lists once per pass (agents/core/skills/loader.py:654-655) and a skill named by its registry name or its folder is not registered at all, before any quarantine row (agents/core/skills/loader.py:733); a registration from an earlier pass is taken out when a later pass denies it, the per-pass snapshot is cleared in a finally, and in safe mode (the owner folder unread) no declared name is reported as unknown. PermissionGate switches off the plugins the lists name when it is built (apply_load_set, agents/core/plugin_gate.py:704), and PluginManager.build drops them from orch.plugins before binding oracle_bridge and Argus (_drop_switched_off, agents/core/plugin_manager.py:198), so the probes, the dashboard and WorldView never reach a switched-off plugin. Each gate holds its own copies of the built-in manifests (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:698), so switching one off never reaches the module table or another gate, and the readers of a plugin's enabled state ask the live gate: CloudImageRuntime is wired with orch.permission_gate (_available, agents/core/cloud_image_runtime.py:542) and the capability board reads the gate's manifests (_plugin_records, agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:127). The plugin toggle (toggle_plugin, agents/core/routers/plugins.py:99) keeps the choice in one place, the plugin's plugins.<id> settings switch when it has one and otherwise plugins_disabled; switched on, it leaves plugins_disabled and joins a declared plugins_only (persist_plugin, agents/core/load_set.py:140). It reads the lists fail-closed (read_setting), so an unreadable store is not overwritten, and answers `persisted` (false when the store refused or could not be read, the live toggle standing). It writes a SETTINGS_CHANGE audit row naming the keys, and a re-enable that cannot be audited is switched back off and answers 503 audit_failed. The MCP load registers only the permitted saved servers (agents/web.py:1967-1974); a switched-off one is held (_MCP_HELD, agents/web.py:1944) and written back unchanged by every save, so the saved configuration never loses it, and adding a server of that name or removing it answers 409 `switched_off` naming the list (_held_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:159). The lists only narrow: nothing is installed, approved, registered or written to the approval store, and a declared name that matches nothing installed is reported as unknown (finish, agents/core/load_set.py:121). The status rows carry it: /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:76), /plugins (agents/core/routers/plugins.py:88) and /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:132) return `load_set` with the declared lists, what was switched off and what is unknown (status, agents/core/load_set.py:132). Safe mode (H275) applies first; the load set narrows further. tests/test_h285_load_set.py (49 cases, plus one in tests/test_cloud_image.py) covers the parsing and its bounds, the six declared rows, the permit table, an unreadable store, a disabled skill and an only-list with their status rows and unknown names, a skill named by its folder, a named-but-absent skill installing or approving nothing (asserted on a private approval store), the skills route, MCP servers switched off and still saved, an MCP only-list, the add and remove refusals for a held server, adding and removing other servers keeping the held one, the MCP list route, the gate's disabled and only lists, the settings-page switch and that only an explicit off counts, that the lists never enable or register, the toggle kept across a restart both ways, a plugin without a settings switch, enabling under an only-list, a toggle the store refuses, and the plugins route. 33 mutants over the parser, the permit table, the persistence, the three loaders, the refusals and the status rows: all caught (two after their cases were added: an explicit off, a refused write). Test manual: ENV-169, ENV-170. Adapted from Hermes: the lists live in the settings store Nerva already persists and edits rather than a YAML file, the plugin toggle writes them, and an MCP server switched off is kept in the saved list rather than dropped. reviews.remaining:
Three cron-lane clauses of Hermes' contract are unmet. The Kanban claim-lease and crash-grace asks are done.

1. HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT: the plain cron path has no per-run wall clock. `JobRunner._fire_once` → `_execute` → `_ask`/`_brief`/`_deliver` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1735-1804, 1846-1872, 1874-1968, 2052-2080) has no `asyncio.wait_for` at any level. In particular, `_send_tracked`/`_send` (jobs.py:2082-2115) awaits the channel adapter bare. A hung Telegram/Discord send therefore holds the job's gate stripe (jobs_dispatch.py:44-59) and its APScheduler `max_instances=1` slot, and nothing breaks it. The script path already does this correctly: `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._ask(...), 120)` at agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:461 and `asyncio.wait_for(self.runner._send_tracked(...), 30)` at :513. The fix is to apply the same bound to the cron path, ideally as a `jobs.run_timeout_seconds` setting next to the existing `jobs.media_send_timeout_seconds`. The overrun should be recorded as a normal failed run through `_failed`, so the 3-strike pause and the incident path still apply.

2. `JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS` defaults to 0, which means unbounded (agents/core/autonomy/executor.py:57-60, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2014-2018). Out of the box, a hung in-process queued task is bounded only by the 3600 s stuck-running reaper. Fix: give it a non-zero shipped default, or promote it to a validated `autonomy.*` setting like `running_ttl_seconds`, and add a test asserting the default is finite.

3. HERMES_CRON_SESSION_DB_TIMEOUT: the jobs store opens sqlite with neither `timeout=` nor `PRAGMA busy_timeout` (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:767-770). The task queue sets `timeout=30.0` + `PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000` (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:402-404). jobs.db writers therefore fall back to SQLite's 5 s default, on a WAL shared by the gateway drain loop and cron firings. One-line parity fix.

Out of scope, not gaps: the row's own rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs (_AUTO_DELIVER_PLATFORM / _CHAT_ID / _THREAD_ID, TELEGRAM_CRON_THREAD_ID). The residual ~14-knob multi-agent Kanban board (_BOARD / _WORKSPACES_ROOT / _ATTACHMENTS_ROOT / _GOAL_MODE / _DISPATCH_IN_GATEWAY) is a product decision about whether Nerva grows a shared task board, not a slice of this row.

reviews.summary:
file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. It can also open an exact spill-file path through a read-only door when the owner's roots exclude the spill directory, and tool_result_store pins file_read to an infinite spill threshold, so reading a spill never spills again. file_search is a bounded literal content search with case_sensitive, whole_word and a file-name glob filter; it never follows symlinks, prunes secret names and reports which cap stopped it. Local 2026-10-09 parser-backed file_read admission refuses an observed on-disk PDF/DOCX size above 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB) as document_too_large before parser discovery or extraction. Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds.

Independent #1233 review (historical scope): file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It can also open an exact spill-file path through a read-only door when the owner's roots exclude the spill directory, and tool_result_store pins file_read to an infinite spill threshold, so reading a spill never spills again. file_search is a bounded literal content search with case_sensitive, whole_word and a file-name glob filter; it never follows symlinks, prunes secret names and reports which cap stopped it.

reviews.summary:
K1, K2 și K3 sunt livrate: execute_code înregistrat pentru model, celule într-un interpreter rezident pe sesiune (K2, `llm.execute_code_sessions`, implicit pornit după opt-in-ul execute_code când backend-ul izolat e configurat; o dezactivare explicită e păstrată) și controale de operator peste el. Spill-ul stdout/stderr într-un fișier funcționează pe ambele căi. `_open_stream_spills` (agents/core/code_tools.py:643) deschide scriitorii în flux înainte de rulare. Pe K1, sinks trec prin `ToolRPCSandboxRuntime.run_python` (code_tools.py:606) până la `Sandbox.execute_python`. Pe K2, worker-ul trimite ieșirea celulei în cadre de cel mult 4096 de caractere (agents/core/session_kernels.py:387-388), iar `_Capture` dă fiecare cadru scriitorului (session_kernels.py:736). Gazda vede deci tot fluxul, iar memoria ei rămâne mărginită: păstrează doar capul și coada. Un flux care a încăput nu lasă fișier; rezultatul unui spill poartă calea, referința, dimensiunea și sha256. Lotul HEQ 1 (H661) a făcut din notiță apelul exact. `_spill_notice` (code_tools.py:211) scrie `file_read(path=…, offset=0, max_bytes=…)`, construit de `page_recipe` (agents/core/tool_result_store.py:145), și cere paginarea prin next_offset. `stdout_read_with` (code_tools.py:292) apare doar când turei i s-a oferit file_read și sonda `_spill_readable` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1532) confirmă că poate deschide acel fișier; altfel notița spune că fișierul e păstrat pentru owner și nu poate fi paginat din tura asta. file_read primește directorul de spill ca ușă read-only (autonomy_coordinator.py:1487). Un spill în flux are acum un plafon: DEFAULT_MAX_STREAM_BYTES, 5 MB (tool_result_store.py:130, cifra lui Hermes). Peste el fișierul ține primii 5 MB și se termină într-un marcaj explicit (coada fluxului rămâne doar inline), iar rezultatul poartă `stdout_spill_capped`, `stdout_kept_bytes` și `stdout_file_bytes` (code_tools.py:294-296). tests/test_code_tools.py paginează înapoi tot fluxul pe ambele căi (tests/test_code_tools.py:829) și verifică plafonul (tests/test_code_tools.py:882).

reviews.summary:
The model can decide to say one short text aloud on one room's device, and can do it again. register_speak_tool (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:684) adds a ToolRPC `speak` tool with gated=True, trusted execution and its own gated intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:711, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:717). It is registered only while JARVIS_MEDIA_DIRECTOR is on (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:697), and AutonomyCoordinator wires it with the broker kernel and the governed enqueue (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:922, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2201). It reaches the same Media Director instance the media routes use, so the owner's device registry and session board apply (agents/core/routers/media_director.py:272). SpeakTool.preflight (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:388) runs at proposal and again before the approved run. It refuses text over the spoken-reply cap and code-only text (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:394, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:396). It resolves a room to that room's one announce-capable default device, so the card title and the persisted args name the speaker (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:268, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:467). It raises no card the run could only refuse: unified API off, kernel off or unbound, no media root, no speech backend, no driver for the device, or no configured presence room each refuse by name (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:415, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:410). SpeakTool.intake (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:445) shows the kernel the exact toolrpc.speak row it enqueues. Under the production composition (worker.kernel_gate over MediationKernelBridge, agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:681, agents/core/kernel/binding.py:132) that decision binds as the row's intake evidence, and a DENY raises no card (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:471). Only the human-accepted durable toolrpc.speak row runs. The kind is trusted (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:69) and the executor routes it to the trusted rail (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2222-2225). ToolRPC re-runs the preflight and requires the trusted execution context (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:678, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:706), and the handler refuses a row of any other kind (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:541). SpeakTool.execute (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:536) synthesizes the clip through SpokenReply on the host TTSEngine in the owner's configured voice (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:552, agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:265, agents/core/voice/tts.py:216). It writes the clip owner-only under the first media root (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:639, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:653) and presents it only through CapabilityActionAPI.perform('action:media.present') in announce mode (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:592, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:597). The facade asks the Action Kernel before the handler runs (agents/core/capability_actions.py:176) and refuses on a DENY (agents/core/capability_actions.py:183), so the kernel authorizes the effect and the tool never reaches a driver. A kernel QUEUE on that present is honoured as the accepted row and audited as speak.durably_approved (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:500, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:522). A DENY becomes kernel_denied with the kernel's reason (agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:614). The Media Director treats an announce as a one-shot notice (agents/core/media_director.py:738): it never blocks the next present and costs no interrupt budget (agents/core/media_director.py:890), and whatever it cut into stays the restore point (agents/core/media_director.py:992). Because the tool is gated, tool_profiles offers it only to the owner on the operator surface (agents/core/tool_profiles.py:190, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:194), and the snapshot pins this (tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json:64, tests/test_tool_profiles.py:202). Tests cover: registration and postures (tests/test_speak_tool.py:170, tests/test_speak_tool.py:196); named preflight refusals that enqueue nothing (tests/test_speak_tool.py:271, tests/test_speak_tool.py:320); and the card naming the device (tests/test_speak_tool.py:286). With the real kernel.authorize, AutonomyPolicy and KillSwitch behind worker.kernel_gate, an approved speak is mediated and audited, and an engaged kill switch refuses both the run and the card (tests/test_speak_tool.py:520, tests/test_speak_tool.py:543, tests/test_speak_tool.py:576). Three back-to-back normal speaks on one device all play at no budget cost (tests/test_speak_tool.py:591). Speaking over music needs high urgency, pays once and keeps the music as the restore point (tests/test_speak_tool.py:608, tests/test_media_director.py:762). A kernel DENY, a missing TTS backend, a missing media root and a driverless device each refuse by name with no playback, and an engine that yields no audio refuses as tts_failed with nothing presented (tests/test_speak_tool.py:681, tests/test_speak_tool.py:469, tests/test_speak_tool.py:666, tests/test_speak_tool.py:703, tests/test_speak_tool.py:716). A row of another kind cannot speak (tests/test_speak_tool.py:753), and the clip spool stays bounded (tests/test_speak_tool.py:779). Known limits outside the accepted adaptation: an accepted speak runs at the next autonomy tick (default 60 s, floor 15 s, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:566), like every gated tool. A presence:auto card names the sentinel, because only play time knows whether the owner is in the presence room. Audible output needs an owner-wired speaker driver (the in-repo NullMediaDriver refuses and LocalFileMediaDriver is a reference), the same host seam as every media.present. The speech-backend gate (tts_installed, agents/core/voice/speak_tool.py:191) needs edge-tts, Kokoro, Piper with a model or the approved TTS command, with edge-tts and the command left out under voice.local_only, like the spoken-reply channel; a named TTS provider alone does not pass it. An announce of any length, including one sent through POST /api/media/present, no longer holds its device, as docs/FLAGS.md states.
