The model now writes its own long-term memory during a turn, through a tool that is atomic, guarded, recorded and undoable. `memory` (register_memory_tool, agents/core/memory_tool.py:413; registered ungated at agents/core/memory_tool.py:519 and wired from the autonomy coordinator's H314 block, whose `_living_memory` getter and `register_memory_tool(` call tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py:544-546 reads back from the coordinator's source) takes `operations`, each an add, a replace of the one fact `old_text` matches, or a remove of it, against target `memory` (the LivingMemory `core` ring of agent notes) or `user` (the `user_core` profile ring) (TARGETS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:61); a call with no operations reads both. The rings are reached only when cognition memory is on: the coordinator's `_living_memory` getter hands the tool the LivingMemory only when `cog.sub_enabled("memory_enabled")` holds (pinned by content at tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py:544-546), and a getter that yields nothing — memory off, safe mode, or a getter that fails (agents/core/memory_tool.py:429-441) — is refused `memory_disabled` (agents/core/memory_tool.py:469-471). Both rings come from one LivingMemory, so the enabled set is both or none: when memory is off the tool's offer says so through the H296 schema hook (OFF_DESCRIPTION, agents/core/memory_tool.py:459-460) and every call is refused `memory_disabled`, rather than the target enum being narrowed to an empty list. Every operation is checked on a working copy before anything is written (plan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:156): one line of at most 300 characters, the core block's own cut (MAX_FACT_CHARS, agents/core/memory_tool.py:63), with no control, format, private-use, surrogate or other invisible character (the quarantine.strip_format_chars set: variation selectors, Hangul fillers, U+034F, U+2800) (_clean_text, agents/core/memory_tool.py:112), scanned with the normalised injection scanner (_scan, agents/core/memory_tool.py:135), an old_text that matches exactly one fact, compared against the whitespace-normalised fact as the prompt shows it (_match, agents/core/memory_tool.py:144), no duplicate, and a full ring refusing an add instead of silently dropping its oldest fact; one refusal changes nothing. The rings are then written by a new compare-and-set (CoreMemory.compare_and_set, agents/core/cognition/memory.py:314) under the lock a forget clears them with, so a forget or another write that ran in between wins and nothing forgotten is written back; a second ring that fails puts the first back (_commit, agents/core/memory_tool.py:320). A compare-and-set that lost is refused `memory_changed_meanwhile`; a ring that cannot be saved is refused `memory_write_failed`. Only a clean owner turn at the operator surface writes: the resolver offers the tool to operator/owner alone, whatever llm.guest_tools says (OWNER_OPERATOR_TOOLS, agents/core/tool_profiles.py:102 and :243), the handler refuses any other posture (agents/core/memory_tool.py:449) and a turn whose origin is untrusted, an inbound message, web content or a flagged recall (agents/core/memory_tool.py:452), so an injected instruction cannot make itself permanent. Every write is committed and then recorded as an intent-log `memory.write` entry carrying the actor, the undo ref, the targets and per operation its target and action — never the text nor a hash of it, since an unsalted hash of a short fact is guessed back and the intent log survives a forget (agents/core/memory_tool.py:497). A record that cannot be made puts the rings back and records the put-back as `memory.write_reverted` (undo: `memory.undo_reverted`) with the same ref, naming exactly the rings it restored, because the intent log keeps a record whose save failed and writes it with its next one; a put-back that cannot be made (a ring moved again) is logged as an error and not recorded as one (_revert, agents/core/memory_tool.py:344; _record_put_back, agents/core/memory_tool.py:307). With no intent log nothing is written (_record, agents/core/memory_tool.py:299). The rings' previous contents are kept under the ref in a bounded undo store beside the rings (UndoStore, agents/core/memory_tool.py:228), which a forget deletes with them and which POST /api/admin/forget empties together with the live rings (clear_live_memory, agents/core/data_purge.py:429), so an undo during a forget cannot write the facts back. undo (agents/core/memory_tool.py:363) restores a write while the rings still hold what it wrote, by the same compare-and-set, recorded as `memory.undo`. The owner reads the rings and the writes undo would still restore — only those whose rings hold what they wrote (UndoStore.recent, agents/core/memory_tool.py:263) — at GET /api/memory/core (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:872) and undoes one at POST /api/memory/core/undo, admin-only (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:886). The Console's Long-Term Memory panel shows both rings and the recent writes with an undo each, and says when an undo is refused (LongTermMemoryPanel, frontend/src/panels/long-term-memory.tsx). A write that changes a ring leaves a `memory_updated` trail row with the changed targets and the actions, never text; a call that changes nothing leaves none (_record_event, agents/core/memory_tool.py:394). The prompt's core block stays frozen per session, so a write reaches the system prompt at the next session and the tool answers with both rings as they now are. tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py (72 cases) covers the plan and every refusal (malformed, injected, invisible-character, ambiguous, duplicate or over-full operations), the compare-and-set and a ring that cannot be saved, an owner write of both rings with its record and its undo, a read, an add already saved, the five postures and untrusted origins, a failing getter, memory switched off and its offer, a broken memory module, an unknown argument, no intent log or one without a record method, a record that fails and its recorded put-back, an undo whose put-back also fails claiming none, a forget between the read and the write, a forget that empties the undo store, a second ring that fails, a full ring, undo after the ring moved, undo of a replace and a remove, undo without memory, an undo that cannot be recorded, the undo store's bound and its listing of only restorable writes, the trail row, the profile offer and the routes; frontend/src/test/long-term-memory-panel.test.tsx pins the panel. 47 mutants: 33 at the build (32 caught, four after their cases were added: a raw over-long padded fact, an audit sink without record, an empty operation list, the undo listing's limit; one equivalent, rewriting a ring the call did not change) and 14 in the review round (13 caught, one after its case was added: an undo whose put-back also fails; one equivalent, widening _moved to rings it is never given). Test manual: MEM-204, MEM-205. Adapted from Hermes: its memory tool's add/replace/remove on the two injected stores, with the writes restricted to the owner's clean turns, committed by compare-and-set, recorded in Nerva's intent log without their text and undoable by the owner.

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207, with H340 in the same change (critic note 21: one skill_view), and fixed after seven adversarial reviews. The first (review-H318: two majors, six minors, nine nits) found an unkeyed signature counted as a vouch and approved changes that never landed. The second (review-H318b: two majors, seven minors, seven nits) found that an approved change disabled the skill it improved (a bundled skill unbundled, a signed or approved one losing its standing) and that the owner still approved without seeing the change. The third (review-H318c: one records major, eight minors, seven nits) found a write between the standing read and the renewal could ride into the vouch, a renewal failure reported as applied, a keyed signature overwritten while its key was missing, a publish that silently dropped a linked file, and cards that could be lost or left pending. The fourth (review-H318d: one major, five minors, six nits) found that text-mode SKILL.md writes made every vouched apply fail on Windows, a partial renewal left a new signature over the old text, publish still followed a link planted after its check, and cards beyond the route's page were called inert. The fifth (review-H318e: two minors, seven nits) found the old SKILL.sig read after the write with no rollback behind it, text-mode test fixtures on the Windows lane, a signature that could not be put back reported as the old text staying, a truncated write, the review superseding by the record's origin, a /v1 card approvable without its diff, and publish describing another read of SKILL.md. The sixth (review-H318f: one minor, four nits) found the whole-file write staging its temporary file inside the skill, where one a crash left would void the signature. The seventh (review-H318g: two minors, five nits) found a standing that could not be read for a moment read as unsigned, and the crash-safety claim wider than the code. All are fixed or stated below; two nits are stated by decision below. Hermes gives the agent skills_list, skill_view (a skill's SKILL.md or one of its linked files) and skill_manage (create, patch and delete). Nerva now offers all three powers under its governance: the two reads as ungated read-only ToolRPC tools, and authoring as a proposal the owner approves.

The three tools are in agents/core/skills/tools.py; register_skill_tools (agents/core/skills/tools.py:192) registers them on the orchestrator's ToolRPC server in AutonomyCoordinator, next to the todo and memory tools; tests/test_h318_skill_tools.py:400 drives all three through the live hub's own server.

The trust gate:
- SkillLoader.catalog_gate (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1365) is the prompt catalog's gate, factored out and now shared by the catalog, skills_list and skill_view.
- It says why a skill is not shown: sandboxed (quarantined included), untrusted (a signature that does not verify here), or declared for other agents. prompt_catalog applies it unchanged, and its suite passes as before.

skills_list {query?, offset?, limit?}:
- It returns name, a one-line description and the command names for every skill the gate passes for the calling agent (agents/core/skills/tools.py:267).
- A row whose text is injection-flagged is left out, as the catalog leaves it out. The query matches name or description, case-insensitively. Pages hold at most 50 rows, with total and next_offset.
- Unknown fields and malformed paging are refused by name.

skill_view {name, file?} (agents/core/skills/tools.py:307):
- It returns the SKILL.md body (frontmatter removed; the heading dialect whole) with its template variables rendered (H340), plus the list of the skill's other files, at most 3 KiB of names as the answer carries them (escapes counted) with files_more counting the rest; a file or body is served up to 64 KiB on disk, as always, and refused only when its escapes pass 128 KiB (MAX_ENCODED_BYTES), and the description is cut to 2 KiB escaped (agents/core/skills/tools.py:87-96). With file, it returns one of those files, listed or not.
- It serves the bytes the trust checks ran on at load, kept as Skill.view_files (agents/core/skills/loader.py:334): each file up to 64 KiB as bytes, at most 1 MiB of a skill, any other file only as its size (listed, refused by name). An edit on disk after the signature check is not what the model reads, and a skill's assets are not held for the process's life. Signing a skill loads it again, so the view follows the signed bytes.
- A path can only name a file of that snapshot. It must be relative, with no '..', leading '/' or backslash, and it is normalised (agents/core/skills/tools.py:182). The snapshot refuses links when it is taken.
- Only text is served (a NUL or bad UTF-8 is refused, a BOM dropped), at most 64 KiB (MAX_FILE_BYTES, counted in bytes) after the template variables render and 128 KiB once escaped. The tool declares the escaped ceiling, the file list's and the description's bounds and 4 KiB of envelope as its own result budget.
- An unknown skill and one this agent is not shown answer alike (skill_unknown).
- The answer is tainted, and carries a warning sentence saying why next to the content, in two cases (agents/core/skills/tools.py:250):
  - the body or the description is injection-flagged;
  - the skill comes from outside the product and the owner has not vouched for it.
- Skill.owner_vouched (agents/core/skills/loader.py:791) is true for a bundled skill, or for an outside one with a keyed signature or the owner's approval of these exact bytes. That is the same rule that decides whether its code may load in-process.
- An unkeyed SKILL.sig is a sha256 anyone can compute. It verifies as integrity-only, but it is no vouch, so a self-signed import stays data (review-H318 M-1, SEC-B2).
- The loop fences a tainted answer as DATA and raises the turn's taint.
- A body view that succeeds for the owner's own turn also declares the skill's required_env names to the code-environment registry for that actor and session, with a validator the registry re-runs before the names are honoured (the same loader, skill, vouch, snapshot and gate), and a tainted view revokes them; a declaration that fails never fails the view (agents/core/skills/tools.py:392, agents/core/code_env.py:161, agents/core/code_env.py:222).

skill_propose (agents/core/skills/tools.py:423):
- {name, content} proposes a new SKILL.md for an existing skill that this agent is shown. It becomes a pending SkillProposalStore proposal with origin agent:<agent>, plus one skill.patch_proposal approval card bound to it in the ledger (queue_card, agents/core/skills/proposals.py:213). The background review and /refine queue theirs the same way.
- A bundled skill is refused (skill_propose_bundled): it is product source, and an edit would unbundle it and, with its code, stop it loading. A change that would rename the skill is refused (skill_propose_rename).
- What the owner reviews comes from the ledger, never from the card. GET /api/skills/proposals (admin, agents/core/routers/skills.py:766) serves the pending proposals, a page of 20 with more counting the rest, each with its whole diff against the live SKILL.md, whether the skill drifted since, and flags for a rename or a bundled skill (describe, agents/core/skills/proposals.py:272); a proposal from before cards were bound, or whose card is gone from the queue, gets its card there, every pending proposal's, not only the page's, and the answer names every pending proposal's card (cards). The /v1 console's panel holds every skill-change card it has no diff for (one beyond the page, or one no proposal names) with Approve disabled, offering Reject (review-H318e n-4), re-reads the action list once the proposals answer, and says the change is loading, or that it could not be read, and holds Approve until it knows; a change the hub will refuse (a bundled skill, a rename) offers reject only in both consoles. The HUD's Decision Inbox shows these under SKILL CHANGES, whole, with approve and reject on the proposal's own card (frontend/src/panels/skill-changes.tsx), and the /v1 console's action panel shows the same diff under a skill-change card.
- Only the proposal's own card decides it (agents/core/skills/curator.py:217): a card anyone with a user token queued naming a proposal id changes nothing, and the decide route says so.
- Re-sending the same text, from any origin, makes no second proposal and no second card; a card that failed to queue is queued by the retry. A newer proposal from the same origin (the caller's own, even when the text re-sent was another origin's) for the same skill supersedes its older pending one (marked superseded, its card withdrawn), whether the tool, the background review or /refine proposed it (each passes its own origin, review-H318e n-2); binding a card withdraws the unbound cards naming the proposal, and a proposal superseded while its card was queued gets that card withdrawn, and a process takes at most 10 proposals a day, new skills included (skill_propose_limit).
- The owner's decision applies it at once: POST /api/actions/{id}/decide on the proposal's card runs SkillCurator.apply_decisions (agents/core/routers/actions.py:147, agents/core/skills/curator.py:154), one pass at a time, the nightly pass included, not gated by the learning loop's flag or the night window. The apply is hash-checked against drift and backed up under the skill's directory name with a unique suffix.
- The applied bytes keep the skill's standing (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1297, agents/core/skills/loader.py:1328): judged on one snapshot of the tree read before the write; after the write, the tree must be that snapshot with only SKILL.md replaced by the approved text, and the SKILL.sig that verified or the owner's approval is renewed over exactly those checked bytes, never a later read. SKILL.md is read and written as bytes, never in text mode, so the line ends on disk are the ones checked, on Windows too, and written whole: staged beside the skill's folder where it can be (a file a crash leaves inside the folder counts as a member and fails the signature closed; where beside it cannot be, another filesystem or a root the hub cannot write, the folder itself is used: review-H318g n-1), created with the old file's mode, flushed to disk and renamed over it, so a write cut short leaves the old text (review-H318e n-3, review-H318f m-1). The old SKILL.sig is read with SKILL.md, before anything is written (review-H318e m-1); a read of it that fails changes nothing and is tried again at the next decision (unreadable_signature, review-H318f n-1), and so does a standing that could not be read for a moment, which no longer reads as unsigned (review-H318g m-1); a signature that stays unreadable is warned about once per proposal. The apply is not crash-proof: a crash between the rename and the renewal leaves the skill sandboxed (untrusted, never trusted) and the next decision reports it as drifted, and on Windows a SKILL.md another process holds open cannot be replaced, so the change is retried as write_failed. Otherwise, or if the renewal fails, the old SKILL.md and the old SKILL.sig are put back byte for byte, where the old signature and approval still hold, the outcome says changed_during_apply or standing_not_renewed (rollback_failed, with the backup, if the old text could not be put back; signature_not_restored if the old text is back but its SKILL.sig could not be, which leaves the skill untrusted until it is signed again; when the old text could not be put back, its signature is not either, so what was renewed is not undone over the text that stays), and the proposal is marked stale with that reason rather than retried every pass. A standing that cannot be read (a SKILL.sig that is not UTF-8) reads as unsigned, and one proposal that fails never stops the pass. A keyed SKILL.sig whose key is not configured is not overwritten: the change waits (signing_key_missing). A shipped skill is known by its load or by where it lives (a shipped name directly under the product's skills tree), so one whose bytes drifted is still refused, by the tool, the background review and the apply. A skill nothing vouched for gains no vouch, a signature that no longer verifies is not renewed, and code changed on disk since the approval does not ride the patch. The answer reports each outcome with the state the skill is left in (shown, sandboxed, untrusted, hidden) or why it was not applied (bundled_skill, renames_skill, drifted_since_proposal, write_failed). A write that failed stays approved and is retried at the next decision, leaving no backup behind for the attempt. Publishing builds the package from one snapshot of the source, the bytes it read, and its registry row describes that snapshot's SKILL.md (review-H318e n-5): a skill whose folder is a link, a member that is a link or not a regular file, or a file that changed while read is refused (422, skill_source_refused: a link, a special file, or a file that could not be read stably), and a link planted after the check is never followed.
- {description, steps} asks for a new skill, which SkillLoader.generate_skill writes into CDX-8 quarantine (PENDING_REVIEW, never executed until the owner approves).
- Nothing writes a live SKILL.md: the live file is byte-identical after a proposal.
- Only an owner's turn that has read nothing untrusted may propose. A guest, a household member, a job, an inbound channel or a turn that read a web page (the action origin a read raises) is refused by name, and so is a turn whose origin cannot be read. Injection-flagged text is refused, as are mixed or malformed arguments.

Differences from Hermes, by decision:
- Authoring is a proposal, never a write. Deleting a skill and adding supporting files stay owner actions.
- skill_propose is offered wherever an ungated tool is, and refuses every turn that is not the owner's clean one; it is not withheld from the offer (a nit both reviews left).
- The daily limit is per process and follows local time: a restart resets it.
- Publishing a skill to the marketplace signs a staged copy, never the owner's tree, so sharing a skill is not vouching for it (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:391).
- All three tools are ungated, so an inbound guest is offered them only when the owner names them in llm.guest_tools (critic note 22). tests/_snapshots/tool_profiles.json is regenerated.

reviews.summary:
The SKILL.md frontmatter contract Hermes parses (agent/skill_utils.parse_frontmatter and tools/skills_tool_plugin.py) now lives in one shared module, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py, used by both the loader and the importer.

Parsing. split_frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:47):
- drops a leading UTF-8 BOM before the fence check (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:56);
- takes the closing fence at column 0 only, as Hermes' `\n---\s*\n` does, so an indented `---` inside a block scalar is content (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:63);
- falls back to key: value lines for a block that is not valid YAML (_naive_key_values, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:83), instead of demoting the file to the heading dialect.

The fallback is stricter than Hermes' line split:
- only column-0 keys count, so a nested `name:` cannot replace the skill's own;
- a value wrapped in matching quotes loses them;
- a fallback that finds neither a name nor a description counts as no frontmatter (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:77), so a heading-dialect file framed by fences keeps its heading parse.

Identity decisions pass lenient=False (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:72), so a name only the fallback can find never decides one: the Hermes pin gate (agents/core/skills/importer.py:271) and the migration and rescan slugs (agents/core/skills/importer.py:1192, agents/core/skills/importer.py:1376).

SkillLoader._parse_manifest decodes with utf-8-sig on both the snapshot and the path read (agents/core/skills/loader.py:857, agents/core/skills/loader.py:859). A manifest the normaliser cannot read registers under the directory name instead of failing (agents/core/skills/loader.py:874).

The manifest:
- The name is capped at 64 characters and stripped after the cut (agents/core/skills/loader.py:893; the caps are at agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:28-29).
- The description is capped at 1024 characters with an ellipsis, quotes kept (cap_description, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:351). When none is declared, it is the first non-heading body line, as Hermes' listing reads it (agents/core/skills/loader.py:895-896).
- A list-valued author or license is joined (agents/core/skills/loader.py:898).
- agents and requires read a YAML list, `[a, b]` or `a, b` as plain strings (agents/core/skills/loader.py:885-886).
- Command entries are reduced to JSON types (agents/core/skills/loader.py:970).

contract_fields (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:359), merged into every frontmatter manifest (agents/core/skills/loader.py:905), keeps the keys Hermes recognises:
- homepage and compatibility;
- platforms, read as Hermes matches them (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:204): a list, or one string as one name. Each name maps through PLATFORM_MAP and matches the OS whose sys.platform starts with it, so darwin and win count and osx and win64 do not. An unmatched name is kept, so a gate refuses it everywhere, as Hermes hides it;
- environments and requires_apps, where a string is one item (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:224, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:234);
- triggers and dependencies;
- tags and related_skills, where a declared metadata.hermes value wins over the top-level key (skill_view's `hermes_meta.get(k) or frontmatter.get(k)`);
- setup, prerequisites and required_credential_files;
- required_environment_variables (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:256), which matches Hermes' _get_required_environment_variables: it merges the declared list, setup.collect_secrets and the legacy prerequisites.env_vars, first entry wins, names are validated, and `optional` is read for truth;
- metadata.hermes.{tags, category, upstream_skill, supersedes, session_platforms, requires_toolsets, requires_tools, fallback_for_toolsets, fallback_for_tools, config} (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:340). A config entry needs a key and a description.

Skill exposes platforms, environments, requires_apps, required_env (names only; no value is read) and hermes_meta, and to_dict carries them (agents/core/skills/loader.py:478, agents/core/skills/loader.py:526, agents/core/skills/loader.py:534, agents/core/skills/loader.py:538, agents/core/skills/loader.py:544).

Imported frontmatter is third-party text:
- json_safe (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:128) bounds depth, width, string length and total nodes, with a 2,048-node budget per value (agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:134). A 2 KB YAML alias bomb that would expand to 64^6 nodes parses in about 0.02 s.
- Dates become ISO strings, and NaN, infinities and integers past 64 bits become null or "". A hex integer past Python's str() limit no longer raises (_scalar_text, agents/core/skills/frontmatter.py:112), so the security-posture route serialises Skill.to_dict with allow_nan=False.
- discover() skips a skill whose load raises and keeps the rest, while the signing misconfiguration still stops discovery (agents/core/skills/loader.py:664-669).
- A second skill taking an occupied registry name is logged: a warning within one tree (e.g. two names sharing their first 64 characters), info for a user skill replacing a bundled one (agents/core/skills/loader.py:681).

Deliberate differences from Hermes:
- A closing fence at end of file with no trailing newline is accepted, as Nerva always did.

reviews.summary: Import-once stays the only way a Hermes / OpenClaw / Claude Code skill enters Nerva's skills tree (no live-scanned external_dirs tier; SkillLoader.discover() is unchanged), and a re-run of `python scripts/nerva_import.py` now notices upstream movement instead of reporting a blanket skipped/exists. Each imported skill is re-detected against the absolute source_path and sha256 recorded in its manifest.json (importer.py:955, importer.py:1000): unchanged; changed, with the old and new digests plus a bounded line diff shown by --json; moved to another folder of the same install and followed (importer.py:934); removed; renamed; unreadable; or source_untrusted when a record names a file outside the install, which is then never read (importer.py:1290). The default run is a dry run. `--apply --update` re-imports only changed skills that this source imported (importer.py:1065): the current copy is backed up under data/imports/skill_backups, PENDING_REVIEW is written before the new bytes land, SKILL.sig and the legacy approval marker are cleared, and the owner's approval is revoked. A linked control file, an unusable backup dir or a refused save fails closed, and the write is bound to the probed digest. Every import and re-import crosses skill.install through the real Action Kernel at the shipped CLI (nerva_import.py:577, bound at nerva_import.py:1044 and as the ImportRunner default at nerva_import.py:682), behind SKILL_IMPORT_CONTRACT (nerva_import.py:145). The persisted kill switch is re-read on every decision, so an engaged halt refuses an import or re-import before a byte moves. The external origin keeps a policy GRANT at QUEUE, and only GRANT or QUEUE writes (nerva_import.py:764), so every write lands quarantined. The human summary names a local edit that --update replaces (with its backup path), a failed revoke, and moved, untrusted and refused rows (nerva_import.py:938). Tests in test_nerva_import.py: 44 passed and 1 live-gated skip under python 3.11 and 3.12. They include test_cli_skill_writes_cross_the_real_kernel_and_honour_the_kill_switch, test_runner_default_authorizer_is_the_kernel_for_skills_and_queue_for_memory, test_source_moved_within_the_install_is_followed_not_reported_removed, test_apply_update_reimports_changed_skill_into_quarantine_and_revokes_approval, test_rescan_never_follows_a_record_outside_the_install and test_reimport_refuses_a_linked_control_file_and_never_writes_through_it. Two known limits sit outside the accepted requirement. (1) The CLI binds no durable audit sink, so each kernel decision is recorded only on its report row (kernel/kernel_reason) and in the in-process kernel metrics. (2) A record written before this change with a cwd-relative source_path (relative --home) is not rewritten by an unchanged re-run. From another directory it reads skipped/exists plus source_untrusted until a changed source is re-imported with --apply --update, which records the absolute path.

reviews.summary:
Nerva now reads each provider's quota off every cloud response and shares a 429 with every process. agents/core/llm/quota.py holds the rules. llm_async_client, the one constructor every cloud backend's HTTP client goes through (Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, xAI, the Responses dialect, VLM), now hangs two hooks (agents/core/llm/egress.py:99-100). response_hook (agents/core/llm/quota.py:338) reads the provider's own quota headers with parse_headers (agents/core/llm/quota.py:146): OpenAI-style x-ratelimit-{limit,remaining,reset}-{requests,tokens}; Anthropic's anthropic-ratelimit-{requests,tokens,input-tokens,output-tokens}-{limit,remaining,reset}; and retry-after as seconds or an HTTP date read as UTC. It understands resets given as durations ("6m0s", "20ms") or RFC 3339 times, and it stores the latest numbers per backend, key and model. On a 429 it blocks that backend, key and model (request_model, agents/core/llm/quota.py:78: Gemini's path, else the JSON body's model), or the whole key when the request names no model, until the provider's retry-after, else 30 s, never over 900 s (QuotaStore.block, agents/core/llm/quota.py:207). request_hook (agents/core/llm/quota.py:317) runs before the egress recorder on every request. It refuses a request whose model or whole key is held with ProviderRateLimited before it is sent, so a refused request never reaches the provider or the egress ledger. Another key in the pool is not held: on a refusal the Anthropic backend (_post_messages, and the stream, which retries a refused open on the next key) and the Gemini backend (generate, tool turn, stream) fail over to the next key as on a 429, and ProviderRateLimited carries retry_in, so AuthProfilePool.report_failure(key, cooldown=retry_in) keeps the held key cool for its whole hold (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:98, agents/core/llm/gemini.py:204, agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:159). The H380 provider probe reports a held key as rate_limited, sends nothing, and caches that verdict no longer than the hold and at most 30 s (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:191). Retry-after and reset values must be finite ('inf', 'nan' and overflowing numbers are unreadable), a negative retry-after is unreadable so the 30 s default applies, and a reset time without a zone is read as UTC. The store drops its pre-model tables once. A local host is never tracked or held, even when the same backend is held in the cloud. The state lives in one SQLite file under the data folder (QuotaStore, agents/core/llm/quota.py:173), so the hub, the CLI, the scheduler and any worker see the same numbers and the same holds. A key is known only by a 12-hex fingerprint of its hash, and every failure is swallowed, so a quota reader never breaks a request. usage (agents/core/llm/quota.py:361) gives each backend's requests and tokens left, the fraction left (clamped, none for a missing or non-positive limit), time to reset and any hold. It is served by GET /api/llm/quota (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:439, admin, 503 quota_unavailable when unreadable or when a row cannot be serialised; each row carries its model, which /usage and the panel name), the HUD Provider Quota panel (frontend/src/panels/provider-quota.tsx, Admin group: bars, numbers, reset times, a hold tag), and /usage (agents/core/commands.py:225, admin tier, rendered by render). The router is not fed a forecast; Hermes' own guard is likewise a refusal before the request, which is what this does. tests/conftest.py gives each test its own quota store, so a mocked 429 never holds a later test (tests/conftest.py:187). tests/test_h373_provider_quota.py (78 cases) covers durations, retry-after (seconds, dates, no zone under another host timezone), OpenAI and Anthropic headers, unreadable values, key fingerprints, and the store: latest numbers, clamping, a negative limit, blocks with retry-after, the default and cap, a hold before numbers, two processes, damaged data and the default path. It also covers the hooks on a real llm_async_client (recording, no headers, a 429 hold refused before dialling and absent from the egress ledger, another key, the default hold, other errors, a local model, a local request of a held backend, a failing store), the local-host test, the hook order, rendering, the admin route and the admin /usage command. The review round added the fail-over on a refusal for both backends and their streams, the cooldown floor, per-model holds, finite and signed header values, zone-less resets, the route's serialisation, and the probe's held key (tests/test_h380_provider_probe.py). frontend/src/test/provider-quota-panel.test.tsx has 3 cases. There are 50 mutants, all killed; the review round's 18 mutants, all killed (5 by tests added after a first pass).

Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (ff8641a7): Fallback is a fixed staircase chosen at backend-selection time: Claude -> Gemini 'cloud-fallback' -> local (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:585-592), local -> 'cloud-flash' governed by the single `llm.cloud_fallback` never/on-demand/always setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:175, agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:618). A failed call mid-turn is not retried on another provider: the Claude backend returns '[Claude API error: ...]' as text (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:136) and the orchestrator returns '[agent error: ...]' (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4877). The nearest reachable mechanism is the cabinet fan-out: several agents (each resolving its own backend/route) answer the same turn concurrently (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4770, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4885, per-agent route at agents/core/orchestrator.py:4926) and a synthesis pass merges them (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4945; agents/core/agent.py:1252-1286), with a local-only floor on the merge (agents/core/agent.py:1288-1300); tests/test_ch02_g1_stream_fanout.py:40 pins fan-out plus synthesis. The Model Arena runs one prompt on two models side by side for comparison (agents/core/routers/arena.py:15). These give multi-model fan-out plus aggregation, but not user-selected reference models feeding an aggregator that drives the tool loop.
reviews.remaining:
- /moa slash command and MoA selectable as a model/provider in the API
- Named MoA presets (reference models + aggregator) managed from CLI/HUD
- Advisors as non-acting reference models whose advice an aggregator model uses while driving the tool loop
- PII privacy filter on advisor output (to user and, at strongest setting, to the aggregator)
- Per-turn JSON trace of what each model saw, said and cost
- Tests for all of the above

Capability tokens exist only per agent (agents/core/kernel/capabilities.py:52), not per external client.

Choosing a model now passes one registry of guards, server-side and before the choice is stored, on every surface that picks a model, as Hermes' selection-guard registry does. agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py holds the registry: register (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:123) adds a guard, and evaluate (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:175) runs every guard once per choice, so a new guard appears on every surface at once. enforce (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:186) returns the findings once all are cleared, or raises SelectionRefused naming every finding and the flags still missing. A flag clears only a literal true. Two guards ship. The cost guard (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:130) asks confirm_expensive for a model whose output costs at least llm.cost_confirm_usd_per_mtok (agents/core/settings_db.py:208; $40 per million tokens by default, 0 never asks, in safe mode the stricter of it and $40 (0, never asking, takes the $40; H490), a negative value refused on write at agents/core/settings_db.py:1149, an unreadable one read as $40). It names the input and output prices from cost_estimator.MODELS; price_of (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:84) prices a routed slug (vendor/model) or a variant (model:beta) by its model, and an unpriced model is not asked. The data-policy guard (agents/core/llm/selection_guards.py:153) asks acknowledge_training for a model or route whose vendor may train on the prompts. reviews.summary: A configured cloud key is checked with its provider before a turn finds out. agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py asks each cloud provider once, with the key the hub would use (configured_key, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:87: for Anthropic and Gemini, the only providers with an AuthProfilePool (POOLED), the first of the `<VAR>S` pool split on commas and whitespace as the router splits it, else `<VAR>`; every other provider reads `<VAR>` only). The command center asks with the key the route's backend holds: the pool's current key for Claude and Gemini, the compatible backend's own api_key otherwise. It sends one authenticated GET (request_for, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:105): Anthropic /v1/models with x-api-key and anthropic-version, Gemini /v1beta/models with x-goog-api-key, OpenRouter `<base>/key` (its model list is public; the key record answers 401 to a key it does not know), and `<base>/models` with a bearer for the other OpenAI-shaped providers, honouring a configured base URL. The GET goes through llm_async_client, so it is in the egress ledger as `llm:<provider>`, and H368's host-protocol mandate refuses a mismatch before it leaves; the xAI and OpenAI Responses probes use trust_env=False, as their backends do (NO_ENV_TRUST, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:67). Nothing is generated. The verdict (probe, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:223) is one of: `ok` (any 2xx, with the listed model count); `no_listing` (404/405: nothing at that URL, so the key is not proven); `auth_failed` (401, or a 400 whose body names a bad key: Gemini API_KEY_INVALID/API_KEY_EXPIRED, xAI "Incorrect API key"; the body is read inside the probe and never returned); `forbidden` (403); `rate_limited` (429, or a key held by the shared 429 guard of H373, with nothing sent); `error` (any other status, which is named, or an unexpected failure); `unreachable` (any transport error); `refused` (the host mandate); `not_configured` (no key, nothing sent); or `not_cloud` (a local provider). Only `ok` proves the key (WORKING, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:61). The key and the response body are never in a result or a log line. A result is cached per provider, key fingerprint and probed URL, so a changed key or base URL is probed afresh: for TTL_SECONDS (300 s), and a transient verdict (rate_limited, error, unreachable) for TRANSIENT_TTL_SECONDS (30 s) or, for a guard-held key, no longer than its hold (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:53-56). Concurrent callers, forced ones included, share one in-flight request (_fresh, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:205). A forced re-check inside MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (30 s) answers the cached verdict marked `throttled`. last (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:263) reads the cache without a request. probe_all (agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:301) asks every cloud provider concurrently, except one whose key variable belongs to a base URL on another host (_key_for_elsewhere, agents/core/llm/provider_probe.py:287): an OPENAI_API_KEY beside an OPENAI_BASE_URL on a gateway is not sent to api.openai.com unless llm.compatible_provider is openai-responses. POST /api/admin/llm/providers/probe (admin; admin_llm_providers_probe, agents/core/routers/admin.py:959) checks one provider or all, with `force`; an unknown provider is a 404. The Console's Provider Check panel (Admin; frontend/src/panels/provider-check.tsx) probes nothing until asked. It shows each verdict (`key rejected` with the HTTP status beside it; `key not verified (nothing at this URL)` in amber for no_listing), the model count and a named HTTP status, offers a forced re-check per provider, and says when a re-check was throttled. The command-center model block asks the provider for a selected cloud route (_cloud_probe, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:224; agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:339) and waits at most CLOUD_PROBE_WAIT_SECONDS (4 s), after which the verdict reads `unreachable` and the probe finishes in the background. The route is ready (`cloud_selected`) on `ok`; `rate_limited` keeps it runnable (`cloud_rate_limited`); `no_listing`, `error` and `unreachable` make it unknown (ready=None, `cloud_no_listing` / `cloud_error` / `cloud_unreachable`); `auth_failed`, `forbidden`, `refused` and `not_configured` make it not runnable (CLOUD_PROBE_REASONS, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:204). The block carries `cloud_probe` (provider, verdict, status code, time, cached; agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:370), and its hint names the provider, what it said and the HTTP status (_model_hint, agents/core/routers/onboarding.py:391). `nerva doctor`'s runtime_resolves and `nerva status`'s runnable line read that block, so a wrong or revoked key now fails them with its reason instead of passing on "a key is set". tests/test_h380_provider_probe.py (30 cases) covers the request per provider with the key only in a header, the key resolution, one read and its model count across list shapes, nine statuses, three transport failures and an unexpected one, the protocol refusal recorded as not sent, the egress row, no request without a key or for a local provider, no key or body in results or logs, the cache per key with expiry, the throttled and then allowed forced re-check, the cache-only read, probe_all, the admin route (admin-only, one, all, force, 404) and the command center's key choice. tests/test_h380b_provider_probe_review.py (35 cases) covers the review round: OpenRouter asked about its key, not its public list; a gateway key kept away from api.openai.com and OpenAI asked when the key is its own; a 400 that names a bad key; a missing listing that proves nothing; the key read as the router reads it and the compatible backend's own key; a guard-held key rate_limited for the hold; concurrent callers sharing one request; the bounded wait; readiness per verdict and the short cache of a transient one; trust_env matching the backends; the hint; and the cache slot per URL. tests/test_first_run_command_center.py covers every `cloud_*` reason and `cloud_probe` in the model block. The panel has 3 vitest cases. The row's 38 mutants were all killed. The review round's 36 mutants: 29 caught at once, six after six cases were added to tests/test_h380b_provider_probe_review.py (a finished request is not joined again, a caller that stops waiting leaves the verdict cached, a request in flight on another event loop is not awaited, the cache-only read forgets a transient verdict, reset forgets a request in flight, the hint for an unknown provider), and one equivalent (`ready is True` and truthiness agree on True/False/None). reviews.summary: **The SOUL body is scanned before it reaches the model, and the HUD is told when it was.** `Agent._read_soul` — the one builder behind `_load_soul` at construction and, since H672, `Agent.refresh_soul` at the compaction boundary — resolves the live file through `soul_path_for`, splits the front-matter, runs `_scan_soul_body` over the *uncapped* body (so truncation can never drop the very lines the detector would have flagged), quarantines flagged lines to a visible stub that names the FILE line, and only then caps the result; the verdict is announced by `_announce_soul_verdict`, one place for both moments a persona lands, so a quarantined persona is the same ERROR line whether it arrived at boot or under a running session, and the over-cap WARNING likewise. The scan is four passes: `strip_invisible` deletes TAG-plane characters and the decoded payload is scanned with `detect_injection`, so a smuggled phrase is named in the flags rather than silently deleted; every line is scanned with `detect_injection_normalized` — the union of the raw line, its Cf-stripped copy, its whitespace-collapsed copy and both together, with the ORIGINAL kept; `_wrapped_injection_hits` re-reads the non-blank lines as one normalised string and, through `quarantine.injection_spans`, quarantines exactly the lines a cross-line match covers, leaving single-line spans to the per-line pass so nothing is flagged twice; and the whole body is dropped for `_blocked_soul_body` (which carries `_SOUL_FALLBACK_RULES`) when flagged lines exceed `_SOUL_BLOCK_RATIO` of the non-blank lines OR when a non-empty body is left whitespace-only by the passes. Passes one, two and four are #1173; #1179 — wave two of the adversarial review — moved the per-line call from `detect_injection` on a Cf-stripped copy to `detect_injection_normalized`, added the wrap pass, and added the second trigger of the escalation. Wave two found the per-line scan defeated by a respacing ("Ignore  all  previous  instructions" with two spaces, a tab or a NO-BREAK SPACE scanned clean, because the patterns are literal with single spaces and stripping cannot answer a real separator without gluing two words together), by a line wrap through the phrase (no pattern contains a newline, and Markdown reflows prose freely), and by a persona written wholly in TAG characters, which returned `("", flags, False)` — an agent with no persona at all AND no fallback rules, so quality.py's persona-consistency rail read an empty forbidden-phrase list for the least-constrained agent on the box. The respacing fix lives in the shared normaliser (`quarantine.collapse_whitespace` + `_detection_variants`), so the catalog-row scan in `agents/core/skills/loader.py` gets it in the same change. `GET /api/agents/{id}/soul` keeps returning the raw bytes on disk — it is the editor view, and the owner has to see what they actually wrote — but carries a `guard` verdict beside it, computed by `_soul_guard_verdict` from the SAME helpers `_read_soul` uses (`_scan_soul_body`, `_cap_soul_body`, `_soul_max_chars`; the router's comments still say `_load_soul`, which still exists and delegates to the builder), so the HUD can no longer show a persona the model is not receiving without saying so, and the wave-two passes reach the verdict without the router changing. Before this the only trace of a quarantined persona was a `logger.error` nobody watches. **An independent review of the original slice found two blocking majors and both were fixed there.** The first was a records defect that would have turned the tree red on merge: the slice edits `agents/core/agent.py`, whose sha256 is pinned by eight evidence entries, and regenerated no reports — dropping the headline to 119/697 and flipping six rows to stale. The second was subtler and worse. The endpoint resolved only `agents/<id>/SOUL.local.md` → `agents/<id>/SOUL.md`, while `_load_soul` checks the user data home FIRST (`Documents/Jarvis/souls/<id>/SOUL.local.md`, the packaged-install overlay). So on a packaged box the HUD read one file, ran the guard over it, and reported `blocked: false` for a persona the model had in fact had dropped — **precisely the case the verdict exists to prevent**, reproduced with a real overlay. Both now resolve through one shared `agent.soul_path_for()`, because two resolutions of "which SOUL is live" is one too many, and `test_the_editor_endpoint_reads_the_file_the_model_reads` drives the real endpoint against a data-home overlay. #1179 left `routers/agents_api.py` untouched — same sha256 either side of the merge. Six new test functions (eleven collected cases) in `tests/test_soul_injection_guard.py` pin the six respacings, the composition with an invisible character, the wrap, the wholly-invisible body, the empty-file non-case, and that a persona's own double spaces and hard wraps still ship byte-identical. H672 (the compaction-boundary refresh) restructured `agent.py` around that builder without changing a pass: `_read_soul(quiet=True)` lets `refresh_soul` compare the rebuilt bytes before announcing, so the same flagged persona is not re-logged at every commit, and a persona rewritten under a running session is scanned, capped and — when it is now mostly injection — dropped exactly as a restart would drop it, at the same ERROR (`test_a_persona_flagged_at_the_boundary_is_announced_at_error_like_a_restart`, `test_a_persona_quarantined_mid_session_is_dropped_at_the_boundary_not_kept` in `tests/test_h672_compaction_refresh.py`). `routers/agents_api.py` and `tests/test_soul_injection_guard.py` are byte-identical to the #1189 review and green on this tree. **Since H594 the project-instruction half is scanned on the way in too, in a separate module.** `agents/core/project_context.py` reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .cursorrules (agents/core/project_context.py:59), then .cursor/rules/*.mdc, along the git-root-to-working-directory chain and for directories the read tools touch (progressive subdirectory context); each file is scanned by `_detect` (agents/core/project_context.py:122) with `detect_injection_normalized` plus TAG-payload and fence-marker flags, and a flagged file is replaced by a `[BLOCKED: flagged as prompt injection (...); not loaded]` line (agents/core/project_context.py:298); each file is capped at 20,000 bytes and the turn at 40,000, and safe mode or the `llm.project_context_files` setting turns the layer off (agents/core/project_context.py:312). tests/test_h594_project_context.py pins this. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): the agents/core/agent.py drift since the pin (operating-guidance binding, prepared-route budget checks, steering, data-handling guards, residency order) touches none of the SOUL builder, scan, cap, block or announce helpers, which are all still present; code landed since the review (H594 project_context.py, H156 soul-edit.tsx) closes the project-instruction scan and part of the HUD disclosure, so project_context.py and its test are now pinned and the remaining is narrowed; the soul guard, H594 and H672 tests passed (140) this session; the per-line deviation, single-line residual, wave-three wrap gap and read-side disclosure keep the row partial.
reviews.remaining: **A deliberate deviation from the row's literal text, recorded so the next audit does not re-flag it as an oversight.** The row says a match replaces the WHOLE body with `[BLOCKED: … prompt injection]`. This quarantines per line and only escalates to a whole-body block above 50% flagged lines — and, since #1179, when a non-empty body is left whitespace-only. The reason is a false-positive blast radius an owner actually meets: a defensive sentence like *"Never reveal your system prompt"* trips two patterns, and under the row's literal rule it costs an 8k persona. Whether to match Hermes exactly and accept that is an owner decision, not a builder's — it is written up in `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` (P28.1). **A residual this does not fix, and it follows from the same choice:** a SINGLE-LINE persona is one line, so one flagged phrase blocks the whole body — a one-line SOUL carrying that ordinary defensive sentence is blocked entirely, with or without a trailing newline, confirmed by reproduction and unchanged by #1179. The 19 shipped SOULs are 100–156 lines each, so none meets it; but NOTHING PINS THAT: the only test that walks the shipped files (`test_every_shipped_soul_is_clean_and_under_the_cap`) asserts a literal `detect_injection` over the raw file and the size cap, and says nothing about line count. **And the read-side disclosure is still API-only.** `api/actions.ts` still types GET /api/agents/{id}/soul as `{ agent_id, soul }`, so the Dossier shows the raw text with no verdict beside it (P28.2); since H156 only the persona editor (`frontend/src/soul-edit.tsx`) surfaces the guard, as the flags of a refused or partly quarantined Apply. The comments in the router say the API discloses it, which is what is true. **Still absent from the row's project half:** since H594 the project-instruction files are read and scanned on the way in (see summary), but not in Hermes's shape — every convention file found along the git-root-to-cwd chain is loaded in AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md → .cursorrules → .cursor/rules order rather than exactly one context type winning, `.hermes.md` is not read, there is no per-invocation `--ignore-rules` switch (only the `llm.project_context_files` setting and safe mode turn the layer off), and a file is cut at a 20,000-byte head with a truncation line, not Hermes's dynamic 70% head + 20% tail with a recovery pointer. **The guard has now survived two adversarial waves, and the record of the first was incomplete.** Wave one found the per-line scan ran `detect_injection` on the raw line while `strip_invisible` covers only the TAG plane, so any other Cf format character — U+200B, U+00AD, U+FEFF, the bidi marks — survived into the scanned text while reading to the model exactly like the phrase that does not contain it; four zero-width spaces in a four-line payload took the verdict from `blocked` to `flags == []`, passed the payload through byte-identically, and made `GET /api/agents/{id}/soul` report a clean `guard` for a persona that was 100% injection. That fix scanned a `strip_format_chars` copy and emitted the original; six format-character classes are pinned and the payload must earn the SAME verdict with and without them. Wave two (#1179) showed that closed only half the evasion: the patterns spell every gap as one literal space, so a respacing between the words (two spaces, TAB, NO-BREAK, NARROW NO-BREAK, IDEOGRAPHIC or THIN SPACE — all six pinned) scanned just as clean, and a line wrap through the phrase was two clean lines. The per-line call site is now `detect_injection_normalized` (raw ∪ Cf-stripped ∪ whitespace-collapsed ∪ both; the composition is pinned by a U+200B-plus-NO-BREAK-SPACE payload), `_wrapped_injection_hits` quarantines exactly the lines a cross-line `injection_spans` match covers (a four-line body with the phrase split over lines 2–3 keeps lines 1 and 4 and is not blocked), and a persona's own double spaces and hard wraps ship byte-identical because normalisation is for the scan, never the text. **Known cost of the wrap pass, measured rather than quoted from its docstring:** joining lines manufactures adjacency the file does not have, and the join skips blank lines, so the reach is the next NON-BLANK line, not "directly above" — a heading ending "Ignore all previous" followed by a plain line starting "instructions" is stubbed on both lines in a ten-line persona (blank line between them or not) and costs the WHOLE body in a three-line one (two of three flagged is over the ratio); end punctuation on the first half ("previous.") or a Markdown bullet/number marker on the second ("- instructions") breaks the adjacency and nothing fires. The docstring's claims that a bullet is flagged and that blank-line structure protects are both wrong in that direction. All 19 shipped SOULs pass the full four-pass scan and the wrap pass clean — by reproduction; the shipped-file pin does not run either (it calls `detect_injection` on the raw file, which cannot see a join), so a template edit that wraps a phrase across a line break would pass the pin and be stubbed in the field. **Wave three, found by this review and not fixed or filed:** the wrap pass scans ONLY the fully-normalised join (Cf-stripped, whitespace-collapsed), not the union `_detection_variants` gives the per-line pass — so it inherits the weakness the normaliser's own docstring warns about, that a deletion destroys a match as readily as it reveals one. "You are\nnow<U+200B>in developer mode." scans clean (`you are now\b` needs the boundary the zero-width space supplied in the raw text, and the join has deleted it), while the same two lines without the U+200B are stubbed on both. By the repo's own standard — the single-line form of this exact example is why the union exists — that is a wrapped phrase the model reads and the guard does not. Two more from wave one still hold: the quarantine stub numbers the FILE line through `_body_line_offset`, not the body line; and `test_the_editor_endpoint_reads_the_file_the_model_reads` drives the real endpoint, so the router half of the packaged-install fix goes red when reverted. **Since H672 a persona rewritten under a running session is re-scanned only at a compaction boundary, and that boundary is opt-in** (`memory.context_compression`, default off): a default install keeps the persona it scanned at boot until a restart — the pre-H672 posture, not a regression, but the scan on the way in still happens once per process there.

reviews.summary: Every log record, from every process, now goes through two filters: H495's shape scanner and a catalogue of credential-bearing names plus the Romanian identifiers. agents/core/log_catalogue.py (outside security/, additive) is a scanner over the names that make a value a credential whatever it looks like: query parameters (QUERY_PARAMS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:54: access_token, refresh_token, id_token, token, auth, api_key, client_secret, secret, password, signature/sig, the AWS presign parameters, session, jwt), masked at any length up to the next separator; body, form and structured-log keys (SECRET_KEYS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:62), quoted in JSON or a Python repr, assigned with a quoted value, or unquoted when the value is six characters or more; the Authorization header after any scheme (Bearer, Basic, Token, Digest, ApiKey, HMAC…), or without one when the value is twelve characters or more and carries a digit, so `Authorization: denied` stays; the credential headers X-Api-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Access-Token, X-Goog-Api-Key, X-User-Token, X-Admin-Token, Api-Key and X-Webhook-Token (SECRET_HEADERS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:68); and the whole value of Cookie and Set-Cookie. It also runs PIIScanner's own CNP and IBAN patterns (agents/core/security/scanner.py:287-288) with their checksum validators, and an IBAN written in spaced groups of four; the other PII patterns stay out (an e-mail or phone number in a log is often the point of the line; card and SSN shapes carry no checksum). A bare `key` parameter (settings routes use it for a setting's name) and a bare `token:` key (token counts) are not in the catalogue. The rules are in _rules (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:91); a value already masked is never re-masked, so a JWT the first filter named keeps its name. CatalogueScanner (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:126) offers redact, scan and the _compiled rows H495's prefilter is built from, and CatalogueRedactionFilter (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:161) runs it through an unchanged SecretRedactionFilter (agents/core/security/log_redaction.py:230): the arguments uvicorn's AccessFormatter unpacks are kept, a secret split between the format string and an argument masks the argument whole and is named after the finding that holds, tracebacks and stack info are masked, a failing scanner drops the record's content to [redaction-unavailable], and the one JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION switch, snapshotted at import, turns both filters off. It wraps rather than subclasses, so H495's installer, which skips a handler already carrying a SecretRedactionFilter, never mistakes it for its own. install_catalogue_redaction_everywhere (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:220) covers the root handlers and every logger's own (uvicorn's detached ones included), idempotently, and counts and names a handler that refuses the filter. core.log's _install_redaction (agents/core/log.py:69) installs it right after the H495 filter, so setup_logging (agents/core/log.py:108) gives every handler both, in that order; install_redaction (agents/core/log.py:102) is the same for a process that configures its own logging. The two entry points that called a bare basicConfig and wrote every record unredacted now call it: the headless coordinator (configure_logging, scripts/coordinator.py:145) and the MCP stdio bridge (configure_logging, scripts/nerva_mcp_stdio.py:149, still stderr only, since stdout is its protocol channel). Neither takes setup_logging's rotating file handler, which a second process would rotate under the hub (critic note 32). The H145 log reader runs the catalogue on every line it serves (agents/core/log_tail.py:167), for lines written before it or by a process it did not cover. The test isolation fixture strips the catalogue filter with the H495 one (tests/conftest.py:271). The H495 module's docstring (agents/core/security/, a protected path) still names the coordinator and the MCP bridge as uncovered and says no PII pass runs; it describes that module alone. tests/test_h410_log_catalogue.py (52 cases) covers the five probes the audit found unmasked and every other name in the catalogue, ordinary text that must stay (a failed authorization, a setting key, an exit code, a token count, a 13-digit order number, an IBAN-shaped string that fails its checksum, a short value), the exact line kept around a mask, CNP and IBAN compact and spaced, an access-log record keeping its five arguments, a traceback, a JWT keeping the first filter's name, a straddling IBAN, the switch, a failing scanner, both filters on every handler once and in order, a refusing handler counted and named, both entry points with a fresh root (the bridge writing nothing to stdout), and the log reader. 31 mutants: 30 killed (4 by cases added after a first pass) and 1 equivalent that removed a redundant `(?:proxy-)?` prefix (`\b` holds after the hyphen). Test manual: SEC-216.

reviews.summary:
Compaction now checkpoints the turns it is about to discard, and fails closed when a required checkpoint does not land. ContextCompressor takes a checkpoint callable (agents/core/context_compressor.py:323). compress() awaits it with exactly the turns the summary replaces (the evicted middle, all of it even when a prior summary covers part) and the whole transcript, before the summary is built (agents/core/context_compressor.py:588-595). The orchestrator builds that callable in _precompress_checkpoint (agents/core/orchestrator.py:419) and hands it to the compressor on every compacting history build (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4556). It calls precompress.run_checkpoint (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:107) over the registered providers, or the default transcript archive. The hook is versioned. A provider declares checkpoint_api_version, and only one at CHECKPOINT_API_VERSION 2 or above counts (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:63). The optional keyword arguments (evidence_messages, require_checkpoint, checkpoint_api_version, session_id) are passed only when the provider's signature accepts them (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:69). A synchronous provider runs off the event loop, and providers get copies, so they cannot change the transcript. The shipped provider, TranscriptArchive (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:174), keeps a raw per-session JSONL copy of the evicted turns. It appends each evicted turn once, by a hash of speaker, time and content, to a file whose name is a hash of the session, under the data folder (compaction_archive), owner-only (0600 in a 0700 folder); the append is flushed and fsynced before on_pre_compress returns (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:208). It remembers what it holds across restarts, skips damaged lines (including a line cut inside a multi-byte character), starts the next record on a new line after a torn last line, and writes images as [image]. It is not an extraction. Nothing mines those turns into episodes, consolidation or LivingMemory, and nothing checks that per-turn LivingMemory extraction landed for them. Recall and session_search never read the archive (TranscriptArchive.read() has no production caller), and no production code registers precompress_providers. The archive runs only while memory.persist is on (agents/core/orchestrator.py:431), and a chat's backup-first delete (H218, which the H262 sweep uses) removes it with the chat, while the sweep prunes orphaned archives (purge_orphan_compaction_archives, agents/core/retention.py:100). memory.compression_checkpoint_required (agents/core/settings_db.py:291, off by default; only a literal true turns it on) makes it fail closed. A failing checkpoint provider, or no checkpoint provider landing ("No active memory provider completed pre-compress checkpoint API v2"), raises CheckpointAborted. The compressor then summarises nothing. Old images are still dropped, with an images-tier lineage row when any were (agents/core/context_compressor.py:518-530). The orchestrator refuses the turn with the compaction refusal reply only when the image-dropped transcript does not fit the model's window (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4603). With the setting off, a failing provider is logged and compaction proceeds. A checkpoint that landed new turns, or had a provider fail, writes memory.precompress_checkpoint to the signed intent log with an archived count (agents/core/memory/precompress.py:148). One that landed nothing new, the steady state once over budget, writes nothing. Every abort writes memory.precompress_abort. The rows carry turn counts, provider names and the reason, never the turns, and every audit write runs off the event loop. tests/test_h427_precompress_checkpoint.py (54 cases) covers the contract (version, names, signature sniffing, copies, a synchronous provider, nothing to evict), the not-required and required paths (failing provider, old provider, no provider, a missing or non-callable hook, a failing audit), and the archive (write once, fsync, restart, damaged lines, hashed names, images and structured content, turn identity, default location). It also covers the compressor (exactly the evicted turns before the summary, a prior summary, abort, under budget, compact fail-closed) and the orchestrator (archived and audited, required failure keeps the transcript with no clock commit, not required proceeds, no provider, refusal exactly at the window, a literal-true switch, the default archive, the settings row, no turn text in the audit). The original build had 51 mutants: 49 killed and 2 equivalent (a non-callable hook fails with the same TypeError either way; re-reading the archive file each time is only slower). The review round added the retention prune, the memory.persist gate, the steady-state audit, the torn-line and multi-byte handling and the file modes, each with a case that fails without it. reviews.summary:
file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). local_docs and agents/core/ingestion/ remain the bulk-ingestion path into memory. Local 2026-10-09 parser-backed file_read admission refuses an observed on-disk PDF/DOCX size above 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB) as document_too_large before parser discovery or extraction. Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds. Local 2026-10-09 PDF text-layer coverage uses one shared parser traversal per request and adds coverage_warning beside unchanged extracted content when more than 20% of pages or at least ten pages yield no text. It reports exact page/gap totals, the first 16 maximal one-based ranges, and preceding source excerpts capped to 160 Unicode code points, with explicit omitted-range and excerpt-truncation fields. Blank/whitespace/None page text counts; reader/page failures retain extraction_failed without partial coverage. Existing normal-loop and nested ToolRPC scanners also scan the quoted metadata; this does not declare every file result untrusted.

A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). local_docs and agents/core/ingestion/ remain the bulk-ingestion path into memory.

reviews.remaining:
Coverage measures extracted text only: nonblank but incomplete/garbled text and visual content are not detected. Only the first 16 gap ranges are listed, with an explicit omitted count; no OCR is performed. Every admitted document page still reparses the whole file, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned. The observed-size admission does not cap parser memory/CPU, decompression or full extracted-text allocation, and cannot prevent file growth after stat; bulk ingestion remains separate. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. The wider format matrix (.ipynb, .xlsx, legacy Office, OpenDocument, .rtf, .epub) and Markdown conversion are not built; the row's rationale does not ask for them.

No size ceiling applies to a document: the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned, where Hermes refuses documents over 50 MB. reviews.summary:
A work run can now be parked on real async work instead of being poked. Three barrier kinds hold a run's next tick without spending anything (BARRIER_KINDS, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:141):
- a registered process until it exits;
- a trigger until it fires: a queued task of this run reaching a terminal status, or an enabled webhook being called;
- a wall-clock time.

The barrier is a `barrier` column on the run (the _v2 migration, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:423). It also adds `run_events` (set and clear audit) and `run_procs` (processes registered for a run). Setting and clearing a barrier are events, not steps: they cost no budget, stay outside the fingerprint, and never change a verification result (set_barrier, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1511; clear_barrier_if, a compare-and-clear, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1586). A move to stopping or any terminal status clears the barrier in the same write, so stop always wins.

Validation, probes and stale clearing live in RunBarriers (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:280):
- request (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:314) refuses a spent or unparkable run and bounds every barrier. Its cap (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:355) is the earliest of its own wait (at most MAX_BARRIER_SECONDS, 7 days, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:74), the run's deadline, and the time the run's budget has left. Since H464b that is the EFFECTIVE budget (now + budget_state's seconds_left), so H487's proven approval-wait credit counts at barriers too; before, a run with credited wait time was refused `no_time_left` or capped early by the whole credit.
- A pid must first be registered for this run through the Python-only register_process (agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:562). That refuses pid ≤ 1, the hub, its parent and dead processes, and allows at most 16 per run. It captures the process's start token, pid namespace and boot id.

H464b made one park path real in the shipped product. With JARVIS_COMPANY_MODE set at boot:

Every step still goes through the governed intake.
- The approved checklist is read back from the goal's own approval task (_read_back, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:228). The task named in the run's `approved_by` (`task:<id>:<decider>`) is re-read from the durable queue and re-minted through approve_from_task, which re-checks that a human accepted that very task. The owner can always let a run go:
- POST /api/company/runs/{run_id}/barrier/clear (user-guarded, agents/core/routers/company.py:179);

- the Company room's two-step "stop waiting".

The clear reports what it did, or what a newer barrier now waits on. A wait the owner cleared is not set again on the same target by the planner or the judge, nor by the hub's in-flight park. A barrier only suppresses work. It grants nothing:
- no approval;
- no resume of a blocked run;
- no budget extension;
- no path around the governed intake.

The margin is the floor the runtime passes, at least a minute (grade_margin, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:136; GRADE_MARGIN_SECONDS, agents/core/autonomy/run_barriers.py:133): the time from a tick to the next sweep on which the scheduler's per-run interval lets the run be due again (next_due_after_tick, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:115: the first multiple of the sweep cadence at or past the 300 s interval) plus a minute (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:434) — 360 s at the default 300 s cadence and at 60 s, 420 s at 120 s, 460 s at 200 s, 1,260 s at 1,200 s. It is never a share of the budget, and the same margin applies before a deadline. With nothing to spare past the margin the hub does not park and the run is graded now. Planner and judge waits are unchanged.
- M4: safe mode leaves company mode out: schedule_company_mode builds nothing and registers no sweep (a new `company_mode` safe-mode layer), and a sweep that finds safe mode on does nothing (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:134).
- M5: the read-back says why it has no goal (_ReadBack, agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:216). "Cannot tell right now" (no reader, a read that raised) HOLDS the run: the planner returns Hold(stop=False) (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:164) and the tick is `idle` "held: …" with no step, no park and no grade (_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:408). Provably not bound (not opened from a goal card, no pin, a task that is gone, a policy decision, an edit, another run's goal, a binding check that raised, and since H464d anything re-minting the task raises) STOPS the run with `plan not bound to its approval: <reason>` as its stop reason, the way a stuck run is stopped, so the brief shows it. Neither is ever graded as a finished checklist.
- M6: a plan row's queued task kind must be inside the goal's scope (task_kind_in_scope, agents/core/autonomy/goal_contract.py:91: a scope kind, or under a whole one then a dot, `research.collect` under `research` and, since H464d, `file.write.append` under `file.write`).
