H464d (the third review, of H464c: one MAJOR, four MINOR, four NIT, and two MINOR the closure found in older code) makes the grading margin exact and the rest of the chain honest:
- A1/B2/F1: the margin above. The 10 % share graded an 8 h run with 40 minutes left over its still-running task (the reviewer's e10: graded at minute 440 on `running`; now at minute 455 on `done`), and a sweep-only floor left a run parked into a window where the scheduler's own interval never let it be ticked again at cadences under 300 s. A run is now graded before its time runs out at 60, 120, 200, 300 and 1,200 s cadences through the real due() gate, whose per-run interval allows 1 s (at most 1 %) of timer jitter (due_slack, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:110; agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:249), so a sweep a moment early does not push grading a whole sweep past the margin.
- B1: anything re-minting the approved goal raises is provable (agents/core/autonomy/company_runtime.py:276): a budget edited to zero steps stops the run with `plan not bound to its approval: invalid_max_steps` (WorkRunError keeps its code; anything else is `approved_goal_invalid`) instead of failing every tick. Only the read is transient.
- B3: the reconciler records each still-open approval wait on every sweep (_observe_wait, agents/core/autonomy/pending_requests.py:307, a settling budget read), so an ask the owner edited before approving is credited up to the last sweep that saw it open whether or not the HUD polled (the reviewer's e1/e1b, ported with a sweep a minute: 180 s credit and 30 s used both ways, 0 and 210 s before). The report routes stay read-only.
- B4: a hold writes one `hold.start` run event per hold (note_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1685, deduplicated while the same hold is open), the first tick that can plan again writes `hold.end` (end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1702; _end_hold, agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:436), the snapshot carries the open hold (hold_state, agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1713), and the brief lists the run as held with a plain reason (_held, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:139). A run the scheduler skips as budget_spent is settled through the supervisor's settle_spent (agents/core/autonomy/company_supervisor.py:520; _settle, agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:269), which re-reads the budget, so a read that failed settles nothing; before, a spent run was never ticked and stayed open for ever.
- F2/F3 (older code): a checklist row whose step failed (the intake raised or returned no task, or the task vanished) is not done; it is tried again on a later sweep, at most MAX_ROW_ATTEMPTS (3, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:77) attempts, then the run stops with `approved row kept failing: <row> (3 attempts)`. A failed read of the run's own steps is a refusal (_run_steps, agents/core/autonomy/company_planner.py:300) the runtime holds on, instead of reading "nothing done" and asking for row 1 again.
- M05/M43 test gaps closed; C4 stop wording; C2 an upgrade note (docs/UPGRADE.md) and plain stop reasons in the brief (_hub_stop, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:150): an in-flight run from before the pin stops once, as "opened before this version tied a run to the plan you approved; approve the goal again to run it"; C3, a rollback reading pinned runs as tampered, is documented there.

The owner can always let a run go:
- POST /api/company/runs/{run_id}/barrier/clear (user-guarded, agents/core/routers/company.py:179);
- `nerva company clear-wait`;
- the Company room's two-step "stop waiting".

The clear reports what it did, or what a newer barrier now waits on. A wait the owner cleared is not set again on the same target by the planner or the judge, nor by the hub's in-flight park. The brief and the HUD say "parked — waiting on …" only while the barrier is in force (_in_force, agents/core/autonomy/company_report.py:112).

A barrier only suppresses work. It grants nothing:
- no approval;
- no resume of a blocked run;
- no budget extension;
- no path around the governed intake.

reviews.remaining:
Not reachable in production yet:
- **No process producer (owner decision 1; blocked on H302).** Nothing in the hub starts run-owned background work and registers its pid: register_process has no caller outside tests. The best first producer is `terminal_run` with `background: true` on the local-host transport. It needs WorkRunLedger.run_for_task; a spawn with start_new_session, bounded log files and a held proc.wait() that records the exit code; a lifetime cap and killpg on cap, ESTOP or stop; a reaper for stopped runs; schema, approval-card and parity updates; and a KillMode in deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service (today a restart kills the child and the barrier clears as `exited`, indistinguishable from success). The owner must say whether the task/hook trigger is an accepted adaptation of Hermes's pid/session barrier, or whether a pid wait must be reachable for "equivalent".
- **Pid waits are unusable on macOS/BSD.** There is no start token there, so every pid wait is refused `pid_unprovable`. The fix belongs in exec_cache.py (ctypes libproc proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)) or in a producer-held Popen handle, and needs macOS hardware or a macOS CI runner to verify.
- **The judge's `wait` verdict and planner waits are not reachable in production (owner decision 2).** WorkJudge.wait_probe needs a model rubric, and the shipped runtime passes no rubric, model planner or graders. Wiring one needs the owner's choice of local model and provider under H513 (auxiliary_request_scope, strict-local, security.data_training_ack) plus opt-in settings forced off in safe mode. Before any model planner, the rest of the intake arguments must be clamped: since H464c the task's kind is scope-checked as well as Action.kind, but the task's agent, title and payload still reach govern_enqueue unchanged.
- **No graders are wired in production.** After the hub park clears, a run idles until its budget ends. Deterministic verifier and judge adapters belong to the company-mode grading work; they must reuse an existing verdict, because _grade has no try/except and a judge that raises after the verifier recorded leaves `verdict_already_recorded` / `tick_failed` on every later sweep.

Deferred:
- Wake-on-fire: a parked run resumes at the next scheduled sweep.
- A `job:<id>` trigger.
- A process output-pattern trigger (needs the process producer).
- An owner-set wait like Hermes's `/goal wait` (owner decision 3): a clock or own-task wait only, never an owner-typed pid.
- Waiting between checklist steps: the checklist still advances when a step's task is approved, not when it finishes.
- A judge-sourced wait reserves no grading margin (only the hub's park does since H464c), so a judge wait that runs to the end of the budget still leaves the run ungraded. It is reachable only with a judge wait probe (owner decision 2).
- The grading margin bounds one run's way back to a sweep, not a queue: with several runs due at once (max_concurrent 1), a parked run can lose the sweep's one slot after its cap.
- A blocked run whose budget runs out is not settled (H464d settles only runs the sweep skips as budget_spent; a blocked one is skipped as blocked and its resume is refused once the owner answers), so it stays blocked on the record.
- The HUD's live wait credit for an open ask runs to now; if the owner then edits the ask, the durable credit falls back to the last sweep that saw it open (at most one sweep's worth).
- An owner stop of a working run is never closed out: request_stop moves it to `stopping` and settles only a second stop (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1436-1438), while ScheduleRuntime.due skips a `stopping` run (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:227-228), so the supervisor that would settle it is never ticked and the run reads `stopping` until the owner stops it again (reproduced on 03643762).

reviews.summary:
Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine [focus] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand.

The command:
- /refine [focus] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:377, registered at agents/core/commands.py:472). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command.
- The focus is one line of at most 200 characters.
- It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list.
- Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. One refusal added since this row's reviews has no wording of its own: a session whose history was imported from another assistant and is still tainted is refused foreign_history_not_promotable before the lease is looked at (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4021-4022), and the command answers it with the generic "The review did not run." line; the guard came with the owner-attested foreign-history resume (commit 8e1775bb), outside this row's claims and tests. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed [… error …] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "[Note: … error", or one a later [1] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3).
- A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:513).
- It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does.

Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4001):
- It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it.
- The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path.
- In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long.
- A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4026). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1).
- A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged.

The learning loop's knobs are declared settings (category learning, agents/core/settings_db.py:347): review_max_tokens (512, 1–32768), review_daily_budget (20, 0–1000), review_cadence (every_turn, every_n_turns, idle_gap), review_every_n (3), review_idle_gap_s (90) and review_max_facts (3), with the defaults the code already used, bounded in _LEARNING_INT_BOUNDS (agents/core/settings_db.py:949). The admin settings API, the HUD and nerva config set can change them; nerva config get shows a number named …max_tokens as the number it is, not masked as a credential, and masks every key the settings store encrypts (the GA4 service-account JSON among them), and nerva config set echoes such a value masked too (review-H465e nit 3). A model id is masked only under a hinted name: llm.default_model shows as typed. Every knob reads within its declared bounds whatever the stored row (a row from before the bounds, restored or hand-edited, reads as the default), the review's model call's token cap included (bounded_learning_int, agents/core/settings_db.py:964). A declared 0 for review_max_facts or review_idle_gap_s is honoured, not read as unset; corrections have a cap of their own (3), so a review_max_facts of 0 keeps no facts, still records corrections, and /refine says what it found but did not keep (_number, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:293).

BackgroundReviewer.run_on_demand (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:335):
- It skips the cadence gate but spends the daily budget, rolling over at midnight, and refunds it when no review was had (a model down, a cut-off answer, a timeout, a cancellation), on the day the pass spent it (review-H465f nit 1). A budget of 0 means no reviews and /refine says so (reviews_off); 2.5 reads as 2, and a value that is not a number or lies outside 0–1000 (text, infinity, a boolean, a hand-edited -3, a fraction below one) is logged once and 20 used (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:268). A per-turn pass that does not run leaves a DEBUG line naming why. It keeps the strict-local model, and is bounded at REFINE_TIMEOUT_S (150 s, below the lease's 180-second wait); no setting raises it.
- It neither resets nor delays the per-turn cadence. It runs one at a time and never beside a per-turn review: a /refine while a per-turn pass runs is refused busy, and a per-turn pass that would start while /refine runs is skipped, not deferred. The exclusion is taken in run() itself (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:394), so a per-turn pass spawned before the /refine, still waiting on the memory lock, is refused on_demand when it enters. A cancelled review leaves no busy flag.
- Its proposals, approval cards and new skills are labelled refine, not background_review; the label is passed down per pass, never kept on the instance. An injection-flagged correction is not recorded (on both paths). Facts found while living memory is off are counted after the injection scan, and said only to the owner who asked.
- run gains a focus slot in REVIEW_PROMPT ("Focus for this review: …", absent when there is none, so the per-turn prompt is byte-identical) and a context bound, which this path sets to the snapshot's.

Tests: tests/test_h465_refine.py (35 cases), tests/test_h465c_refine_review.py (9, the second review), tests/test_h465d_refine_review.py (31, the third review), tests/test_h465e_refine_review.py (37, the fourth review), tests/test_h465f_refine_review.py (34, the fifth review), tests/test_h465g_refine_review.py (18, the sixth review), tests/test_nerva_cli.py (a token budget shown unmasked), and tests/test_slash_commands.py pins the command in the owner's list. They cover:
- the focus slot and its bound;
- cadence skipped while the budget is spent, and the day's rollover;
- one review at a time, and facts written;
- the snapshot's bound, order, cutting and junk;
- a whole snapshot reaching the prompt;
- the reviewer receiving this session's snapshot while the session stays unchanged;
- busy while another turn holds the lease, and not busy inside the command's own lease;
- the empty and unavailable cases;
- the owner-only command and its report, each named refusal, and /help;
- the review's cases: a degraded reply is no review and costs no budget; the timeout; a cancelled review; mutual exclusion and the cadence kept; facts found with living memory off; an injected correction; the refine label; commands left out and contiguity; a chat of commands only; a refusal keeping the last result; the focus cut and where a new skill waits; a guest told /refine is the owner's.

Mutation: 20 mutants; 18 were caught at once, and the other two after cases were added (the snapshot's bound reaching the prompt, the day rollover). Independent #1233 review (historical scope): Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine [focus] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand.

The command:
- /refine [focus] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:377, registered at agents/core/commands.py:472). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command.
- The focus is one line of at most 200 characters.
- It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list.
- Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed [… error …] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "[Note: … error", or one a later [1] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3).
- A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:513).
- It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does.

Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4001):
- It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it.
- The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path.
- In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long.
- A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4026). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1).
- A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged.

The learning loop's knobs are declared settings (category learning, agents/core/settings_db.py:348): review_max_tokens (512, 1–32768), review_daily_budget (20, 0–1000), review_cadence (every_turn, every_n_turns, idle_gap), review_every_n (3), review_idle_gap_s (90) and review_max_facts (3), with the defaults the code already used, bounded in _LEARNING_INT_BOUNDS (agents/core/settings_db.py:949). The admin settings API, the HUD and nerva config set can change them; nerva config get shows a number named …max_tokens as the number it is, not masked as a credential, and masks every key the settings store encrypts (the GA4 service-account JSON among them), and nerva config set echoes such a value masked too (review-H465e nit 3). A model id is masked only under a hinted name: llm.default_model shows as typed. Every knob reads within its declared bounds whatever the stored row (a row from before the bounds, restored or hand-edited, reads as the default), the review's model call's token cap included (bounded_learning_int, agents/core/settings_db.py:964). A declared 0 for review_max_facts or review_idle_gap_s is honoured, not read as unset; corrections have a cap of their own (3), so a review_max_facts of 0 keeps no facts, still records corrections, and /refine says what it found but did not keep (_number, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:293).

BackgroundReviewer.run_on_demand (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:335):
- It skips the cadence gate but spends the daily budget, rolling over at midnight, and refunds it when no review was had (a model down, a cut-off answer, a timeout, a cancellation), on the day the pass spent it (review-H465f nit 1). A budget of 0 means no reviews and /refine says so (reviews_off); 2.5 reads as 2, and a value that is not a number or lies outside 0–1000 (text, infinity, a boolean, a hand-edited -3, a fraction below one) is logged once and 20 used (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:268). A per-turn pass that does not run leaves a DEBUG line naming why. It keeps the strict-local model, and is bounded at REFINE_TIMEOUT_S (150 s, below the lease's 180-second wait); no setting raises it.
- It neither resets nor delays the per-turn cadence. It runs one at a time and never beside a per-turn review: a /refine while a per-turn pass runs is refused busy, and a per-turn pass that would start while /refine runs is skipped, not deferred. The exclusion is taken in run() itself (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:394), so a per-turn pass spawned before the /refine, still waiting on the memory lock, is refused on_demand when it enters. A cancelled review leaves no busy flag.
- Its proposals, approval cards and new skills are labelled refine, not background_review; the label is passed down per pass, never kept on the instance. An injection-flagged correction is not recorded (on both paths). Facts found while living memory is off are counted after the injection scan, and said only to the owner who asked.
- run gains a focus slot in REVIEW_PROMPT ("Focus for this review: …", absent when there is none, so the per-turn prompt is byte-identical) and a context bound, which this path sets to the snapshot's.

With llm.kanban on (agents/core/routers/kanban.py:28-30) the owner's chat model gets the board tools (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1580, agents/core/kanban/runtime.py:76), whose profiles are the orchestrator's agents; kanban_create is described for exactly this, creating child tasks with assignees linked through `parents` (agents/core/kanban/schemas.py:392-400). tests/test_hermes_kanban_tools_port.py:47 drives kanban_create over the real RPC. The ported specify and decompose routes answer unavailable (agents/core/kanban/dashboard_api.py:923-931) and the CLI refuses them as unbound (agents/core/kanban/cli.py:60-63), so no auxiliary model rewrites a triage card into a spec, decomposes it with description-based routing, or auto-decomposes on dispatcher passes.
reviews.remaining:
- Specify: an auxiliary model rewrites a triage card into an actionable spec and promotes it out of triage.
- Decompose: split a triage card into linked children routed to the agent whose description fits, falling back to single promotion when fan-out is not worth it.
- Auto-decompose a bounded number of triage cards per dispatcher pass, under Nerva's planner clamps.
- Tests pinning parent-linked child creation and routing.

reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (ff8641a7): The graph primitives a swarm is built from are reachable: kanban tasks, dependency links (agents/core/kanban/dashboard_api.py:323) and comments, plus the dispatcher, so an owner can lay out workers, a verifier and a synthesizer by hand. The one-command `kanban swarm` is refused as unbound (agents/core/kanban/cli.py:61). /api/swarm is a read-only cockpit, not a swarm writer (agents/core/routers/swarm.py:1-12). Tests: tests/test_hermes_kanban_cli.py, tests/test_swarm_summary.py.
reviews.remaining:
- Bind `kanban swarm <goal> --worker … --verifier … --synthesizer …` to write the whole shape (completed root, parallel workers, linked verifier, linked synthesizer, blackboard comments) over the existing tables.
- An HTTP/HUD entry point for it.

reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (ff8641a7): The Hermes diagnostics engine is ported: agents/core/kanban/upstream/kanban_diagnostics.py:256 (hallucinated_cards), agents/core/kanban/upstream/kanban_diagnostics.py:370 (repeated_failures), agents/core/kanban/upstream/kanban_diagnostics.py:510 (review_dependency_deadlock) and the other stateless rules return a kind, severity and suggested actions. It is served at GET /api/kanban/diagnostics (agents/core/kanban/dashboard_api.py:597) and `nerva kanban diagnostics` (agents/core/kanban/cli_parser.py:269-274). tests/test_hermes_kanban_cli.py:97 runs it. The suggested actions cannot all be carried out: reclaim answers unavailable (agents/core/kanban/dashboard_api.py:905), and no HUD renders the action buttons.
reviews.remaining:
- A HUD surface that renders each diagnostic's actions as buttons.
- Bind the reclaim action (and reassign with reclaim_first) so the suggested recoveries can actually run.
- Scoped config for the rule thresholds (unbound today).

reviews.summary:
The delivery foundation exists, but it only carries approval decision cards; nothing subscribes a chat to a work item's completion. EscalationRouter (agents/core/autonomy/escalation.py:96) is a governed, allowlisted, contract-bounded multi-channel fan-out. AwayNotifier (escalation.py:142) adds presence-aware routing through OwnerPresence (agents/core/autonomy/presence.py:104). AutonomyWorker._maybe_push (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:1472) pushes under the daily interrupt budget (INTERRUPT_BUDGET_PER_DAY at worker.py:55, InterruptBudget over the attention ledger) and uses is_night_window (worker.py:519). These tests pass: tests/test_h12_11_escalation.py, tests/test_h34_2_presence.py and tests/test_autonomy_worker.py. When a task finishes, the worker transitions it to DONE and audits; the smart terminal branch first attaches a signed completion proof to that one result (worker.py:1860-1865). No listener or subscription fires on terminal task, work-run or mission events. A grep for notify_subscribe, last_event_id and subscription in agents/core/autonomy returns nothing relevant. H487 promotion collateral review (2026-10-02, 42d4678a): the queue diff adds only a private grouped-approval notification outbox and records effects on ordinary grouped withdrawal; the worker diff only drains those effects from approval housekeeping and immediate promotion. The claimed behavior of this row and its other cited source branches are unchanged. Focused H487/grouping/expiry regressions pass; no new capability claim is made for this row. The row's claimed routing, speech, completion or cron behavior is unchanged; 163 focused approval/expiry/broker tests pass. No new capability claim is made for this row. Smart-terminal collateral review (2026-10-03, base 326d21ed): this row retains its prior code verdict. The changed branches add default-off sealed terminal judging, exact live request/actor checks and guardian labels; this row's other producer/consumer branches remain. Focused terminal/queue/judge regressions and all 1884 frontend tests pass. This is offline collateral evidence, not a new capability or live-provider claim. Final smart-terminal correction review (2026-10-03): the new kernel receipt seam is restricted to terminal.exec ordinary ASK in AUTO; unchanged consumers retain their existing call shapes. Typed terminal intake preserves task/session association and machine execution origin. Manual Docker kernel-off behavior is regression-tested. The 725-case focused union passes. Existing verdict and remaining limits are preserved; no live-provider or new-equivalence credit. H485 collateral review (2026-10-03, parent 802b3b4b): complete queue diff inspected. Task3 actuation collateral review (2026-10-03): a smart terminal worker result can now carry a signed completion proof, and a same-turn tool call can await that exact task. reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (9f92d937): The Hermes `project` command tree is ported: create (folders, primary, board, use), list/ls, show, add-folder, remove-folder, rename, set-primary, use, archive, restore and bind-board (agents/core/kanban/cli_upstream/projects_commands.py:21-63), dispatched against a durable per-profile store (agents/core/kanban/cli_upstream/projects_commands.py:231-251). The owner reaches it as `nerva project ...` (agents/cli/nerva.py:132, agents/cli/nerva.py:3767-3775) via POST /api/kanban/projects/command (agents/core/routers/kanban.py:63-65). The store persists folders and the active-project pointer (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:630-640). Cards on a project-bound board inherit the repo worktree and a deterministic branch name (agents/core/kanban/upstream/kanban_db.py:1285-1291, agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:731). The repo-discovery cache is only a table and store functions (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:66-69, agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:678, agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:704): nothing outside tests ever scans for repos, calls record_discovered_repos or reads list_discovered_repos, so no owner surface ever sees a cached discovery. Tests pin the lifecycle, binding and rollback (tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:23), the store and branch naming, with the discovery cache exercised only by direct store calls (tests/test_hermes_kanban_projects.py:264-281), board-to-project inheritance (tests/test_hermes_kanban_board_projects.py:31) and the HTTP path producing a `my-app/` branch on a new card (tests/test_hermes_kanban_surfaces_wiring.py:151-160); 87 tests pass across these four files.
reviews.remaining:
- A repo-discovery scan (bounded to the file roots) that fills the discovered_repos cache through record_discovered_repos/reconcile_discovered_repos_policy; today these have no caller outside tests
- An owner-reachable surface (CLI verb, route or HUD) that runs discovery and lists the cached repos
- Tests that pin discovery through that surface, not only through direct store calls

reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (9f92d937): Local rooms exist: named, persisted multi-agent conversations with history, created and used over /api/rooms (agents/core/routers/rooms.py:20-27, agents/core/routers/rooms.py:62-71), where an @mention routes the message to a member agent (agents/core/routers/rooms.py:87-92; store at agents/core/rooms.py:28-53). Cross-machine intake is A2A: an allowlisted, HMAC-verified peer can submit a task that lands in a pending inbox for owner approval (agents/core/a2a.py:1-15, agents/core/a2a.py:224, agents/core/a2a.py:262). There is no authority gateway with an ordered event log, no replicas or authority takeover, no RoomLinks with scoped grants, no target-side execution policy for remote members, no policy checkpoints, no turn planner and no driver lease.
reviews.remaining:
- Hosted room core: authority gateway with an append-only ordered event log
- Replicas with fenced primitives to take authority when the host dies
- RoomLinks storing routes and scoped grants with re-authorization status in the UI
- Target-side execution policy (toolsets, iteration cap) for remote members' turns
- Policy checkpoints, deterministic turn planner and a single-driver lease
- Tests

reviews.summary: Fresh assessment 2026-10-13 (ff8641a7): Pieces exist on separate surfaces: Idempotency-Key replay for external requests (agents/core/idempotency.py:1-6) on action intake (agents/core/routers/actions.py:57) and webhooks (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:502), tested in tests/test_h659_idempotency.py. Subagent steer and stop live in agents/core/routers/mesh.py:346 and agents/core/routers/mesh.py:358, company runs list/get/stop in agents/core/routers/company.py:80-164, and approval resolution is a separate route. Chat streams SSE (agents/web.py:1513) but declares no idempotency (agents/core/client_protocol.py:198-199). There is still no single run object.
reviews.remaining:
- One run resource: POST returns a run_id (idempotent create), GET polls state, an attachable/detachable SSE /events stream (tool progress, deltas, lifecycle), /stop, /steer and /approval on that same id.
- Jobs over that REST shape and a session-key header that scopes long-term memory separately from the transcript.

2026-10-09 cloud standalone-image continuation: newly approved cloud PNGs now use the committed shared sidecar publisher and ID reservation. The generated-ID download/edit reader checks the expected digest, while local task recovery still independently checks the durable completion SHA. Cloud root safety remains checked before publication and at the final guard; live authority is rechecked immediately before the PNG link. Storage failures retain unknown outcome, governance declines after generation withhold, and machinery/mediation failures retain their existing classifications. Approval configuration binds the actual imported publisher source and refuses source drift. Existing completion/projection/catalog shapes and the single provider dispatch remain intact; restart recovery performs no request. The earlier local-only limit below is superseded for new built-in cloud artifacts; legacy sidecar-free IDs remain unbound on raw reads and no old artifact is backfilled. H477 remains partial. 2026-10-09 standalone local-image continuation: new ComfyUI and local OpenAI PNGs persist a strict expected-digest sidecar. The shared generated-ID reader verifies exactly its returned bytes for downloads and edit references, refusing malformed metadata or mismatch. Cooperating local publishers reserve an ID, refuse existing final names, sync private files, link the sidecar first and recheck authority immediately before the PNG link. Prepublication failure removes only this invocation's sidecar; after PNG publication or an ambiguous link outcome whose identity cannot be established, the binding stays. Directory sync is best effort, and missing sidecars preserve legacy availability without a verified claim. Separate cloud publication does not participate in this reservation; a forced same-ID mixed pair can refuse until reconciled, and deletion of metadata cannot be distinguished from legacy. The existing user guard, response shape and no-replay boundary remain intact. This increment does not close H477. 2026-10-09 local-producer continuation: the shared atomic PNG publisher now returns SHA-256 of its already-validated immutable bytes after successful publication. ComfyUI and local OpenAI image generation pass that producer digest through MediaGenManager to the optional catalog field without opening a result path. New catalog rows from these built-in producers therefore verify on md delivery/export; a same-size different valid PNG is refused. Missing producer hashes preserve legacy catalog calls, while present malformed values including null skip cataloging with the existing generation-success/warning behavior. The seven-file focused union passes 189 cases using offline actual-backend fixtures. Typed task artifact views and raw download enforcement remain unchanged; raw producer output gains the additive digest. This does not bind old rows or arbitrary legacy producers. 2026-10-09 expected-digest continuation: new cloud-completion catalog rows carry their verified completion SHA-256. Catalog delivery/export freezes one selected row for path and expected digest, reads bounded MIME-valid bytes and refuses a mismatch; exports mark bound rows verified and legacy rows unbound. Strict optional-field validation rejects malformed stored/supplied hashes. Stable-ID retries retain the existing row without silent hash migration or removal. No new network dispatch, ownership boundary or local-producer binding is added. The 180-case focused union covers signed cloud completion, tampering, recovery, stable identity, export and legacy behavior; broad row equivalence remains unclaimed. 2026-10-09 bounded discovery continuation: GET /v1/capabilities now exposes descriptor_schema=1 for the five mounted chat/session operations, their auth tiers, request/response schemas and runtime SSE media, session selection/resume semantics and the absence of POST keyed replay. Referenced component schemas resolve inside the descriptor. It separates server release from protocol_version=null and links existing readiness; no readiness probe, model/provider override or remote authority is added. Legacy GET /v1 remains HTML. Auth text describes the actual tier-specific credential predicate, including the revoke-without-sentinel restart residual and admin-only remote user-route restriction. DELETE permits orphaned-outcome cleanup with nullable backup. This supersedes the prior statement that no API contract descriptor exists, only for this narrow chat/session scope. Existing stale evidence outside the reviewed descriptor delta is deliberately not restamped; the whole row still needs broader re-review. The historical assessment below keeps its original scope and test dates.

H477 re-reviewed against live code on 2026-09-18; the inherited 2026-09-07 "missing" verdict is wrong and last night's "already equivalent" triage is also wrong. Nerva does have a real capability-discovery surface, under /api/* not /v1/*: GET /api/capabilities (agents/core/routers/analytics.py:244, user_guard) returns capability_registry.snapshot() (agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:509), whose build_records() (:480) merges seven sources — _missing_records (:193), _plugin_records (:127), _action_records (:235, every ACTION_CAPABILITY_MANIFESTS kind joined to kernel/registry.ACTION_REGISTRY), _acquired_records (:430), _tool_records (:314), _component_records (:364), _skill_records (:395) — each record carrying inputs/risk/requires/supports/verification/rollback plus a missing→seam→wired→verified→ga readiness state Hermes has no analogue for; GET /api/metrics/capabilities (analytics.py:227) is the open legacy twin. Skills enumerate at GET /skills (routers/skills.py:39) and /skills/imported (:477); tools at GET /api/toolrpc/tools (routers/mesh.py:175, from ToolRPCServer.tools(), tool_rpc.py:424 — a surface the triage missed); health at GET /healthz (routers/ops.py:42) + GET /readyz (:149) + GET /api/health/components (routers/status.py:68) + /status (:79) + /api/status (:113). Outside that scope, four rolled-up children were never checked by the triage and three are absent: no browser-control registration at all (rg over agents/ for browser_control|controller_id|extension_control returns nothing; browser_transport.py is SSRF resolver pinning for in-process Chromium, not an external controller), no platform-event normalization (rg reaction|message_edited over agents/ hits only food-diary prose in agents/frigga/HEARTBEAT.md and agents/frigga/SOUL.md, no code; POST /api/channels/{id}/inbound is message ingress), and no per-request model/provider override (ChatRequest, agents/web.py:1090, is extra="forbid" and takes only agent/reasoning/session_id — the reasoning third of the clause is satisfied via reasoning_scope at web.py:1331, model_routes precedence is not). reviews.summary: `nerva send` trimite un mesaj către o destinație configurată fără apel de model, cu corpul rezolvat ca la Hermes: argumentul MESSAGE, altfel `-f PATH` (`-` citește stdin), altfel ce e legat pe stdin — un terminal nu e citit niciodată, nici cu `-f -`; un stdin închis e eroare de utilizare, nu traceback; se citește cel mult limita plus un caracter, iar un BOM UTF-8 e eliminat. `-s LINE` e un subiect pe o singură linie *imprimabilă* (orice caracter de control sau separator de linie Unicode e refuzat), purtat de ntfy ca titlu nativ — ASCII imprimabil, cel mult 120, refuzat cu motiv în loc să fie trunchiat tacit de adaptor — și de celelalte canale ca prima linie (subiect, linie goală, mesaj — forma Hermes); `-q` nu tipărește nimic la succes; `--list CANAL` filtrează țintele: un nume care nu poate fi canal direct-send e eroare de utilizare decisă offline, iar un canal pe care un hub mai vechi nu-l listează e exit 1 cu ce listează numit; un argument MESSAGE gol înseamnă „fără mesaj” și cade pe `--file`/stdin. Scara de ieșire e declarată în `--help`: 0 trimis · 1 nelivrat (hub-ul a refuzat sau transportul a eșuat) · 2 utilizare · 3 fără hub · 4 neautorizat. Un fișier binar la `-f` e refuzat cu îndrumarea pentru atașamente, fără să-i reflecte octeții; limita de 4.000 de caractere e regula seam-ului (`carried_length`: subiectul contează unde devine prima linie, nu la ntfy) și CLI-ul aplică aceeași regulă înainte de orice cerere; șirurile venite de la hub sau tastate sunt curățate de caractere de control înainte de terminal. `POST /api/channels/send` primește `subject` opțional (o linie, ≤200), iar seam-ul outbound aplică limita la ce se livrează efectiv. Rate-limit-ul și înregistrarea în IntentLog rămân pe drum. O recenzie adversarială independentă a găsit cincisprezece probleme (două majore: două pin-uri existente din `tests/test_nerva_send.py` rupte), toate remediate în același PR, fiecare cu test. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): outbound.py only lets a caller pass an already-read owner chat (the environment still wins), and nerva.py's send path changed only to show the tail of a long --file path in its errors, beside unrelated new verbs; body resolution, subject rules, the 4,000-character seam limit and the exit ladder are unchanged, no MEDIA attachment or platform:chat addressing landed, and the 169 pinned tests pass.
reviews.remaining: Atașamentele `MEDIA:<path>` nu sunt purtate: o rută care citește căi locale și le trimite pe un canal e egress de fișiere și trebuie să ajungă în spatele Action Kernel-ului, cu un director-sursă delimitat, înainte să existe. Cerința structurală „fără gateway pornit” rămâne o divergență documentată: `nerva send` trece prin hub ca să existe IntentLog și rate-limit. Corpurile peste 4.000 de caractere sunt refuzate, nu fragmentate (Hermes fragmentează per platformă). Slack și Discord rămân reply-only (restul H018); email-ul e exclus deliberat. Nu există adresare `platform:chat_id[:thread]` / `platform:#canal` ca la Hermes: `--channel telegram` înseamnă întotdeauna chat-ul owner-ului. Precedența diverge deliberat: la Hermes argumentul câștigă în fața `--file`, aici ambele deodată e eroare de utilizare. Erorile nu au prefixul `hermes send:`. `JobRunner._send` își păstrează propria rezolvare a destinației (lot-ul jobs). Fără probă live pe un canal real din această sesiune: verificarea a fost prin hub fals și prin ChannelManager-ul real cu adaptoare false.

reviews.summary: **The variant-expansion half of the row.** `hardline_match` no longer screens one spelling: the old single-pass body becomes `_scan_one`, and the public function screens the command in every spelling `_detection_variants` yields — as given, unwrapped from a shell wrapper (`_shell_c_payloads`, recursively to `_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH = 2`), and de-obfuscated (intra-word quotes and escapes collapsed, so `mk""fs` reads as `mkfs`), type-preserving so an argv stays an argv. A non-string command is materialised ONCE up front, which fixes a real one-shot-iterator drain that turned `hardline_match(iter(["rm","-rf","/"]))` from a refusal into a miss. The original slice changed nothing in HARDLINE or the contract, so that pass was additive: an 80,000-case differential fuzz against the pre-slice module returned `refusals_cleared_by_slice = 0`. **That invariant no longer describes the module after PR #1177** (re-assessed 2026-09-19 against the diff 1c5054ea→494a13b2): HARDLINE itself changed — `_CMD` and `network_to_shell` now carry a `_PATH_PREFIX`, so a command word and any wrapper in front of it are read by basename (`/sbin/mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda`, `/usr/bin/sudo /sbin/mkfs.ext4`, `curl … | /bin/sh` all refuse where they returned None; `_recursive_root_removal` compares basenames through `_command_name` too, so `['/usr/local/bin/rm','-rf','/']` refuses instead of only the two literal `/bin/rm` spellings) — and #1177 clears refusals in BOTH directions. Two false-positive classes are cleared on purpose (a `case` label; a heredoc body that quotes a catastrophe), and #1177's mechanisms for them ALSO cleared TRUE refusals the pre-#1177 module gave — **both closed by this slice (H481, branch `hermes/h481-cleared-refusals`, 2026-09-22).** `_strip_case_labels` acted on the flat text of any `case…esac` span and its first-label rule fired after any word-initial `in`, so `(echo case in; reboot); echo esac` — which /bin/sh, dash and bash all execute — went `power_cycle`→None, and the `$IFS`-spliced `(echo case in; mkfs.ext4$IFS/dev/sda); echo esac` / `wipefs$IFS-a$IFS/dev/sda` went mkfs/wipefs→None; the strip now fires only inside a real command-position `case WORD in … esac` region (a `case` keyword, confirmed per match by `_in_command_position`), so all three refuse again — and, made symmetric, a single-line `case $1 in wipe) rm -rf / ;; esac` refuses through the segment path too while `case $1 in shutdown) echo bye ;; esac` still does not. `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` looked only LEFT of `<<`, so `cat <<EOF | sh` / `rm -rf /` / `EOF` and `cat <<'EOF' >x.sh; sh x.sh` / `rm -rf /` / `EOF` went `recursive_root_removal`→None although both hand the body to a shell that runs it; it now also reads the heredoc's own pipeline stages AFTER the redirection and a file the body is written to that a shell later runs, so those refuse, while `bash <<EOF` and a heredoc written to a plain file (`cat > README.md <<'EOF'`) are unchanged. Each shape was reproduced against /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash first (harmless `echo RAN` stand-ins) and pinned red-first. **An independent review of that closure found nine items — three blocking, three major, two minor, one nit — and all nine are fixed in the same branch, each reproduced against the three shells first:** (1) the rewritten `_heredoc_feeds_a_shell` counted a shell UPSTREAM of the heredoc's pipe stage (`bash -c echo | cat <<EOF` was `power_cycle` although every shell prints the literal body); (2) it took ANY word of a later shell statement as the run file (`cat > x.yaml <<'EOF'` / `shutdown: graceful` / `EOF` / `bash run.sh x.yaml` was `power_cycle` — the exact config case the heredoc-as-data rule exists for); (3) it read an `xargs`-reached shell as a consumer (`cat <<EOF | xargs -I{} sh -c 'rm -f {}'` with a `reboot.log` line was `power_cycle`; xargs hands lines to the shell as arguments); (4) `_in_command_position` read the compact `if true;then case $1 in` as the word `true;then`, skipped the strip and refused the label (`;then case` / `;do case` were `power_cycle`, label-only in every shell); (5) the new `_CASE_BLOCK_RE` (`\bcase\s+WORD\s+.*?\bin\b.*?\besac\b`) was super-linear on ordinary prose — 4000 chars of case/in prose 10 → 531 ms, eight argv items of it 0.28 → 128 s; (6) the redirect-target branch re-tokenised every later line for every heredoc — 400 `cat <<E >x` blocks in 4000 chars 25 → 2,471 ms, 33.6 KB 109 ms → 97.5 s; the first pass's '78.7 → 78.4 ms' held only for input with no `case` word and never entered that branch; (7) the named-shell file-exec claim was overstated: `(sh x.sh)`, `{ sh x.sh; }`, `if true; then sh x.sh; fi`, `cat x.sh | sh`, `sh -c '. x.sh'`, `. x.sh`, `source x.sh`, `tee x.sh <<EOF; sh x.sh` and a quoted `> "x.sh"` target all ran the body and returned None; (8) this row still said 'eleven across two reviews'; (9) the report said 11 items were red before the fix when 12 were, and the `case WORD in` tightening was pinned by nothing. Fixes: the consumer test looks only at the heredoc's own stage and the stages downstream of it, and a stage counts only when its shell reads its stdin as the script (`_interpreter_call`: a `-c` line, a file operand and an `xargs`-reached shell are data — unless the `-c` line itself launches a stdin-reading shell, so `bash -c sh <<EOF`, `sh -c 'eval "$(cat)"' <<EOF` and `sh -c '. /dev/stdin' <<EOF` still refuse, verified); the file test looks only at the operand a shell RUNS (`_script_runs`: `sh x`, `. x`, `source x`, the same behind `(`/`{`/`then`, a file piped into a stdin-reading shell, a `-c` line that runs it), collects `tee` operands and quoted targets, and the statement lines after a heredoc are tokenised once, lazily, shared across heredocs and decided last heredoc first; the `case` region is found by three single-purpose searches (`case WORD `, then the first `in`, then the first `esac`), each starting where the last stopped, and the keyword-before test accepts the compact `;then`/`;do`. A 671,995-case differential fuzz against origin/main (the suite's 275 pinned literals recombined with 14 statement prefixes, 10 suffixes, 17 heredoc heads, 13 pipe tails, 4 upstream stages, 18 same-line and 10 later-line follow-ups, plus 60,000 seeded-random recombinations) returns refusals_added = 55,059 and refusals_cleared = 22,304 — so the first pass's 'refusals_cleared = 0' is withdrawn, not restated. Every cleared case is explained by one of the two changed mechanisms and belongs to a class no shell executes, each verified with `echo RAN` stand-ins: 19,311 by the consumer rule — a heredoc redirected into a shell that carries its own script or `-c` line, or into `xargs sh` (`sh -c cat <<EOF`, `bash run.sh <<EOF`; main refused both, every shell prints the body) — and 2,993 by the command-position rule — `case` used as an ARGUMENT followed by `label) …` (`echo case $1 in`, `x=1 case …`, `sudo case …`: a parse error in every shell) or a `case … esac` quoted inside heredoc DATA, where main's unconditional strip put a `;` in place of `in label)` and so invented a command position the shell does not have (disabling main's strip makes every one of them None on main too). Every added refusal is explained by the same two mechanisms (33,619 consumer, 21,434 command position, 6 in garbage recombinations with unbalanced quotes reached through the de-obfuscated variant) and adds an executing shape of the kind pinned in the tests. Two false refusals main had are therefore cleared on purpose and pinned as such (`sh -c cat <<EOF`, `bash run.sh <<EOF`). The cleared classes are still cleared on purpose: a `case` label (`case $1 in shutdown) echo bye ;; esac` was `power_cycle`; `_strip_case_labels` drops the pattern inside `case … esac` while keeping the branch body a command position, so `case $1 in wipe) rm -rf / ;; esac` still refuses) and a heredoc body that merely quotes a catastrophe (`cat > README.md <<'EOF'` / `rm -rf / will destroy the box` / `EOF` was `recursive_root_removal` because `segments` ignored the body flag `text` honoured; a body line is now narrowed to its `$()`/backtick substitutions via `_substituted`, so `cat <<EOF` / `$(rm -rf /)` / `EOF` still refuses). **An independent review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed here, and every one was reproduced against a real shell first.** **(1)** The payload was taken as the token immediately after the first `-c`-shaped flag, and the search then stopped — but a shell keeps parsing options until the first non-option operand. `/bin/sh -c -x 'echo RAN'` runs, and `sh -c -x 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'`, `sh -c -- 'rm -rf /'`, `sh -c -e …`, `sh -c -u …` and `sudo sh -c -- 'wipefs -a /dev/sda'` all returned None. One decoy character defeated the entire mechanism, reachable end to end at the transport's spawn seam. The scan steps over options to the first operand now, `--` included. **(2)** A `sh -c` payload is a shell SCRIPT, and a newline separates statements exactly as `;` does — but the newline was squeezed into a space before segmentation, so nothing ever occupied a command position on line 2 and `sh -c 'echo hi` + newline + `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'` passed the floor. **Pressing Enter was the bypass.** Unquoted newlines are separators now, quote-aware so a newline inside a string literal stays data and ordinary prose is not screened as a command. #1177 closed the way that screening could be switched off again: any `<<` opened a heredoc and an unmatched delimiter swallowed every following line as body, so `grep "<<<<<<< HEAD" src/x.py` + newline + `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` returned None; `_heredoc_open` is now quote- and `$(( ))`-aware, skips `<<<` here-strings, and a delimiter that never comes back opens nothing. **(3)** `_CMD`'s command-position anchor learned four more shapes a shell steps over, each a live miss: a brace group (`{ mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda; }`), a compound-command keyword (`if true; then mkfs.ext4 …`), an assignment prefix (`FOO=1 mkfs.ext4 …`) and `env FOO=1 mkfs.ext4 …` — and, with #1177, a fifth: a directory prefix on the command word or on any wrapper before it, spelled as deterministic `component/` chunks with `=` excluded so `FOO=/sbin/mkfs.ext4` stays an assignment and `echo /sbin/mkfs.ext4` stays an argument. **(4)** `busybox` was named as a shell but not as a command-position wrapper, so `busybox mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda` — the standard shape on exactly the container targets this module says it keeps the floor on — walked straight through. Four documentation claims were corrected rather than left standing, including the one that said the known-gap list was complete (the first review found five entries missing from it; #1177's second review found six more — a re-expansion budget filled with decoys, a path in front of the command word, a `<<` that opens no heredoc, a heredoc a shell reads as a script, a heredoc body screened as argv, and a `case` label — so the docstring now says twenty-two across four reviews) and the one that said an over-matched flag shape can never clear a refusal (it could: `powershell /c -Command Stop-Computer` returned None where `powershell -Command Stop-Computer` refused — fixed by the same change as (1)). A test whose NAME promised a bound on work it never measured was renamed to what it actually pins, which is the opposite: that depth-3 nesting is a deliberate miss (`test_nesting_past_the_depth_cap_is_a_miss_and_that_is_the_pin`, still present and green). **#1177 also removed the only breadth cap:** `_MAX_SHELL_EXPANSIONS = 8` bounded how many level-1 payloads were unwrapped again, in encounter order — an order the caller writes — so eight cheap `sh -c ok;` decoys in front of `sh -c "sh -c 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'"` returned None where seven refused, and padding a payload past `MAX_ARG_CHARS` had the same effect; every payload is now re-expanded and `_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH` is the only cap, with breadth bounded by the fact that each level's payloads are disjoint substrings of the level above. reviews.summary: The logging half of the row, and only that half. `agents/core/security/log_redaction.py` adds `SecretRedactionFilter`, a `logging.Filter` that runs every record's message and its `args` through `SecretScanner.redact` before a handler can write it. The enable flag is snapshotted at import, so an agent-authored mid-session write to `JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION` cannot turn it off — Hermes's `_REDACT_ENABLED` rule, ported deliberately. A cheap length/substring pre-check runs before any regex (≈8.75 µs per clean record, ~1.9× faster than the full scan; the builder's report said 17.22 µs and ~2.1×, which did not reproduce and is corrected here). `setup_logging()` installs it. **Two majors found by an independent review and fixed before landing:** the module's own docstring tripped the AUD-14 raw-env-read ratchet — the prose contained a literal `os.environ[...]` subscript and the ratchet greps file text line by line, so `tests/test_o26_p2_env_config.py` was RED in the delivered tree; and `install_log_redaction()` walked only the root logger's handlers, while `uvicorn` and `uvicorn.access` set `propagate=False` and own theirs, so the production HTTP server's own access and error logs — the ones that carry an `Authorization` header — were structurally unreachable. `install_log_redaction_everywhere()` now covers every handler owned by any logger in `logging.Logger.manager`, and a test drives a real uvicorn `dictConfig` and asserts a key in an access line is masked. Three minors fixed with it: the length floor was defeated by an extra pattern whose NAME collided with a built-in (it now matches by regex SHAPE, one-to-one, and fails closed on any mismatch); an ordinary `%`-format bug was being swallowed into a bare `[redaction-unavailable]` instead of logging's loud diagnostic (now `[log-format-error]` with the message, args and exception, all scanned first); and the test fixture destroyed an ambient `JARVIS_LOG_FILE` for the rest of the session. 47 tests, each fix red-proofed by neutering it. **Follow-up in the same PR:** the blocking bandit gate flagged both swallowed exceptions as NEW findings. Only the filter's last-ditch blank was suppressed (`# nosec B110`, with its reason); `_cover`'s per-handler swallow became a counted, warned coverage figure and `_managed_loggers`' registry-walk failure became a warning, closing the gap this row disclosed. 52 tests at landing. **#1177 (2026-09-19) closed a log-integrity hole inside this same control, re-assessed here rather than refreshed:** the in-place path used to give up and flatten the record to `msg`/`()` whenever a secret straddled the boundary between the format string and an argument ("correctness beats shape"), and flattening is exactly what DELETES a uvicorn access line — `AccessFormatter` unpacks five `record.args`, raises on an empty tuple, and `Handler.handleError` swallows it. `password_assignment`'s `\s*[=:]\s*` jumps the space uvicorn's `'%s - "%s %s HTTP/%s" %d'` puts between the request path and `HTTP/`, so `/login?pwd=` is inert on its own — 11 characters, so the 10-char floor does not even apply; `password_assignment` needs at least six unquoted (four quoted) non-space characters after the separator and the bare argument has none — and a match once rendered: any unauthenticated client could erase its own access-log entry by appending `?pwd=` to a path. `SecretRedactionFilter._mask_joined_args` now replaces whole arguments — one at a time first, then cumulatively for a secret assembled from several — the cumulative pass can also mask an innocent argument that sits between two culprits (`"%s HTTP/%s and %s HTTP/%s"` with two `?pwd=` paths loses the `1.1` between them): over-redaction, never a leak, and the arity still holds — — until the re-rendered line is scanner-clean, keeping the tuple's arity, putting an argument back when its conversion refuses the mask (uvicorn's `%d` status code stays an int), and naming the mask after the pattern the scanner reports, `[REDACTED:straddling_secret]` when it cannot. Flattening survives only for a straddle no masking can clean, i.e. the secret sits in the format string itself (`pwd=%s`). Seven tests were added — four of them through uvicorn's real `dictConfig` plus `setup_logging()`, asserting the access line for `/login?pwd=`, `/admin?password=`, `/x?passwd:` and `/z?api_key="12345678` survives with the straddling text gone (three are `password_assignment` straddles; `/z?api_key="12345678` is `generic_api_key` matching `api_key="12345678 HTTP/1.1"`, the access line's own closing quote completing the quoted value) and the client, verb and status kept — and the earlier straddle test was inverted to assert `args == ("[REDACTED:anthropic_key]",)` instead of `()`. `agents/core/log.py` did not change and still installs the filter from `setup_logging()`. `tests/test_log_redaction.py` collects 64 tests, all green on 2026-09-19. Nothing in #1177 touches the other six paths the row names; the still-owed list below stands.
reviews.remaining: This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies `redact.py` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a `cat .env` from `terminal_run` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning `[redaction-unavailable]` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID `«redacted:ghp_…»` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), `code_file=True` sparing source constants, `_mask_control_split_tokens()` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared `.env` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose `addFilter` fails is counted and published through `uncovered_handler_count()` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a `loggerDict` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (`# nosec B110`), where a `logging.Filter` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. `install_log_redaction()` remains exported although the `everywhere` variant is what production uses. **A later slice's full-suite run surfaced one more thing about this control, recorded here rather than fixed:** the scanner's `high_entropy_secret` pattern matches an ordinary filesystem path. Under `-n auto --dist loadfile` a warning naming a pytest tmp file arrived as `truncated: [REDACTED:high_entropy_secret].md`, which is what a real operator would see when a log line names a file with a long random-looking segment — a debuggability cost the module docstring already warns about in general terms, now with a concrete case. Separately, `setup_logging()` installs the filter on every handler of every logger and nothing took it back off, so every later test on the same xdist worker ran under a live redactor. The installer is PRODUCTION code, not the tests: `agents/run.py` calls `setup_logging()` at module level, so importing it installs the filter during pytest COLLECTION — before any fixture runs — and eight test files import it; `agents/web.py` calls it from the FastAPI lifespan, so any test that drives the app installs it again; five test files call it directly on top of that. There is no list of leaking files to fix. The cleanup therefore lives in `tests/conftest.py` as an autouse fixture that strips unconditionally BEFORE each test as well as after — a snapshot-and-restore fixture, which is what the two neighbouring isolation fixtures do and what this was first written as, treats a collection-time install as pre-existing and preserves it for the life of the worker. That version went green locally and RED in CI on exactly the test it was meant to fix. The first attempt at it matched by `isinstance` and silently did nothing: `agents/` is on `sys.path`, so `core.security.log_redaction` and `agents.core.security.log_redaction` are two module objects over this one file with two distinct `SecretRedactionFilter` classes, and the root handler was carrying the other one. The match is by class name now, and four paired tests pin both halves — including the alternate import path, which is the case the first attempt missed.
