reviews.summary: **Gap (a) of four, plus the row's `chmod 0600 atomic writes` clause.** Both pairing credentials stop being written in the clear: `SenderPairing._code` becomes `_code_hash`, and each deeplink entry moves from being keyed by its raw token to being keyed by an opaque 8-byte id with the token's salted digest inside the entry. Verification hashes the candidate and `hmac.compare_digest`s two fixed-length hex digests, so neither the length nor any prefix of the stored credential leaks and the deeplink failure reasons stay indistinguishable. A one-time migration accepts a pre-H497 plaintext file, rehashes it in memory and rewrites it, preserving each link's channel, `created_at` and `expires_at` — an upgrade never locks the owner out nor resurrects a spent link (since H689 a migrated link that carries no install id is refused as other_install, so the owner mints a fresh identity-bound link instead). `_digest` encodes with `surrogatepass` so a lone surrogate (from a hand-edited store, or from the body of the one pairing route a stranger is meant to reach) misses instead of raising. `atomic_write_json` lands every JsonStore file owner-only. **The review found three false claims and all three are corrected — two of them by changing the code rather than the prose.** (1) The module docstring said the store "holds nothing that can pair anybody". True of a 192-bit deeplink token; **false of the pairing code**, which is whatever the owner typed: a four-digit code was recovered from the file by exhausting 10,000 candidates in **0.006 s** and then used to pair. The code is now stretched with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 240,000 rounds, `kdf` and `rounds` stored beside each digest so raising the count later cannot lock an owner out, and a record written by the first cut is upgraded in place on the next successful pair — the one moment the plaintext is in hand — while a FAILED guess leaves it untouched. The deeplink token stays on plain SHA-256, deliberately: `redeem_deeplink` hashes once per outstanding link, so a slow hash there is a CPU lever for any stranger sending `/start junk`, and at 192 bits there is nothing for stretching to buy. (2) The salt comment defended leaving the code unstretched by pointing at the store-wide guess budget — an ONLINE control held in memory, which has no bearing on an attacker who has read the file, the exact threat at-rest hashing answers. Rewritten to say what stretching does and does not promise. (3) `atomic_write_json` claimed its chmod-before-replace ordering left no readable window. It left a shorter one: `write_text` creates the tmp at `0o666 & ~umask` and the whole payload is in it before the chmod runs. The tmp is now created EMPTY through a descriptor opened 0600 and closed again (json_store.py:74) before the unchanged `Path.write_text` call at json_store.py:78 opens that existing file — a mode `write_text` leaves alone — so no byte of a pairing digest ever lands in a file whose mode the umask chose; pinned by a test that neutralises `os.chmod` and still requires 0600. **#1179 (adversarial wave two) touched only this row's test file; `pairing.py` and `json_store.py` are byte-identical to the #1171 state.** The review claimed every inbound `/start` costs 240k rounds outside any budget. It does not, for two reasons worth keeping apart. First, `/start` never reaches the code KDF at all: a Telegram `/start <payload>` is routed by `TelegramChannel._maybe_pair_deeplink` (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1500-1538) to `redeem_deeplink`, which is one plain-SHA-256 `_digest` per outstanding link, and every other chat message reaches `gate_inbound` through `ChannelGateway.route` with `code=kwargs.get("pairing_code")` (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:92), a kwarg no channel in the tree ever sets — so the one path on which a stranger can spend a KDF run is `POST /api/channels/pairing/request`, the route the new test's docstring names (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:472). Second, on that path the KDF sits behind a budget: `_code_guess_budget_spent` (pairing.py:606) is store-wide and is consulted at pairing.py:587, BEFORE `_code_matches` at pairing.py:592, so a stranger rotating sender ids — the per-sender bucket is keyed on an id the caller chose — buys at most `_MAX_CODE_GUESSES_PER_WINDOW` = 10 KDF runs per 10-minute window however many ids they present, and a request presenting no code never reaches the KDF at all. `test_the_kdf_a_stranger_can_trigger_stays_inside_the_guess_budget` (tests/test_pairing_secrets_at_rest.py:469) now pins that by counting `_stretch` calls rather than timing them, so a slow CI box cannot fail it: 60 requests from 60 fresh ids → 10 runs with 50 turned away `rate_limited` (with the budget check removed it is 60 runs and 0 refusals — re-reproduced at this re-verification), and zero runs for a code-less request. That is the code-side counterpart of the deeplink decision above — the token stays unstretched because nothing budgets `redeem_deeplink`'s per-link compare; the code may be stretched because its compare sits behind one. Nothing in #1179's persona-scan (`agent.py`, `quarantine.py`) or MCP-stdio (`mcp/client.py`) work touches this row. **Second slice (2026-09-22) — one store per process, and the one-use claim made true for the deeplink path.** The module promised a deeplink is "one use, ever", and inside one instance it was; production held two. The orchestrator registers the long-lived `sender_pairing` (the gateway gates on it, the pairing router mints and revokes on it) and `TelegramChannel` was built in `web.py` without one, so `_maybe_pair_deeplink` opened a throwaway `SenderPairing()` per `/start <token>`. A `JsonStore` reads its file once and every save writes the whole in-memory state back, so the two were two stores, not two views of one: a token redeemed over Telegram was spent in the throwaway and still outstanding in the orchestrator's copy, whose next save — any save; a stranger knocking is enough — wrote it back to disk, where the next throwaway redeemed it again and paired a second sender. With a relocated data root the two did not even share a file (the registry spelled a cwd-relative `memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`, the throwaway used `data_path(...)`), so under `JARVIS_HOME` no link ever redeemed. Fixed by wiring, not by hardening the store: `TelegramChannel` takes `pairing=` and `web.py` passes `gateway.pairing`, the same object by identity; an adapter handed nothing refuses to pair rather than building one (same reply as a bad token, a warning naming the cause, the message still swallowed); the registry entry spells the path through `data_path("sender_pairing.json")`. Five tests in `tests/test_telegram_pairing_shared_store.py` pin the resurrection with two instances over one file as the premise, a spent link staying spent after the owner's store saves, `revoke_deeplinks()` reaching the live adapter, an un-wired channel building nothing, and the real lifespan handing the channel `orch.sender_pairing` under the data root; red-proofed against the unpatched sources. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): diffed pairing.py, gateway.py and web.py since 92c3eeb3, telegram.py since 4b7714f9 and the two drifted tests since their pinned merges; the code hashing and PBKDF2 stretching, the store-wide guess budget before the KDF, the 0600 temp file and the shared store handed to Telegram and Discord are unchanged, minting now refuses without an install identity and redemption refuses a link with no hub id, the gateway adds a pending-reply route that still checks pairing for workspace channels, citations were moved to their HEAD lines, the remaining text was corrected because the owner/user command split already exists (only whoami is missing), commands.py and its test were pinned, no lockout or generated code landed, and the 79 pinned tests pass.
reviews.remaining: **The row names four hardening gaps; (a) is closed, (c) is closed for the deeplink path, (b) is open and (d) is half closed.** (c) *revocation reaching live adapters*: `revoke_deeplinks()` and `unpair()` now act on the one object the Telegram adapter redeems from and the gateway consults on every message, so there is no second copy for a link or an approval to survive in — pinned by `test_revoking_on_the_shared_store_reaches_the_live_telegram_adapter`. Slack and Discord have no deeplink path and gate through the same gateway instance. Still outstanding, from the row itself: (b) *no lockout after N failed attempts* — the row wants a 1 h lockout after 5 failed approvals, checked BEFORE the pending lookup so a code already in flight cannot be brute-forced past it; there is still only a rate limit and an in-memory guess budget, both of which reset on restart. (d) is half closed: the chat command registry does split owner and user tiers on channels — `_channel_principal` makes only a configured owner sender an admin principal and every ADMIN-tier command refuses anyone else with "owner command" (agents/core/commands.py:159-165) — so a paired stranger gets only the user-tier commands; still missing is the always-allowed floor's `whoami` (no such command exists), so the row's `{help, whoami}` floor is not met. **Unaddressed from the Hermes column:** pairing-code GENERATION (8 characters from a 32-char unambiguous alphabet via `secrets.choice`) and the code's 1 h TTL — the code here never expires; "max 3 pending per platform" (the store bounds 200 globally); "1 request per user per 10 min" (it is 5); `unauthorized_dm_behavior` treating inbox-shaped platforms differently from chat-shaped ones; and the ordered authorization union (allow-all flag → pairing approvals → per-platform allowlist → global allowlist → global allow-all → default DENY), which is still an ad-hoc sequence in `is_allowed`/`gate_inbound`. **Two honest limits of the second slice.** The store itself still has no defence against a second instance — the guarantee is one instance per process by construction, and the premise test says so in words. And an install that had relocated its data root (`JARVIS_HOME`) and paired senders through the HUD kept them in `<cwd>/memory_logs/sender_pairing.json`; the store now opens under the data root, so those senders are held once more until re-approved (the owner's allowlisted ids never lived in that file and are unaffected). **And the limit carried from the first slice.** Stretching is a work factor, not a wall: a four-digit code goes from milliseconds to minutes, an eight-character mixed-alphabet code becomes infeasible, and **nothing enforces a floor on what the owner types** — `PairingCodeBody` caps the length at 128 and sets no minimum — while generating the code for them, the row's own prescription, is not implemented.

reviews.summary:
Nerva now warns about a dangerous host posture, as Hermes does, on top of a network half that was already stronger. assert_safe_bind (agents/core/boot_guards.py) still refuses an unauthenticated non-loopback bind and prints the exact env vars that fix it, and GET /api/security/posture still reports the secrets backend, skill signing, sandbox isolation and guardrails honestly. agents/core/host_posture.py adds the host half: three read-only checks that never block and never change anything, each answering ok, warn or unknown (it could not tell, never a false green), with a reason, what it saw and the fix. check_root (agents/core/host_posture.py:71) warns when the process runs as root (euid 0) on any host, headless included, or elevated on Windows (IsUserAnAdmin). check_sshd (agents/core/host_posture.py:168) reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config the way sshd does (_SshdScan, agents/core/host_posture.py:120): Include files are read in place, relative paths from /etc/ssh, each pattern's hits in lexical order, at most 16 deep; Keyword value, Keyword=value and trailing comments are accepted and keywords and values are case-insensitive; the first PasswordAuthentication outside a Match block wins, so a drop-in Included at the top overrides the main file; a Match block (to the end of its file, an Include inside it conditional) never sets the global value but a Match block that turns passwords on warns too; an absent directive is the sshd default yes and warns; no sshd_config is ok; an unreadable file is unknown unless the answer was read elsewhere; an unrecognised value is unknown. check_container_storage (agents/core/host_posture.py:241) detects a container (/.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, or a docker, kubepods, containerd, libpod or lxc cgroup of PID 1, in_container) and then finds the mount the data root (resolved through symlinks) lives on in /proc/self/mountinfo (parse_mountinfo with its octal escapes, mount_of taking the longest containing mount point and the later of two stacked mounts): the container's own root filesystem or a tmpfs warns, a volume or bind mount is ok, no mountinfo or no mount is unknown. run_checks and report (agents/core/host_posture.py:273, :287) run the three independently, a failing check becoming an unknown row. The hub logs each warning once per process at start, after logging is set up, off the event loop (log_startup, agents/web.py lifespan). GET /api/security/posture (admin) gains host: the three findings and a warnings count (agents/core/routers/security.py). python scripts/doctor.py and nerva doctor show them as the advisory rows host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords and container_storage at the end of the report: a warning is warn with the fix and never fails the verdict, a check that could not tell or could not run is skip, never ok (check_host_posture, scripts/doctor.py:247). The module is stdlib only so the doctor can use it on a broken install. The shipped Dockerfile has no USER, so a stock container now shows the root warning; running the image as a non-root user is left to the deploy. Tests: tests/test_h501_host_posture.py (42), with real sshd_config trees in a temporary directory (drop-ins read first and last, lexical order, absolute and quoted Includes, Match blocks in the main and in an included file, a trailing comment naming a file, an Include loop) and real mountinfo text. 55 mutants: 53 killed after five cases were added; the other two were dead code, removed.

Re-read 2026-10-10 after two pinned files drifted. The mechanism files (agents/core/host_posture.py, agents/core/boot_guards.py, scripts/doctor.py, tests/test_h501_host_posture.py) hold their pins and every citation above resolves unchanged. agents/core/routers/security.py changed by one hunk that widens DataHandlingAck.target with the video roles; the posture route still returns the host findings (agents/core/routers/security.py:396). agents/web.py changed by auth-event auditing, channel pending handlers and ntfy opt-in hunks, none of which mention the posture checks; the startup warning is still logged off the event loop (agents/web.py:497). tests/test_h501_host_posture.py passes (42) and the full backend suite is green on this head. Verdict unchanged.

**`JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE` flips from opt-in to default-on**, so a spawned stdio MCP server is handed the `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` baseline plus its own `env` instead of `os.environ.copy()` — API keys, tokens, proxies and every `JARVIS_*` setting withheld. A second flag, `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV`, is the owner-reachable migration remedy: a comma-separated list of host variable names that pass the baseline even when `_SECRET_LIKE` matches them. `_merged_env()` emits one INFO line per connect counting host values the child does not receive, carrying **no variable name and no value**. `GET /api/admin/mcp` rows gain `env_baseline`. And Nerva's own WorldView MCP server is handed its `WORLDVIEW_API_URL`, which the flip would otherwise have silently replaced with the built-in `http://localhost:4000`. **The review found two blocking majors and four false claims; all six are addressed.** **(1)** `routers/mcp.py` asserted an invariant the code did not hold: the comment said a row that spawns no subprocess reports `None` "rather than a badge it has not earned" and enumerated two cases. A third exists and is the only one an owner can create today — `POST /api/admin/mcp` does no command validation, so a row with a whitespace-only command or a shell metacharacter persists, and `connect()` answers `unsafe_command` from `_command_argv()` **before** `create_subprocess_exec`. Such a row reported `env_baseline: true` for a child that never existed; the row now calls the same `_command_argv()` `connect` does, so the two cannot disagree, and the guard test carries both spellings. **(2)** `BACKLOG.md` still shipped the pre-flip claim and therefore stated the OPPOSITE of the code — "opt-in, default-off … keeps working until the owner opts in" — in the one file `CLAUDE.md` tells a reader to query for what is delivered. That is exactly the misreading the slice's own documentation work exists to prevent. Corrected, and `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` now covers BACKLOG.md too, including a check that the "opt-in, default-off" wording is gone. Two wording corrections went with them: the `env_baseline` field describes the live FLAG, i.e. the posture for the NEXT spawn, not the environment the running child holds (`_merged_env()` runs once at connect, the row is read per request); and the migration note steered the reader at auth failures only, when the flip also withholds `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `HTTPS_PROXY`/`NO_PROXY` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` — plumbing whose absence produces an ImportError, a hang or a connect timeout, nothing resembling an auth error. **#1179 (cda4e19d, adversarial-review finding 4) widened the DISCLOSURE, not the guarantee, and touched two of the five cited files.** `agents/core/mcp/client.py`: the module docstring now names a SECOND route by which a hostile child recovers the withheld keys — not only `/proc/<ppid>/environ` but the **filesystem**, which the baseline narrows not at all: `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` in the child reaches the very file `plugin_manager.build` read those keys from (`client.py:17-36`). New `_CWD_SECRET_FILES = (".env", ".env.local")` and `cwd_secret_files(cwd)` (`client.py:215-242`; `None` → `Path.cwd()`, the inherited default; unreadable and missing both count as absent) report which of them the child can open, and `_merged_env()` calls it right after the withheld-count INFO line — only when something WAS withheld (`:555`) and such a file is readable — emitting one WARNING per connect, "withholding is undercut — .env readable in the server's working directory", carrying **filenames only, never a variable name** (`client.py:565-571`), because a variable name enumerates which providers the box holds while `.env` tells the owner nothing new. Deliberately not a refusal: refusing to spawn over a `.env` breaks every dev checkout and re-pointing `cwd` breaks every server that resolves a relative path, so the module's posture stays *withhold and say so*. `tests/test_mcp_transports.py` gains `test_cwd_secret_files_reports_what_the_child_can_open` (`:830`; a directory named `.env.local` is not a file) and `test_the_withheld_count_is_not_announced_alone_when_a_dotenv_is_reachable` (`:854`; WARNING level, `OPENAI_API_KEY` absent from the line, silent when no file is reachable). Everything else above is as assessed: the default-on flag (`client.py:90`, `:190`), `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST`/`_SECRET_LIKE` (`:161-176`), `stdio_env_extra_allowed` (`:197-208`), the count-only INFO line (`:556-559`) are untouched, and `worldview_write.py` and `tests/test_mcp_admin.py` are byte-identical to the prior stamp. **The later fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1) touched two cited files without touching this slice:** `client.py` gained `tool_patterns_over_bounds` (`client.py:138-154`) and a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (`:407-418`), and `admin_mcp_add` now also refuses a `tools_allow`/`tools_deny` over the 64-pattern / 128-char bounds (`routers/mcp.py:216-222`); neither reads the environment, the baseline flags or `env_baseline`, so the env code above only moved (+19 lines up to `MCPServer.__init__`'s filter block, +31 after it). The docstring pin `test_env_baseline_is_documented_as_defence_in_depth_not_a_boundary` (`test_mcp_transports.py:554`) survived the rewrite because both strings it asserts remain (`/proc/<ppid>/environ` at `client.py:21`, "defence in depth, not a security boundary" at `:30`). 41/41 cited tests green (33 + 8), re-run at the bounds-change head. MCP transport audit collateral review (2026-10-09): the route adds only fixed-field authentication telemetry at the existing RPC gate. This row's admin/listing, validation or transport-auth behavior and remaining limitations are unchanged; its previously current mcp.py pin and explicit coordinates were reviewed. MCP token audit collateral review (2026-10-10): the six-line insertion follows successful inbound token signing and only submits fixed-field telemetry. Existing admin configuration, stdio environment, outbound filters/trust and absence of ACP session-scoped servers or outbound approval/audit are unchanged; cited coordinates precede the insertion. Independent source review and all five cited/relevant MCP suites (67 tests) preserve this verdict and its gaps.
reviews.remaining: **The documented per-server `env` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.** `MCPServerConfig` has no `env` field (`routers/mcp.py:145-157`, no `model_config`), `POST /api/admin/mcp` drops the key (pydantic's default `extra="ignore"`), and neither `to_config` (`client.py:798-812`) nor `load_from_config` (`:814-849`) writes or reads one — the module docstring says as much at `client.py:41-45`. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the **host-wide** `JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV` (`:92-98`, "Host-wide, not per-server"), which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as `docs/OWNER_TASKS.md` §P28.3 with both options. **Related and also owner-level:** `XAUTHORITY` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` are both on `STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST` (`client.py:169`), and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped (`_SECRET_LIKE` at `:174-176` matches the `AUTH` in `XAUTHORITY`) while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. **And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:** this is **defence in depth, not a security boundary**, and since #1179 the module states that ceiling by TWO routes rather than one (`client.py:17-36`). The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of `/proc/<ppid>/environ`; and the baseline narrows the **filesystem** not at all — `cwd` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so `open(".env")` hands back exactly the keys that were withheld, which `cwd_secret_files()` now says out loud at connect (WARNING, filenames only, `client.py:565-571`) rather than leaving the owner to infer a protection from the withheld count alone. What the baseline buys is that a *careless* or *curious* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's `JARVIS_*` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise; closing the filesystem route as well as the `/proc` one needs real process isolation (separate UID, namespace or container — `client.py:33-36`), which is not shipped. **Unaddressed from the row:** there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary (the docstring itself calls the screener "still-unshipped", `client.py:34`), and `POST /api/admin/mcp` still stores `req.command` verbatim after checking only transport, trust tier, tool-filter shape and bounds, and duplicate name (`routers/mcp.py:188-241`, `:184`); the only shape check is `_command_argv()`'s shell-metacharacter/NUL refusal at connect (`client.py:519-529`), which is not a screener. #1179 changed none of this — it explicitly chose disclosure over refusal. This slice hardens what the child *receives*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to *be*.

reviews.summary: archive_safe is the only module in Nerva that reads an archive. Backup verify and restore unpack through extract_tar_path (agents/core/archive_safe.py:573; agents/core/backup.py:598, agents/core/backup.py:667). Marketplace install_from_zip unpacks through extract_zip_bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:637; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:816). The old backup._safe_extract and the marketplace _safe_targets+extractall pass are gone. An AST scan (tests/test_archive_safe.py:702, with probes at tests/test_archive_safe.py:688) fails when any other product module imports tarfile or zipfile outside a write-only allowlist, opens an archive for reading or calls an extract-family method. normalize_member (agents/core/archive_safe.py:122) folds backslash to '/' first. It then refuses empty, NUL, POSIX-absolute, Windows-absolute, UNC and drive-lettered names, and any '..' or empty part. Only regular files and directories are written. Symlink, hardlink, device, fifo and sparse tar members raise (agents/core/archive_safe.py:504), and so do symlink, device, fifo, socket and encrypted zip entries (agents/core/archive_safe.py:596). _Planner (agents/core/archive_safe.py:182) validates every member before the first write: name, type, in-archive conflicts and duplicates, member count and declared bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:257). It also checks the destination's existing content (agents/core/archive_safe.py:286): a link on the way to a member is refused, and so is a directory where a file goes (tests/test_archive_safe.py:365, tests/test_backup.py:471). The pre-scan reads the stream to its end (agents/core/archive_safe.py:522), so a bad gzip CRC, trailing data or a corrupt header part-way through is a refusal, not a shortened tree (tests/test_archive_safe.py:482, tests/test_archive_safe.py:517). Bytes are counted again while streaming (agents/core/archive_safe.py:389). The byte budget is clamped to free space plus the blocks of the single-link files the archive replaces (agents/core/archive_safe.py:314), so an in-place --force restore fits (tests/test_backup.py:443). PAX and GNU long-name header payloads are capped before tarfile reads them, 1 MiB each and 256 MiB in total (agents/core/archive_safe.py:461, agents/core/archive_safe.py:483; tests/test_backup.py:515). A link or hardlinked name at a member's path is unlinked and the file is created O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, never written through (agents/core/archive_safe.py:373; tests/test_archive_safe.py:323, tests/test_archive_safe.py:349). Backups take their caps from JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_MEMBERS and JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES (agents/core/backup.py:86); skill packages use SKILL_PACKAGE_LIMITS (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:42). On the producing side, create_backup writes both the encrypted and the plaintext branch through atomic_write, a sibling temp file that is fsynced and then os.replace'd (agents/core/archive_safe.py:654; agents/core/backup.py:415, agents/core/backup.py:420). Archives are GNU-format tar (agents/core/backup.py:474). The export walk skips symlinks (agents/core/archive_safe.py:715; agents/core/backup.py:401). publish_skill uses it on the staged copy it signs (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:392); the copy itself is built from the bytes of one source snapshot, which refuses a linked folder, a link or non-regular member and a file that changed while read (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:375), which has its own test (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:219). Every other name, hardlinked ones included, is archived as its own regular member (agents/core/backup.py:434, agents/core/backup.py:458; tests/test_backup.py:388). verify and restore compare the manifest's file_count with what the archive held (agents/core/backup.py:625; tests/test_backup.py:430). install_from_zip stages inside skills_dir, runs the signature gate there, and only then renames the tree into place (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:854, agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:885). A non-zip upload is a 400 refusal (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:194). Staging left by a killed install is swept once it is an hour old (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:773; tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:203). Restore stays an operator CLI action. It prints 'partial restore' when a failure came after the first write (agents/core/backup.py:716) and 'nothing restored' only for a pre-scan refusal (agents/core/backup.py:722). tests/test_backup.py:606 pins that no product module, script or subprocess caller reaches it. The pre-scan also refuses a component longer than the destination's NAME_MAX or a path past PATH_MAX, which the existing-path walk cannot see under a new directory (agents/core/archive_safe.py:251; tests/test_archive_safe.py:726), and a write the destination refuses mid-restore (permissions, a full disk) is a named ArchiveRejected marked partial, never a traceback (agents/core/archive_safe.py:445; tests/test_archive_safe.py:738). A restore leaves the archive's manifest in the target; create_backup never archives a top-level backup_manifest.json from the data root (agents/core/backup.py:482), so a backup of a restored root carries one manifest and verifies, restores and serves the forget purge's verified pre-snapshot (tests/test_backup.py:636, tests/test_backup.py:675). A backup of a restored root made before this change carries that name twice; verify and restore accept exactly that one repeat, last wins as tarfile resolved it, and count the dropped copy against the manifest's file_count (agents/core/backup.py:599, agents/core/backup.py:642; tests/test_backup.py:651). The repeat is bounded: the dropped copy still counts against the member and byte caps, and a third copy or any other duplicate is refused (agents/core/archive_safe.py:220, agents/core/archive_safe.py:223; tests/test_archive_safe.py:768, tests/test_archive_safe.py:775, tests/test_archive_safe.py:790). Known limit: backups made on main from a data root holding a symlink or hardlink fail verify and restore by design.

Startup validates all configured CA bundle paths and certifi, loads them through SSLContext, requires actual certificates, and supplies named repair instructions. Model egress uses an explicit trust context; invalid CA paths never imply verify=False. Per-target insecure overrides are explicit, loudly logged and ignored in hardened mode. Functional adaptation retained from the existing implementation: custom bundles may contain a valid short EC or pinned self-signed certificate; the 1024-byte minimum is reserved for the multi-root certifi bundle. Actual SSL parsing and certificate presence validate custom trust material instead of rejecting a valid anchor by byte length. All 45 TLS tests plus 22 plugin-egress tests pass, including real generated certificates and a loopback HTTPS server that fails without and succeeds with the owner CA. No external-provider connection or host trust-store change was performed.

**The write half, as a generic mechanism rather than a special case.** `agents/core/tool_rpc.py` gains a registrar-owned *call classifier*: a gated tool may register a pure function over one call's args returning bounded labels. `handle()` stamps them onto the durable approval card's payload and appends the notice to the card title; `execute()` re-derives them from the args about to run and refuses with `approval_class_mismatch` unless the approved card carried the same `class` — so a card approved as a scratch note cannot be redeemed against a write to SOUL.md. `_classify` fails closed (a raising, non-Mapping, over-long or non-alphanumeric result refuses the call rather than letting it through unlabelled) and strips the reserved `tool`/`args`/`target` keys so labels cannot rewrite the card's identity. `agents/core/file_tools.py` registers `FileTools.classify_mutation` for `file_write` and `file_delete`, matches on the BASENAME in any directory inside the roots (an instruction file is wherever the harness that reads it looks — `_load_soul` alone searches three), carries a `steers_future_runs` flag into the kernel Action payload, and adds a secondary floor in `_mutate`. A sandboxed script cannot label its own write nor strip the label off one: the classifier is registrar-owned and `handle()` returns `approval_required` before the handler is ever reached. **The review found one major and it is fixed here.** The roster omitted `HEARTBEAT.md` and `HEARTBEAT.local.md` — the files in this repo that *literally* schedule future runs: `core/heartbeat.py` scans every agent directory for them, prefers the gitignored `.local` overlay exactly as `SOUL.local.md` does, and turns what it finds into cron-scheduled agent runs. Both names are in the class now, and the roster is pinned against `heartbeat.py`'s own source rather than restated, so a loader that learns a new name fails the test instead of silently escaping the class. The exact-set pin beside it was tightened, not loosened. **Widened by #1177 (the #1161–#1174 adversarial review) — same mechanism, larger class, re-assessed here.** The roster is now `INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES` (`soul.md`, `agents.md`, `claude.md`, `gemini.md`, `.cursorrules`, `heartbeat.md`) and every `.md` name's gitignored `.local` overlay is *derived* by `_local_overlay` into `INSTRUCTION_FILE_NAMES` (eleven names) instead of being spelled out by hand — which is what brought `CLAUDE.local.md` / `AGENTS.local.md` / `GEMINI.local.md` into the class; the first cut listed only the SOUL and HEARTBEAT overlays, so a `CLAUDE.local.md` write — same harness, same authority, and it wins over the committed file — asked with the title of a scratch note. `looks_instruction_name` now also matches by extension through `INSTRUCTION_FILE_SUFFIXES = (".mdc",)`, so Cursor's freely-named `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` files, the format that superseded `.cursorrules`, are in the class as well. `classify_mutation`, the `steers_future_runs` flag, `_authorize`, the `_mutate` floor and `register_file_tools` are unchanged, and `tool_rpc.py` is byte-identical. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): since their pins, agents/core/tool_rpc.py (478ed8fc) and agents/core/file_tools.py (39d6f81b) changed, so the '#1177 left tool_rpc.py byte-identical and register_file_tools unchanged' sentence describes that change only — at HEAD tool_rpc.py also classifies on the registrar-bound gated_intake path (labels returned beside approval_required) and register_file_tools gains an optional mutation_intake that receives classify_mutation's labels, while _classify's reserved-key strip, execute()'s approval_class_mismatch refusal, the INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES/_local_overlay/.mdc roster and the steers_future_runs payload flag are intact (the rest of the file_tools diff is checkpoint-history capture/apply); the three pinned test files pass (109 tests).

Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 26 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:89), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, require('child_process').exec, a bare exec( in a file that imports child_process, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or `%`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, createCipher without an IV on any receiver, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote `<script>` without integrity=. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags `${{ github.event.* }}` inside a GitHub Actions `run:` step, on the run line or in its `|`/`>` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a `- run: |` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: `model.eval()` and `obj.eval()`, `def eval(`, `yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)`, `torch.load(..., weights_only=True)`, `regex.exec()`, an `===` comparison with innerHTML, `hashlib.md5(data)`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns `{rule, line, message}`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at `\n` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a `scan-incomplete` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. `.env`, `.env.*` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1277) adds `code_warnings` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), `code_warning_count` and a title notice (`code not fully scanned` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a `./` or `//` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's `approval_required` answer carries `code_warnings`/`code_warning_count` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:200), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1758): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:1024), the model reads `code_warnings` with a `code_guidance` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer `code_warnings` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:490) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1211), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a `scan-incomplete` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's `code_warnings` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:493), and generate_skill resets them first (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1051), so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and [learn:] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is `security.code_guidance` (read by enabled, agents/core/code_guidance.py:161: on by default, only an explicit off turns it off and an unreadable store keeps it on; the settings row is seeded on in settings_db DEFAULTS, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:110). An aliased child_process module (`cp.exec`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. The review round added crafted megabytes (one per quadratic rule) scanned in under a second and a card labelled promptly through the ToolRPC intake, the time and size cuts, the pause reply driven through the agent loop, skill_propose's warnings and the reset, the symlink and path spellings, a package padded with assets, the `- run: |` block, the wrapped and nested calls, the child_process and createCipher spellings, CR/form-feed/U+2028 lines, the dotfiles and the safe-mode switch. The review round's 44 mutants were all killed, ten after seven cases were added.

reviews.summary: Reviewed against live code; the inherited 2026-09-07 "partial" verdict stands, but for a different and much smaller reason than the audit recorded. The audit's "no Host-header validation anywhere" is stale: agents/core/host_policy.py is a 204-line module whose docstring (:4-22) names DNS rebinding explicitly, with normalize_host() at :54, parse_allowed_hosts() at :104 refusing a `*` entry at :119-120 and a leading-dot suffix wildcard at :121-122, host_accepted() at :157-181 matching loopback names, any IP literal, JARVIS_HOST, the ASGI scope's arrival address and JARVIS_ALLOWED_HOSTS, and assert_parseable_allowed_hosts() at :184 refusing boot on an unparseable list. It is wired at agents/web.py:20 (import) and agents/web.py:853-873 (`_host_guard`, returning {"error": "host not allowed", "code": 400}), registered so it runs before the rate limiter and inside the security-header and golden-signal layers (agents/web.py:827-830). Dumping app.user_middleware on the HEQ lot-1 head gives _golden_signals, _security_headers, _host_guard, _rate_limit, _no_store_for_polling, then lot 1's pure-ASGI _ForwardedProtoMiddleware, which only sets the request scheme and runs inside the guard. The boot guard is genuinely reached on the real serve path: agents/core/boot_guards.py:354, inside enforce_boot_posture, which the lifespan calls at agents/web.py:478-479 after the .env files load (agents/web.py:472-473, H273), so a list that lives only in .env is checked too; assert_front_door runs the same check over a caller's own mapping (agents/core/boot_guards.py:320). Refusal logging is rate-shaped (agents/web.py:836-838, agents/web.py:869) and logs only a coarse peer trust class (agents/web.py:841-850), never the attacker-chosen header value. Driven live on the lot-1 head with a loopback TestClient: `Host: evil.test` gets 400 on /status, /dashboard and /api/agents, where the real host gets 200 on /status and /api/agents. The row's other two asks hold, and lot 1 (H691) tightened the proxy half. Trusted-proxy entries are validated as bounded CIDRs at agents/core/proxy_trust.py:107 and :165 (note :308 only WARNS on a wide entry, it does not refuse). uvicorn's own forwarding-header allowlist (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, --forwarded-allow-ips) now refuses boot from the boot pass, which runs after the .env files load, when an entry is a wildcard, a /0, not an address, or a peer outside JARVIS_TRUSTED_PROXIES and loopback (agents/core/proxy_trust.py:570). serve.py switches uvicorn's proxy-header layer off, X-Forwarded-Proto is believed only from a listed peer, and the rate limiter's localhost exemption now follows the localhost gate's origin (agents/web.py:812), so an unlisted same-box proxy is throttled. CORS is validated with reported rejections at agents/core/cors_policy.py, and no CORS middleware is installed at all by default. The WebSocket clause was excluded by the row itself on the premise that Nerva had no WebSocket routes; that premise no longer holds, but the upgrades that now exist run the Host check themselves: agents/web.py:831-832 records that @app.middleware("http") does not cover WebSocket scopes and that Kanban's event upgrade calls host_accepted() and the admin guard explicitly in its router (agents/core/routers/kanban.py `_upgrade_request`; the Hermes runtime `/ws` upgrade in agents/core/routers/hermes_runtime.py does the same), and agents/web.py:708 is still the only ASGI app. 104/104 tests pass across the five relevant suites on the lot-1 head. What keeps this off "equivalent" is the residual the code names about itself at agents/web.py:833-835: _PROBE_PATHS is exempt from the guard (agents/web.py:857-858), so `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz. Re-confirmed live on the lot-1 head: a rebound page therefore still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts — cross-origin, because rebinding makes the browser treat them as same-origin. That is low severity and a deliberate operability trade, not an oversight, but it is a real deviation from Hermes' clause as written (which has no carve-out) and it is shippable work, so the row is partial rather than equivalent. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): the agents/web.py diff since 92c3eeb3 shifted every cited line (re-pointed by content: _host_guard, the registration comment, the lifespan boot-guard and .env calls, refusal logging, the rate-limit exemption, _PROBE_PATHS and the residual comment) and replaced the 'no WebSocket routes today' comment, because Kanban and the Hermes runtime now have upgrade routes that call host_accepted() themselves — the WebSocket sentence is corrected accordingly; serve.py only swaps os.environ reads for env_str and keeps proxy_headers=False; the probe-path residual is unchanged and the five pinned suites pass (104 tests).
reviews.remaining: The Host guard exempts _PROBE_PATHS (agents/web.py:800, applied at agents/web.py:857-858), so /healthz, /readyz and /metrics answer a rebound name: live-verified, `Host: evil.test` returns 200 on /healthz and /metrics and reaches the route on /readyz, while every real API route returns 400. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. The code names this residual itself at agents/web.py:833-835 ("a rebound page can therefore still read the golden-signal counters"). Close it by narrowing the exemption rather than removing it — the operability reason for it is sound. Suggested shape: keep /healthz and /readyz exempt but strip /readyz's detail to a bare ready/not-ready when the Host is not accepted, and require an accepted Host for /metrics unless the request is unambiguously non-browser (no Origin and no Sec-Fetch-Site, or an explicit JARVIS_METRICS_ALLOW_ANY_HOST opt-in for a monitor that scrapes by an unlisted name). Needs a test alongside test_healthz_from_any_host_is_exempt asserting that a refused Host cannot read the counter body. Separately, the row's "no WebSocket variant is needed" premise is now stale: the Kanban events and Hermes runtime upgrades refuse an unaccepted Host before accepting the socket by closing it with the generic policy code 1008, not with Hermes' machine-parseable rejection reasons and close code 4403, and no pinned test drives a rebound Host against either upgrade.

reviews.summary:
A spoken reply sounds like speech rather than read-out markdown, as Hermes requires, at every text-to-speech entry point. agents/core/voice/speech_text.py is the one normaliser (for_speech, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:161). It drops the file-mutation verifier footer (_VERIFIER_FOOTER, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:42), <think>/<thinking>/<reasoning> blocks (an unclosed one to the end, and everything before a closing tag that never opened), fenced code (``` or ~~~, an unclosed fence to the end) and HTML tags. [text](url) reads as its text, ![alt](url) as its alt, and a bare or <autolinked> URL as "link". Headings, list items, task boxes, block quotes and table rows lose their markers and end with a full stop (_line, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:133); table cells read with commas; separator rows and rules are dropped. Bold, italic, strikethrough and inline-code markers go and their words stay (_inline, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:122), with word guards so 2*3*4 and my_var_name survive. Symbols are said in the reply's language (_symbols, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:113, WORDS, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:88): & as and/și, % as percent/la sută, -> => as to/spre, degrees as degrees/grade; the language comes from the request, else a ro-RO voice, else the engine default (speech_lang, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:104). Emoji go: pictographs, flags, keycaps, skin tones, ZWJ sequences, variation selectors and tag flags (_EMOJI, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:70). Fish [emotion] tags are kept intact. Newlines are flattened to one spoken line. Text with no letter or digit left is "" (_SAYABLE, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:85), and the result is a fixed point (checked over every shared case).

Verifier footer (the clause the 2026-10-10 repair closed). Only the pinned producer's exact shape is removed from speech, and only from speech: the whole warning sentence with the warning sign (with or without U+FE0F), a positive count of at most twenty digits, and a contiguous block of at least one two-space-indented bullet with text, on its own lines, LF or CRLF. Preceding and following prose is kept. Near misses stay spoken exactly as ordinary prose: a header with no bullet, an empty bullet, a count of 0, a count of twenty-one digits, no warning sign, a lone leading space, and ordinary talk about verification. The visible chat text is untouched. One limit is stated plainly: Nerva has no producer of this advisory (it appears nowhere else under agents/); the format is the donor turn finalizer's, so the strip matters for resumed foreign sessions and for model-echoed text, and this row claims nothing about a Nerva-side file-mutation verifier.

Wiring. TTSEngine.speak normalises before any backend, Fish included, and synthesises nothing when nothing is left (speak, agents/core/voice/tts.py:216, normalised at agents/core/voice/tts.py:232; speech_for, agents/core/voice/tts.py:211). speak_stream normalises the whole reply before splitting sentences (agents/core/voice/tts.py:315), so a code, reasoning or footer block spanning sentences is dropped whole, and each sentence is then normalised again without change. Through TTSEngine.speak this covers the wake-word VoicePipeline, VoiceChannel.send and chat voice notes: speakable() is for_speech plus its cap (agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:69). POST /tts answers 204 with X-Nerva-Speech: nothing_to_say instead of synthesising (agents/core/routers/voice.py:76), and /tts/stream frames carry the spoken sentences. The HUD twin is speechText (frontend/src/speech-text.ts:110), pinned by the same shared cases as the hub. SpeechStreamFilter (frontend/src/speech-text.ts:155) drops a fenced block, a reasoning block or a footer whose markers arrive split across token deltas, holding back only a bounded tail that could still become one, and flushes cleanly. frontend/src/voice.ts uses it on the live sentence stream (frontend/src/voice.ts:297) and normalises each sentence (frontend/src/voice.ts:318); a 204 is silence, never an empty clip or the fallback voice (frontend/src/voice.ts:330). Mobile sends the reply to /tts, so the hub normalises it; ttsFetchBase64 (mobile/src/api/client.ts:2517) reads 204 as '' and speak() finishes at once (mobile/src/api/client.ts:2538, mobile/src/audio/tts.ts).

Verification at this head. tests/test_h526_speech_text.py runs every shared case (57) plus the fixed-point property: 135 Python tests pass with the TTS emotion suite. frontend/src/test/speech-text.test.ts and voice-speech-text.test.tsx pass 82 tests, including a live push-to-talk turn with a fence split across deltas, a footer split at many boundaries with CRLF, the plain warning sign, and a zero or over-long count spoken exactly as the whole-reply normaliser speaks it. mobile/src/api/__tests__/tts.test.ts passes 2 under jest. Full frontend suite 236 files, 2,198 tests, tsc clean. A first run with an incomplete virtualenv showed 27 failures that were missing bs4/numpy (26 reproduce identically on unmodified main); with the locked dependencies they pass. Mutation pass on the footer logic written in this repair: Python 12 mutants, 11 killed; TypeScript 10 mutants, 8 killed. The first pass left real survivors (a zero count, the twenty-digit cap, the required warning sign, and in the stream filter the plain warning sign and the same count rules); four shared cases and two stream tests now kill them. The three remaining survivors are equivalent (footer replaced with an empty string rather than a space, because the match is bounded by newlines or the string ends; a digit-after-count guard the final startsWith check already implies; >= for === on a probe that is fed one character at a time). The earlier normaliser had its own pass (126 mutants, 124 caught, two redundant code removed). Not claimed: physical audio output or a live TTS provider. reviews.summary: Conducta de transcriere validează, pregătește și livrează: acceptă octeți direct (`BytesIO`, fără fișier temporar, deci vorbirea nu ajunge pe disc), îi mărginește, trece rezultatul prin filtrul de halucinații și întoarce santinele oneste în loc de text inventat. Are acum doi consumatori — ruta HTTP a browserului și canalul Telegram — peste un singur motor local partajat, nu unul per apelant. Named speech progress adds explicit selected STT command identities through the common registry, pinned across async selection and executor handoff. Native mode choice, input handling and sentinel cleanup remain covered by inbound voice and STT regressions; broader provider coverage remains open.
reviews.remaining: Un singur backend. Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, `local_command`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC `TranscriptionProvider`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și `POST /api/audio/transcribe`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin `plugin.egress` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. Cache-ul motorului stă tot în `routers/voice.py`, care e casa greșită pentru el; canalul îl importă în loc să-l dubleze, iar mutarea lui e o schimbare separată. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat.

reviews.summary: Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură *inbound*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. `hallucination.py` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (`CANNED`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (`AMBIGUOUS`) cad doar când durata *decodată* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în `STTEngine.transcribe` și întoarce `[silence]` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în `frontend/src/voice.ts`: `recordUtterance` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după `SILENCE_MS`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un `rg -i 'vad'` peste `frontend/src/` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. `voice-vad.test.tsx` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul. Named speech compatibility review: the Whisper hallucination filter and decoded-duration handling remain on the native transcribe path; named commands preserve the existing exact-sentinel behavior. Hallucination and speech selection regressions pass.

reviews.summary:
A turn can read a document directly through file_read instead of relying on pre-indexed memory. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). Local 2026-10-09 parser-backed file_read admission refuses an observed on-disk PDF/DOCX size above 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB) as document_too_large before parser discovery or extraction. Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds. The same 2026-10-09 change (#1247) added scanned-PDF coverage detection: local_docs.extract_pdf_pages feeds one per-page traversal to pdf_coverage_warning, and file_read adds a coverage_warning beside the unchanged extracted text when more than 20% of pages or at least ten pages yield no text, with exact page/gap totals and the first 16 one-based empty page ranges, each with a bounded excerpt of the text before it (tests/test_file_pdf_coverage.py, tests/test_file_pdf_coverage_rpc.py).

reviews.summary: Nerva has no ACP editor-agent surface. No handler for session/new, load, resume or fork exists anywhere under agents/, and the editor-surface row H542 is itself still missing, so nothing can accept an mcpServers array from an editor. The only outbound MCP registry is the process-wide MCPManager (agents/core/mcp/client.py:728-730), which holds a single servers dict. It is filled by the admin-guarded POST /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:188-189) and the persisted global config. There is no per-session server scope, no per-session mcp-<name> toolset, no bounded discovery join and no late refresh of the tool registry. tests/test_mcp_client.py and tests/test_mcp_admin.py exercise only the global registry. MCP transport audit collateral review (2026-10-09): the route adds only fixed-field authentication telemetry at the existing RPC gate. This row's admin/listing, validation or transport-auth behavior and remaining limitations are unchanged; its previously current mcp.py pin and explicit coordinates were reviewed. MCP token audit collateral review (2026-10-10): the six-line insertion follows successful inbound token signing and only submits fixed-field telemetry. Existing admin configuration, stdio environment, outbound filters/trust and absence of ACP session-scoped servers or outbound approval/audit are unchanged; cited coordinates precede the insertion. Independent source review and all five cited/relevant MCP suites (67 tests) preserve this verdict and its gaps.
reviews.remaining: Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (4) A scheduled late refresh that re-reads the session's tool list after slow discovery finishes. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's.

reviews.summary: Filtrele allow/deny pe nume și glob (`tools_allow`/`tools_deny`, potrivite cu `fnmatchcase` pe numele original al uneltei) restrâng atât listarea, cât și apelarea uneltelor MCP; deny prevalează (`tool_visible`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:603-610). `_list_tools` nu oferă o unealtă ascunsă (:596-601), iar `MCPServer.call_tool` răspunde `tool_filtered` înainte să plece vreun frame (:616-617), deci scoaterea unei unelte din filtru o revocă imediat, și la apel, nu doar la înregistrare. Un filtru malformat îngustează, nu lărgește: un allow care nu e listă devine `[]` (`_clean_tool_patterns`, :124-135). Limitele (64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere, :120-121) sunt fail-closed. Ruta de add (`admin_mcp_add`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:214-223) refuză cu 400 `{"error": "invalid_tool_filter", "field": ...}` un `tools_allow` sau `tools_deny` peste limite, în loc să-l taie (`tool_patterns_over_bounds`, client.py:138-154), la fel ca pe o valoare care nu e listă sau pe o intrare goală. Un deny care nu poate fi păstrat (peste 64 de pattern-uri, un pattern peste 128 de caractere, sau care nu e listă) venit dintr-un config editat manual prin `load_from_config` îngustează serverul la nimic (`tools_allow = []`) și loghează un avertisment (:407-418), pentru că un deny tăiat ar face din nou vizibilă unealta pe care o numea. Filtrele fac round-trip prin `to_config`/`load_from_config` (:808-809, :852-853). H557 is PARTIAL, not missing and not equivalent. The 2026-09-07 verdict is stale on one half and still correct on the other; the overnight triage's "already equivalent" is wrong. Re-read 2026-09-22 after #1179 (cda4e19d): that PR touched agents/core/mcp/client.py only in the stdio env-baseline disclosure — the scope paragraph of the module docstring (client.py:17-36), `from pathlib import Path` (:58), the `_CWD_SECRET_FILES` comment block + constant + `cwd_secret_files()` (:211-242) and the "withholding is undercut" warning block in `MCPServer._merged_env` (:560-571) — none of which this row relies on; `MCPTool`, `_list_tools`, `MCPManager.get_tools`/`_resolve`/`find_tool`/`call_tool` are byte-identical to the pre-#1179 file, and the six other evidence files are unchanged. Only line numbers moved (they had already drifted 94 lines at #1174 and were 151 off after #1179). Re-read again 2026-09-23 after the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1): it added `tool_patterns_over_bounds` after `_clean_tool_patterns` (client.py:138-154), a deny-bounds block in `MCPServer.__init__` (:407-418), a bounds refusal in `admin_mcp_add` (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:216-222) and bounds tests at the end of tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:112-159); none of it touches a schema, a tool name or the resolver, so client.py pointers moved another +19 (the `MCPTool` block) or +31 (from `MCPServer.__init__` on) and routers/mcp.py pointers past the filter check moved +4. Every pointer below is at HEAD. One fact did change between the 2026-09-07 stamping and HEAD, by #1152 (0ef4002f, 2026-09-15) rather than #1179: a fifth provider serialization path now exists (see NOT SHIPPED).

SHIPPED (the row's rationale half). The name-collision correctness bug is fixed and tested: agents/core/mcp/client.py:748-777 `MCPManager._resolve` accepts a bare tool name only when exactly one server offers it and otherwise returns `{"error": "ambiguous_tool", "servers": [...]}` (:772-776); `server/tool` or an explicit `server=` pins the server (:756-767); `find_tool` (client.py:779) and `call_tool` (client.py:788) both route through it; `MCPTool.qualified_name` (client.py:367-370) is the `server/tool` form. tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-74 proves first-wins is gone (3 tests, passing; file 6/6 at HEAD). This is a genuine different-spelling equivalent of Hermes' disambiguation property, so `missing` under-reports the row.

NOT SHIPPED (the row's headline half). There is no `_normalize_mcp_input_schema` equivalent. agents/core/mcp/client.py:584-601 `_list_tools` still stores `t.get("inputSchema", {})` verbatim (client.py:592) into `MCPTool.input_schema` (client.py:357) with zero repair — the 2026-09-07 evidence sentence is still literally true. Nerva repairs at the dialect boundary instead, and on only ONE of five provider serialization paths: agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:401-470 `gemini_schema` covers Hermes' `required`-pruning (:456-460) and missing-`type` coercion (:453), and :473-483 `gemini_function_declarations` avoids the empty-OBJECT 400 (:479-481); its output feeds only gemini.py's `generate_tool_turn` payload (`functionDeclarations`). The other four paths pass `input_schema` through byte-for-byte: Anthropic (tool_dialects.py:147-151 `anthropic_tools`, :149, via anthropic.py's `cache_marked_tools(anthropic_tools(tools))`), OpenAI chat-completions (tool_protocol.py:19-27 `ToolSpec.as_openai`, :25 — shared by base.py's `LMStudioBackend` and `OllamaBackend`, openrouter.py's `OpenRouterBackend` and deepinfra.py), OpenAI Responses (responses.py:73-82, :78) and xAI Responses (xai.py — `XAIBackend._payload` overrides `ResponsesBackend._payload` at responses.py:60, so the responses.py builder never runs for xAI; this path landed in #1152 on 2026-09-15, after the original verdict counted four). Two of Hermes' five repairs are absent on every path: re-run at HEAD, `gemini_schema({"anyOf":[{"type":"string"},{"type":"null"}],"default":null})` → `{"default": null, "anyOf": [{"type":"string"}, {}]}` (the Pydantic null branch is not collapsed; on the Gemini path it degenerates to an empty schema, and the Anthropic/OpenAI/xAI paths ship the raw nullable union untouched — reproduced through `anthropic_tools` and `as_openai` on a ToolSpec carrying that property), and `{"definitions":{"Node":…},"properties":{"node":{"$ref":"#/definitions/Node"}}}` → `{"type":"object","properties":{"node":{}}}` (draft-07 `definitions`/`$ref` are not promoted to `$defs`, the referenced shape is silently deleted). No name sanitization exists anywhere: the only `mcp__` in agents/ is an example name in a tool_result_store.py docstring, and `qualified_name`'s `/` is not a legal provider function-name character.

ON REACHABILITY. The triage is right that this is currently unreachable from a model: `MCPManager.get_tools()` (client.py:742-746) has zero callers in the whole repo, `MCPTool.input_schema` is read nowhere outside its constructor (`grep -rn "MCPTool" agents/` hits only client.py; `grep -rn "\.input_schema" agents/` outside agents/core/llm/ hits only client.py:357 and the hub's own MCP-server side in route_tools.py), the only `MCPManager` instances are `orch.mcp` (built in `Orchestrator.__init__`, reached from web.py's `_save_mcp_config`/`_load_mcp_config` and routers/mcp.py for config and HUD only) and the one `WorldviewWriter` builds, and agents/core/routers/mcp.py:119-126 and :284 expose only name/description/read_only to the HUD, never the schema. Unreachability is a reason the remaining work is small and belongs inside the bridge PR — it is not a reason to record the row as done. The model can read a document mid-turn through a tool call. file_read in agents/core/file_tools.py is off unless JARVIS_FILE_TOOLS is set and bounded to JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS (no `..`, no symlink escape, secret-looking names refused, bytes capped by max_bytes). It returns a .pdf (pypdf) or .docx (python-docx) as extracted text when the input is admitted and parseable, names a missing parser (`parser_missing`) or a parse failure (`extraction_failed`) instead of returning replacement characters, and returns the bytes with raw=true. Since H661 it pages: `offset` starts the read at a byte, a read that stops early returns `next_offset`, a page is trimmed to end on a whole UTF-8 character (unless max_bytes is smaller than one), and an offset that is not an int in 0..MAX_OFFSET is refused as `bad_offset` rather than read from 0. A document pages through its extracted text: `offset` counts bytes of the extracted UTF-8 text, and `text_size` is reported beside the file's `size` (tests/test_spill_paging.py pages a .pdf's extracted text, with the extractor stubbed, back to its last byte). Local 2026-10-09 parser-backed file_read admission refuses an observed on-disk PDF/DOCX size above 50,000,000 bytes (decimal 50 MB) as document_too_large before parser discovery or extraction. Equality is admitted; raw=true and ordinary byte pages retain their output bounds. Local 2026-10-09 PDF text-layer coverage uses one shared parser traversal per request and adds coverage_warning beside unchanged extracted content when more than 20% of pages or at least ten pages yield no text. It reports exact page/gap totals, the first 16 maximal one-based ranges, and preceding source excerpts capped to 160 Unicode code points, with explicit omitted-range and excerpt-truncation fields. Blank/whitespace/None page text counts; reader/page failures retain extraction_failed without partial coverage. Existing normal-loop and nested ToolRPC scanners also scan the quoted metadata; this does not declare every file result untrusted.

reviews.summary: The owner's own chat attaches @file:path, @file:path#L10-40 and @file:"a b.md" for the turn. agents/core/context_refs.py holds the rules. expand (agents/core/context_refs.py:209) finds a reference that starts a word or follows an opening bracket, quote or backtick, and not one inside a word or a path (x@file:, a/@file:, @@file:) (_REF_RE, agents/core/context_refs.py:49); a double-quoted path may hold spaces, #L7 is one line and #L2-L3 a range, and trailing punctuation or a closing quote is not part of it. The routes keep the owner's message as typed: commands, skills, LLM-backend control, the router and memory see only it. The "--- Attached Context ---" section is bound to the turn (bind_attached, agents/core/context_refs.py:251; agents/web.py:1317 on /chat, and inside the stream task at agents/web.py:1415) and appended after the message only in the model prompt (attached_block, agents/core/context_refs.py:266; Orchestrator._build_agent_turn_text, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3850), so the file text is never stored as the owner's words, replayed in a later turn's history or embedded. Hermes keeps the expanded message in the user turn; Nerva shows the attachment to the model for the attaching (tainted) turn only. Each file's text is in a fence longer than any backtick run in it, so no line of it can close the fence (_fence, agents/core/context_refs.py:194), under a header that names the file as typed and the lines actually attached, `(line 7)` or `(lines 2-3)`, as attached file content, not instructions; injection patterns and a forged Attached Context marker are flagged in that header (`flagged: …`, _flags, agents/core/context_refs.py:180), not withheld. Each path is resolved through the same FileScope as file_read (_attach_one, agents/core/context_refs.py:133), so outside the file roots, .. traversal, a symlink escape and a secret-looking path such as .env are refused. A missing file, a directory, a binary file (a NUL in its first 8 KB), a bad line range, a range past the end, an unreadable file, an over-long name, a denied stat and an unknown ~user each become a one-line warning in the same section instead of failing the message. With JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS unset, the file tools' default root <data home>/workspace is used; only an unusable JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS makes the section say nothing was attached. The limits are 8 distinct references per message, 64 KB per reference and 128 KB in all, counted in bytes. A cut reference says so, and a repeated one is attached once. A line range skips the lines before it a 64K-character chunk at a time, up to 64M characters into the file (MAX_SCAN_CHARS; past it, the warning "line N is too far into the file"), keeps at most the byte budget and never reads a line whole (_read_lines, agents/core/context_refs.py:105); invalid UTF-8 is read with replacement characters. The expansion runs on /chat and /chat/stream (agents/web.py:1306, agents/web.py:1534), off the event loop, so both the HUD and nerva chat get it; the one message that skips it is a raw checkpoint command (`/rollback` or `/checkpoints` as the whole message, checkpoint_command_name), which never becomes a model turn, so nothing is read, bound or tainted for it. It never runs for a channel message, as Hermes' gateway does not expand either. A turn that attached anything is tainted: handle_input and handle_input_stream call _taint_attached_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:378, :2372, :2593), which raises the turn's action origin to recall:untrusted. An action planned from attached content therefore escalates GRANT to QUEUE at the kernel, while an inbound turn keeps its more specific origin. complete (agents/core/context_refs.py:272) lists in-scope completions for what follows @file:, with directories ending in / and a path with a space quoted (a name no reference could name is left out). It shows dot files only when asked and never secret paths or links out of the roots, is bounded to 50 entries, and returns nothing for a prefix over 1,024 characters. GET /api/context-refs (agents/core/routers/commands.py:63, user-guarded, read-only) serves it and the reference types, and answers 503 file_roots_unusable when the roots cannot be used. The HUD composer (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:229, :284, frontend/src/context-refs.tsx) offers the reference types while `@` or `@fi` is typed (Tab takes `@file:`), then the in-scope paths; a list is shown only for the text it was fetched for. tests/test_h579_context_refs.py (70 cases) covers the bounds, parsing, whole files, line ranges (single, L-form, past the end), every refusal and warning, a symlink, punctuation, word starts, dedupe, the byte cut, the shared budget, the reference limit, an unreadable file, invalid UTF-8, the roots, an explicit scope and the marker; completion (prefixes, dot files, secrets, roots, a long prefix, a file or missing folder, the bound); both routes, the completion route, the turn taint on both paths, and an inbound turn. The review round added attached text never read as the owner's command (a slash command, a skill, a backend switch) and never stored or carried to a later turn, through the real routes; a file that cannot close its fence; injection and a forged marker flagged; a range in one huge line bounded in memory and a range of many short lines linear; a range too far into a file; quoted paths and their completion; references after brackets and quotes and not inside words; the distinct-reference limit; the header's path and lines; paths the system refuses to look at; and the roots. frontend/src/test/context-refs.test.tsx has 6 cases. The row's 53 mutants predate this code; the review round's 34: 28 caught at once, five after five cases were added, and one equivalent (a kept read stops at the budget either way, since readline(0) answers "").
