reviews.summary: Both intake halves of the accepted adaptation exist: the HUD composer and the terminal. useComposerImages (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx) takes image paste and drag-drop (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:113-114) plus a file chooser, and accepts at most eight PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images of up to 4 MiB each (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:4-5); the shared InputBar wires paste and drop in (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:247). Each draft is first reviewed against the server (prepare / selected-prepare with image digests, destination binding, data-policy and remote/training/cost acknowledgements), and App.submit sends an image draft to runVision (frontend/src/app.tsx:511, frontend/src/app.tsx:477). runVision picks one of three routes (frontend/src/vision-turn.ts:8): POST /api/vlm/composer/describe-prepared (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:499), POST /api/vlm/composer/chat-prepared for a selected main route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:584) or POST /api/vlm/composer/selected-chat for a selected Ollama route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1092); the router is registered at agents/web.py:1669. All three routes check data-URI signatures and bound raster decoding (validate_raster, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:61) and refuse a malformed body with its first reason instead of FastAPI's echoing 422 (_BoundedValidationRoute, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:28). describe-prepared and chat-prepared also refuse a non-local destination without the owner's acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:718) and call VLMBackend.generate_vision_checked (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:460); selected-chat is local Ollama only, refusing any remote acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:985-987) and streaming /api/chat itself (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1051); the H277 native adapters (OpenRouter, DeepInfra, Nous, Claude, Gemini, Responses, xAI), empty-reply recovery and reply normalization sit behind that guard. The terminal: `nerva chat --image PATH` (repeatable, up to eight) and `--clipboard-image` (agents/cli/nerva.py:445-448) turn the chat verb into a vision turn (dispatch at agents/cli/nerva.py:2748, _vision_turn at agents/cli/nerva.py:3119) that refuses --agent/--session/--reasoning and never posts to /chat. Files are typed by signature (_image_mime, agents/cli/nerva.py:2862; _read_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:2872); the clipboard is read by wl-paste, xclip, pngpaste/osascript or PowerShell (_clipboard_command, agents/cli/nerva.py:2947; _clipboard_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:3057) under a bounded, deadline-killed reader (_run_reader, agents/cli/nerva.py:2972), and an off-machine destination needs --remote-vision naming it (agents/cli/nerva.py:3208). Governance gap found on this re-read: the previous verdict rested on isolation (the vision answer a client-only transcript entry, ordinary turns posting only {message, agent} to /chat/stream). Since #1233/#1246 that holds only for describe-prepared and the terminal. The chat-prepared and selected-chat routes commit the image-derived question/answer pair into the durable conversation (orch.complete_selected_image_turn at agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:619-623 and agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1065), and later text turns in that session post to /chat/stream with the session_id (frontend/src/app.tsx:404-405) and read that history. That history is now governed (H586 fix, 2026-10-12, c9f67240, 0631eeb9, 9a485766, 44b53b51, 0bc59ec5 and 307b33eb): every later chat turn runs _guard_media_history (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2359-2377) at both turn entries (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2453 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2674), which reads the session history and, when any turn carries media, raises the turn's action origin through mark_turn_recall_tainted, so a side-effecting action derived from that history is queued for approval (ASK) instead of auto-granted, and an unreadable history marks the turn too; one-shot completions (process/process_detailed: the autonomy _llm executor, nightly reflection, the summarize route) run the same guard inside an action-origin binding scoped to the call (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2224-2226), so the mark never leaks to the caller; image turns are embedded with taint metadata (taint_source external:image, agents/core/memory/manager.py:342-345), so recalling the image reading in any later turn taints that turn through the existing RAG guard, and a session_search hit on a turn carrying media is flagged image_derived and taints the turn too (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:239-240 and agents/core/memory/session_search.py:244-248), and, since the model's call runs search_sessions in a worker thread whose own mark cannot reach the turn, the production mechanism is the registered tool handler declaring tainted on its result (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:281-283), which the agent tool loop reads as declared_taint and turns into the turn's mark; and a session holding a media turn is never promoted to durable memory, like a foreign import: _session_has_media (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2379-2384) stops the per-turn learning review (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3978 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:4064), the LivingMemory feed (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4093) /refine, which answers image_history_not_promotable (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4023-4024), and nightly reflection, whose KG/core-lesson consolidation skips a window holding a committed image turn (agents/core/autonomy/reflection.py:166-167); /undo, on the web (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1961-1963) and on channels (agents/core/channels/session_lifecycle.py:226-228), copies the kept turns with their media provenance, so an undo cannot launder the image reading into trusted history. tests/test_h586_image_history_taint.py pins the QUEUE verdict through the real kernel authorize (with a stubbed history and with a real MemoryManager after a committed image turn), the untouched text-only origin, the fail-safe mark, both entries' call order, a one-shot completion over image history running tainted without leaking the mark, the tainted embedding read back through rag_guard, and the refusals of review, LivingMemory and /refine, a web /undo keeping the provenance (guard, promotion gate and tainted re-embedding) and nightly reflection skipping the image window and a session_search hit on an image reading tainting the turn, directly and through ToolRPCServer.handle (13 cases, red before the change). Stated limits: the guard reads the held history, which keeps the newest 100 turns, so a media turn that has aged out of it no longer marks later turns (its embedding stays tainted), and with the opt-in memory.compression_summarizer the per-session summary cache can carry image-derived text past that window. Tests this session: 25 pinned backend files (tests/test_h277_image_turn_memory.py, tests/test_composer_vision.py, tests/test_nerva_chat_image.py, tests/test_h586b_image_review.py, tests/test_h586c_image_review.py, tests/test_h586_image_history_taint.py and the 19 pinned tests/test_h277_* files) 509 passed, 0 failed; frontend/src/test/composer-images.test.tsx and frontend/src/test/composer-vision-turn.test.tsx 50 passed; frontend/e2e/composer-images.spec.ts (Playwright) and mobile were not run. Known limits kept: the receipt's model stays null for a terminal image turn; no live-provider or native-mobile acceptance.

reviews.summary:
Nerva reads a project's convention files into the turn, as Hermes reads its context files and subdirectory hints. agents/core/project_context.py walks from the nearest git root (never above the file root) down to the working directory (llm.project_dir when it is a folder inside the roots, H218; else the first JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS root; since #1233 a bound kanban workspace's cwd instead, read inside that workspace's scope), and reads AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules and .cursor/rules/*.mdc in each directory in that order (CONVENTION_NAMES, agents/core/project_context.py:59; candidates, agents/core/project_context.py:168). A directory that the model's file_read, file_list or file_search touches is noted for the session (note_tool_path, agents/core/project_context.py:408, bounded to 8 directories and 256 sessions, agents/core/project_context.py:70-71); its chain is read on every later turn, and the tool's own result carries the files the turn had not seen yet, marked tainted so the loop fences it (attach, agents/core/project_context.py:427; _with_project_context, agents/core/file_tools.py:653, called by the three read tools at agents/core/file_tools.py:841, agents/core/file_tools.py:897 and agents/core/file_tools.py:1020). A script's file call (execute_code, no tool turn) brings none. A local terminal_run runs only after approval, by the worker from the queue: the queuing turn's session is recorded at intake (note_task, agents/core/project_context.py:439) — on ToolRPCServer.handle's generic gated path (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:638) and, since #1233 gave terminal_run its own trusted intake, in _terminal_intake (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1192, the call at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1257; registered with gated_intake and gated_review at agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1284-1285) — and when the approved command ran locally, note_terminal (agents/core/project_context.py:451; keyed by the task id, not by a turn) notes its cwd for that session, so its next turn reads the chain (_rpc_terminal_run, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1189). Normally the command runs outside any turn and its result goes to the task row, not to the model; with Smart review or a live owner-once/consent reply, the registrar's gated_review (review_terminal_task, agents/core/autonomy/terminal_review.py:22-24) awaits the worker's own run of that task and hands the queue-verified result back to the model in the same turn — the directory is noted either way. A project SOUL.md, HEARTBEAT.md or IDENTITY.md is never read, not even through a symlink (HUB_FILES, agents/core/project_context.py:63; _admit, agents/core/project_context.py:183). Every file is resolved through FileScope (outside the roots, symlink escape and secret paths refused), must be a regular file (a FIFO is never opened), and is bounded to 20 KB, with 40 KB and 12 files a turn and 8 rules a directory (agents/core/project_context.py:65-68), shared by parallel tool calls under the turn's lock; a cut says how much was shown, a file past the budget is named, and files past a count cap are counted (load_file, agents/core/project_context.py:220; collect, agents/core/project_context.py:239; render, agents/core/project_context.py:274). Each file's text and name are scanned with detect_injection_normalized, plus Unicode TAG characters (decoded and scanned) and the fence's markers (_detect, agents/core/project_context.py:122). A flagged file becomes a [BLOCKED ...] line naming the rules (injection_flag_names) with none of its text, and a flagged name is withheld; other names have non-printable characters escaped and undecodable bytes replaced. The caveated block, which holds the files in the untrusted-data fence, sits after the core-memory block in _build_agent_turn_text (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3866-3872); _begin_project_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:388-416) builds it off the event loop at turn start in both turn paths (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2470 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2699) and marks the turn recall-tainted when any file was given, so an action planned from it escalates GRANT to QUEUE. A noted directory's files are in every later turn of the session, so those turns are tainted too: web_search, web_extract and memory writes refuse until the setting is off or the hub restarts. A guest's turn is given none of them. It is off with llm.project_context_files (agents/core/project_context.py:74) and in safe mode (layer project_context, agents/core/safe_mode.py:77, named on the HUD banner; enabled, agents/core/project_context.py:312). tests/test_h594_project_context.py: 66 cases. reviews.summary: The pool mechanism is wired end to end. AuthProfilePool (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py) holds several keys per provider, read from *_API_KEYS with a *_API_KEY fallback (from_env, agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:86). hybrid_router builds Gemini and Anthropic pools (agents/core/llm/hybrid_router.py:328). ClaudeBackend and GeminiBackend fail over to the next key on a rotatable status (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:132, agents/core/llm/gemini.py:208). report_failure (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:159) applies an exponential cooldown from 30 s to 15 min. Pool health is exposed. status() (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:181) returns masked per-profile failures and health through the admin-guarded GET /api/llm/auth-profiles (agents/core/routers/models_llm.py:454). AuthProfilesPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2698) renders it, under the console route at frontend/src/console-routes.ts:119. tests/test_h12_20_auth_rotation.py (18 passed) and tests/test_route_guard_contracts.py::test_llm_auth_profiles_requires_admin (passed) cover the pool and the guard. reviews.remaining: The accepted branches are missing. _ROTATABLE_STATUS (agents/core/llm/auth_rotation.py:28) is {401, 403, 429}, so a 402 billing failure neither rotates nor gets the long (1 h) cooldown. No OAuth credential type exists, and a 401 has no refresh-then-rotate step. Keys resolve only from os.environ in from_env; VaultResolver (agents/core/secrets_vault.py:16) is never consulted for LLM keys. The owner also cannot see partial degradation. AuthProfilesPanel shows one healthy/failing tag per provider, derived from the pool-level healthy count, so a pool with some keys cooling still reads green. The API returns per-profile cooldown, but the panel does not render it.

reviews.summary:
The shared identity band exists. agents/_identity/IDENTITY.md is one behaviour contract: the reply-sizing rule (match length to the weight of the ask), earned depth, the named prohibitions (no filler, no restating the request, no re-summarizing, no narrating visible tool calls), the anti-sycophancy line ('agree because it is right, not because the owner said it') and 'say when you do not know'. Its reply rules govern the agent's own replies to the owner: text drafted in someone else's voice (an email, a post, a message written as the owner) keeps that voice, greetings and sign-offs included, and a persona's warmth or curiosity lives inside the answer (review-H670 m-5); its honesty rules hold for everything an agent writes, drafted text included (review-H670b m-1). Its leading maintainer note (stripped before the model sees it, _strip_maintainer_note, agents/core/agent.py:453) says never to add 'be targeted and efficient in your exploration', and why. The repo-root SOUL.md mirrors the text, so agents working on the repo read the contract the product ships; a test keeps the two equal. identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolves it as soul_path_for does a persona: the data home's souls/IDENTITY.local.md, then a gitignored agents/_identity/IDENTITY.local.md, then the shipped file. read_identity (agents/core/agent.py:481) runs it through the same H387 helpers as a SOUL (the injection scan on the uncapped body, then the cap), announces a flagged or truncated contract (its blocked and quarantined stubs name the contract, not a persona), caps it at its own 4,000 characters (IDENTITY_MAX_CHARS, never above the persona's cap, so the two bands stay within the persona cap plus 4,000), and reads it once per settled file signature for the whole process. An override that cannot be read (not UTF-8, a directory, no permission) is reported at ERROR and the shipped contract used instead, cached against the shipped file's signature so an edit of it is seen; a contract that cannot be located or read at all leaves the agent without it; none of these stops an agent from being built. Agent.system_prompt (agents/core/agent.py:572) is the contract, then the agent's persona (either may be empty; an agent without a SOUL still gets the contract). Every place a system prompt is built uses it: Agent.process (agents/core/agent.py:1090) and the synthesis path in agent.py, and the orchestrator's two sites (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2824, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4685) through _system_prompt_of (agents/core/orchestrator.py:512). At a compaction boundary refresh_soul (agents/core/agent.py:741) re-reads the contract as it re-reads the persona (_refresh_identity, agents/core/agent.py:610): a few stats when unchanged; when the file that resolves is absent, vanishes before the read or cannot be read, the contract in force is kept, reported at the boundary as failed-open and warned once per episode (an override absent for an instant resolves to the shipped file for that boundary, as a persona's does); and a moved contract reported as rebuilt, so an edit reaches running agents without a restart. The contract in force at start is committed to the prompt VC (SoulVersionStore) as _identity (_record_identity_version, agents/core/orchestrator.py:494), a no-op when unchanged or empty, so its history is recorded and diffable through /api/admin/prompts/_identity/... beside the personas; what is served is the file (a rollback in the VC does not change it), and an edit picked up at a boundary is recorded at the next start. The prompt-size report counts it as a shared component every call pays (identity_component, agents/core/prompt_size.py:136), and the packaged build ships it through its agents/*/*.md glob (overrides, *.local.md, never ship). IDENTITY.md and its .local overlay are in the H506 instruction-file class (INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES, agents/core/file_tools.py:260), so a file write to them asks as an instruction file; a test derives the class from every name the contract's and a persona's loaders can resolve. The data home's README lists souls/IDENTITY.local.md. Persona SOULs and Persona.prompt_block (agents/core/cognition/persona.py:142) stay the character layer on top. tests/test_identity_contract.py (18 cases) covers every rule's presence, the banned line's absence and the kept warning, the mirror, the scan verdict, every active agent's system prompt starting with the contract (and exactly contract then persona), an agent without a persona, the orchestrator's helper and all four sites, both overrides and their order, the scan and the cap on an override, an edit reaching a running agent at the boundary, the one-stat unchanged path, a failed re-read keeping the last-good contract, the version record (once, and a failing store never stopping a start) and one read shared across agents; tests/test_h670b_identity_review.py (21 cases) covers the first review: the instruction-file class, a contract absent or vanishing at a boundary, a non-UTF-8 or unreadable override, the contract's own cap, no empty version, the start-time record, the contract's scope, a mid-file comment, the prompt-size component, the ERROR on a flagged contract, the stubs' wording and CHT-117; tests/test_h670c_identity_review.py (14 cases) covers the second review: honesty unscoped, a shipped contract that stops being UTF-8, a vanish before the real read, the hub's start recording the contract, one warning per episode and a second one, a reader that raises, the fallback following a shipped edit, a directory override, a permission error at load and at a boundary, the fallback rules once when both bands are blocked, and the docs. 2026-10-09 execution-admission continuation: the production coordinator now supplies a separate authorization-only live profile resolver to the agent loop. Each ToolRPC call rechecks its selected registered name/gated metadata after the independent job scope and registration checks, synchronously before preflight, gated approval intake or handler admission. Revocation during the tool_started await is therefore refused locally even without a context fold. Resolver failure or a missing selected tool denies with the existing tool_not_allowed reason. The check uses inherited principal/origin/job context and does not rebuild provider schemas, change the stable gate/taint views or write H661 turn-offer notes. A production-wiring regression checks the unchanged offer sentinel inside the handler child; a gated regression records no preflight, intake, pending approval or handler effects. This check itself makes no provider call. In-flight tools, direct/script RPC and already-approved execution are outside this admission increment. Standalone runtimes with only the offer hook retain legacy behavior unless execution_profile is wired; the sole production constructor wires both. Existing stale source pins are deliberately not globally restamped. The historical fold/persona assessment below keeps its original scope. Both refreshes from Hermes's row exist (`agents/core/session_refresh.py`, the parked mechanism commit 89b53e85 cherry-picked unchanged; its module docstring has since gained a note on where each half is wired) and are wired at Nerva's two compaction boundaries, each failing in its own direction. **Nerva is turn-based, so most of the row was already true between turns and is pinned as such**: `Orchestrator._prompt_context` reads the skills catalog per turn, the plugin block is rendered per turn, and `AgentToolRuntime._run_loop` resolves ToolRPC → capability registry → tool profile at the top of every run (`test_between_turns_the_offer_was_already_live`). Two things were not live. **(1) The system prompt.** `Agent._load_soul` ran once in `__init__` and `orchestrator.py` sent `agent.soul["content"]` for the life of the process, so a persona edited or quarantined mid-session needed a restart. `Agent._read_soul` is the one builder (same file resolution, same H387 scan, same cap) behind both `_load_soul` and `Agent.refresh_soul`, and `_refresh_souls_at_boundary` (orchestrator.py, a module function so the bare-stub tests of that path keep working) calls it for every agent from `_history_for_prompt`'s `publish()` — after the clock CAS, never before it, and pinned as such: a refused `commit_clock` migrates nothing, an accepted one is followed by the refresh in that order. In front of the builder sits an `os.stat` probe (`_soul_signature`: resolved path, inode, size, mtime, ctime and the body cap), because once a session is over budget the conversation-level commit happens on **every** turn — `ContextCompressor.compact()` recomputes from the raw turns each call — and the walk is process-wide: an unchanged persona costs one stat, and only a file whose kernel signature moved reaches the builder (measured over the 18 shipped SOULs, 76 KB: 59.0 ms → 0.55 ms per boundary, 18 → 0 reads and scans). A file written within the last two seconds has no trusted signature (git's racy rule: a same-size edit in the same timestamp tick would be invisible to a stat) and is read and compared by bytes until it ages. Past the probe the keep path is byte equality of the builder's whole output — body *and* front-matter, so a tier or trait edit with the same body is adopted and the HUD's `soul["meta"]` follows — never a dirty flag; a builder that throws keeps the last-good bytes (fails OPEN); a file absent for the instant of an editor's save-by-rename keeps them with a plain warning, and an agent that had no persona and still has none is unchanged, not failed. A scan verdict is not a failure — a persona that is now mostly injection is dropped exactly as a restart would drop it — and it is announced exactly as a restart announces it: `_announce_soul_verdict` is the one place both moments log, so a quarantine at the boundary is the H387 ERROR line, not an INFO line. **(2) The tool set inside one turn.** A loop of up to `llm.tool_loop_max_iterations` model turns kept the list it resolved at the top. `_run_loop` treats a committed fold (`_compact_context` grew `compacted`) as the boundary and re-resolves through `_resolve_offer` (the same three steps, minus the turn-start side effects) via `session_refresh.refresh_tools`, which fails CLOSED: a resolver that raises withdraws every tool, an empty resolution is a revocation, and either ends the loop with `_TOOLS_WITHDRAWN_REPLY` after a `tool_loop_withdrawn` event rather than asking a provider a turn on a stale or empty list. The offer and the executor move together (`_specs_for` rebuilds the specs, the gate map the executor checks `offered` against, and the untrusted set) — pinned by a tool withdrawn through the *profile* while still registered in ToolRPC, the one shape that can tell the executor's `tool_not_allowed` from the RPC's own (keeping the stale gate map runs the handler, and that test goes red). Between folds the registry is not consulted at all, so the set stays stable between two folds; Nerva's fold happens inside one user turn, so Hermes's "mid-turn tool sets stay stable" reads here as *between folds*. reviews.summary:
A compaction summary no longer holds the owner's turn past a short bound, and a silent summarizer is cut. Hermes keeps two clocks: how long the summary may make the user wait, and how long the summarizer may go quiet. Nerva awaited the strict-local summarizer inline with neither. Its only limit was the httpx read timeout (120 s for Ollama), a total-duration wait on a non-streaming call, and nothing told the owner. (1) Bounded hold. ContextCompressor takes a gate (agents/core/context_compressor.py:327, used at :605). The orchestrator builds it per turn (_summary_gate, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4383, passed at :4514) around SummaryHold (agents/core/compaction_hold.py:149). SummaryHold.wait (:159) waits at most memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds for the LLM summary (settings_db.py:312; default 10 s, 0 = never wait, clamped 0..120 by hold_seconds, compaction_hold.py:64). One summary per session is written at a time: a turn that finds one still in flight neither waits on it again nor starts a second. Past the hold the turn goes on without the summary, and compress marks the result summary_deferred (context_compressor.py:630). compact (:422) then sends the turns verbatim, their old images dropped, when they still fit the window under the owner's memory.compression_max_tokens; otherwise it sends the deterministic digest. The summary keeps being written. reviews.summary: Re-read on main at 55d625f4. Telegram has the partial-then-edit mechanism: TelegramDraft (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:124) sends the first token as a message, then edits it in place through _edit_message (telegram.py:598) at most once per STREAM_EDIT_INTERVAL (telegram.py:60, 1.2 s) and only when the visible text changed; finish() (telegram.py:197) settles the final text in the streamed message, sends overflow as new messages, retries markup Telegram rejects as plain text and falls back to a fresh send when the final edit fails. The adapter declares supports_edit=True (telegram.py:240) and exposes begin_stream (telegram.py:614). The real caller is Orchestrator._begin_channel_draft (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2049), invoked for every non-observed channel turn (orchestrator.py:1652): it opens a draft only when the adapter has begin_stream, its descriptor says supports_edit, the owner setting channels.streaming_replies is on (orchestrator.py:2057) and the delivery router would send to this source; the turn then runs through handle_input_stream with an on_token callback that forwards each token to draft.push (orchestrator.py:1997) and draft.finish (orchestrator.py:1677) replaces the whole-reply send. The conservative default is declarative rather than a stub: ChannelDescriptor.supports_edit defaults to False (agents/core/channels/descriptor.py:36), so an adapter that declares nothing gets the whole reply. Slack and Discord (and now ntfy) are deliberately excluded from streaming (orchestrator.py:2054) because their replies go through the governed channel.reply approval queue (_queue_workspace_reply, orchestrator.py:1686-1687); test_edit_support_alone_cannot_publish_unapproved_tokens pins that an editable transport alone cannot publish tokens before that approval. Tests: 82 passed, 1 skipped (tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py needs slack_sdk, absent on this box) across tests/test_telegram_streaming.py, tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py and tests/test_slack_socket_mode.py. #1188's change to telegram.py (the process's shared SenderPairing handed in at construction, deeplink pairing refused when none is wired) does not touch the draft, edit or send paths. Selected-main image collateral review (2026-10-02, 2fce39ca): The source diff adds optional bounded image provenance and a new reviewed conversation-image path. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. Drift re-read (2026-10-12): diffed channels/slack.py, discord.py and telegram.py since 92c3eeb3 and orchestrator.py since 2fce39ca; the draft, edit-interval, finish and supports_edit paths are unchanged apart from Telegram forum-topic routing on sends, the channel turn now runs through the session lifecycle service with the draft passed in, ntfy joins Slack and Discord on the approval-queued no-streaming path, Telegram gained a TTL delete only for ephemeral system notices, citations were moved to their HEAD lines by content, none of the three remaining gaps closed, and the pinned tests give 82 passed, 1 skipped (slack_sdk absent).  Re-read 2026-10-12 (c9f67240, 0631eeb9, 9a485766, 44b53b51): the only changes to agents/core/orchestrator.py and agents/core/memory/manager.py are the H586 image-history fixes (a turn whose history holds a committed image turn runs tainted; image turns are embedded tainted; a session holding one is not promoted by the learning review, LivingMemory or /refine; one-shot process() completions run the same guard; /undo keeps image provenance on the copied turns); every citation of this row into those files was re-resolved by content and no claim was touched.
reviews.remaining: (1) No edit or delete in the base contract: ChannelAdapter (agents/core/channels/base.py:14) still declares only abstract start/stop/send plus receive, and no adapter implements a delete operation for a sent reply (the only deleteMessage in agents/ is Telegram's TTL cleanup of ephemeral system notices at telegram.py:504, not a channel-contract method), so a sealed streamed preview cannot be removed and there is no base method that fails loudly for a channel that cannot edit; the fallback to a whole reply is silent. (2) Slack and Discord do not stream: both descriptors declare supports_edit=True (agents/core/channels/slack.py:105, agents/core/channels/discord.py:51) but neither adapter implements begin_stream or an edit call (Slack's send posts via chat_postMessage only, slack.py:609), and _begin_channel_draft refuses both (and ntfy) because a streamed draft would publish tokens before the channel.reply approval; streaming there needs an approval contract that covers output not yet generated. (3) No acknowledgement at ingest: Telegram sends a typing chat action only while reading an inbound attachment (telegram.py:1632) and a record_voice action before a spoken reply, so an ordinary text message gets no receipt signal until the first streamed token or the whole reply; Slack and Discord send none (the Slack Socket Mode envelope ack is a transport ack to Slack, not a signal the sender sees).

2026-10-09 local first slice: both public orchestrator entrypoints measure their complete invocation through cleanup with a monotonic clock. A request-owned collector claims once, rejects nested or late publication and closes before transport projection; there is no per-session last-result cache. ChatResponse and every SSE end carry one optional outcome, currently null or {latency_ms: nonnegative integer}. Only a normal return publishes a measurement; commands and handled refusals can have a duration, while exceptions, cancellation, busy and uninstrumented paths have none. Duration does not imply successful model or tool execution. The declared display.status_bar_fields setting defaults to [latency], validates up to eight unique vocabulary entries and filters metrics server-side; an empty, invalid or unavailable selection hides the metric without breaking the answer. The existing Admin Settings editor exposes the preference. Both HUD cockpit and focus chat render one shared Turn duration strip from the current end and clear it on new work, stop, errors, session/agent changes and DEMO transitions; entering DEMO cancels an in-flight live turn. The field is not persisted in history. Mounted tests cover stale callbacks, malformed numbers and session resets; compiled browser regression covers 1280px and 390px, a no-data reply and reload. Focus composer shrink/wrap rules fix the measured 390px overflow. This is the common outcome transport requested by build-queue critic note 10; H220 context/cost and H396 exit/accounting must extend it. No token speed, model name, context percentage, cache ratio or compression counter is claimed. H18.33 now consumes the same server-selected explicit SSE end in native chat, accepting only nonnegative safe integers including zero. The accessible current-turn strip uses separate ephemeral state; new work, stop/error, history/session and connection changes clear it. Agent selection revokes the metric without cancelling a pending text reply, including A-to-B-to-A. Exact persistence projection and remount tests exclude duration from history.
